The 55 physical fields and 14 JSON/key-family rows retain separate primary CMF
records. `answered_original_as_array` is a typed `VARCHAR[]`, not JSON.
`source_metadata` and `judgment_payload_json` are physical JSON values; their
named keys, open copied maps and unknown nested quote values are separate
serializer-domain records rather than being inferred from broad runtime types.

### Article Payload And Bounded Hydration Reconciliation

| Fields / CMF rows | Actual selection or hydration role | Boundary that remains distinct |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Project/display/payload/snapshot/article identities (`CMF-1195`-`CMF-1199`) | Scope keyed payload reads and the candidate-to-payload join. Article also keys detail/export sets and breaks prompt-preview order. | A matching candidate/snapshot key does not freeze later payload mutation or current-table hydration. |
| `article_created_at` (`CMF-1200`) | Orders the one-row prompt-preview payload query and participates in strict rebuild checksum; detail may use it as fallback. | Prompt preview returns detail-row time, so payload selection order and displayed article time are different contracts. |
| `source_metadata` (`CMF-1201`, `CMF-1250`-`CMF-1252`) | Joined before list limit but never drives list membership/order; consumed after selection by list/detail and bounded export. It is `json_merge_patch(article, selected import)`. | Named Covidence/source paths, producer-defined keys, current joins, transfer source serialization and rendered badges are not one frozen schema. |
| `abstract_text` (`CMF-1202`) | At-most-2,000-character summary used by keyed detail, one-row preview and bounded export hydration. | It is not candidate-selection data and does not freeze the later CSV artifact. |
| `full_text_preview` (`CMF-1203`) | At-most-2,000-character text used only as detail fallback when the current article full text is absent. Preview selects the field through `SELECT *` but uses separately read current full text. | Selected field presence is not current consumer proof; preview/detail full-text behavior is current-table hydration. |
| `payload_bytes` (`CMF-1204`) | Worker count/checksum input only. It sums source character lengths before preview truncation, including both full-text forms and both metadata values. | It is neither encoded persisted bytes nor a size ceiling, and no route consumes it. |
| `payload_updated_at` (`CMF-1205`) | Writer timestamp and startup mutation-probe field. | It is not a read lease, cleanup receipt or response freshness guarantee. |

Generic list SQL performs the payload join before its outer order/limit, but
only `source_metadata` is selected and none of its fields changes candidate
membership or order. LLM, Human and Both routes first select a bounded page,
then hydrate judgment detail in chunks capped at 100 article IDs and 10,000
rows; Unassessed does not hydrate judgments. These per-chunk caps do not prove
one request-wide payload budget when prompt count, parallel chunks and response
serialization are considered separately.

Detail uses one article-payload row, then recursively pages LLM and Human detail
at 512 rows until no full page remains. It separately reads current article
full text and other base state. Prompt preview reads one ordered payload row,
one detail row and one current full-text row. Export limits article and judgment
hydration by durable selected IDs times snapshot scopes/prompts, but it executes
at download time and still joins current article/source state. These are
separate selection, hydration and artifact contracts, not one snapshot freeze.

### Judgment Detail Fields And JSON Serializer Domain

Project/review/snapshot/list/payload-kind/article/prompt keys
(`CMF-1206`-`CMF-1212`) scope and deduplicate physical reads. `prompt_order`
(`CMF-1213`) orders detail/export hydration. Judgment/model IDs and scalar/array
answers (`CMF-1214`-`CMF-1217`) feed route and export transforms;
`placeholder_kind` (`CMF-1219`) suppresses unanswered LLM placeholders;
`detail_updated_at` (`CMF-1220`) is a response-date fallback and startup probe.
Their roles do not make their values equal to corresponding JSON keys.

| JSON family / CMF rows | Exact current serializer boundary | Current consumer boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LLM top envelope (`CMF-1253`) | `assessments`, `chunkingStrategy`, `confidenceOriginal`, `createdAt`, `explanation`, `id`, `isAnswered`, `model`, `payloadReference`, `placeholderKind`, `prompt`, `quotes`, `snapshotProjectId`, `snapshotProjectModelName`, `updatedAt`. | List uses a small subset plus relational columns; detail uses model/prompt/assessment and judgment fields; export extracts prompt/explanation/quotes or retains the JSON. |
| Assessment (`CMF-1254`) | Latest assessment only: comment, correctness, created/updated times, assessment ID and judgment ID. | Detail response consumes the array; list does not. |
| Model (`CMF-1255`-`CMF-1257`) | ID, name, provider, thinking, version and copied open `metadataJson`. | Detail uses named model display fields but explicitly returns `modelMetadataJson: null`; lists prefer relational model ID. Open metadata has no demonstrated payload consumer. |
| LLM reference (`CMF-1258`) | `{kind,judgmentId}` with placeholder versus judgment kind. | Serialized and exported only through generic JSON; no direct mounted response transform was found. |
| Prompt (`CMF-1259`) | Criteria disposition, ID, order, original text, heading and type shared by LLM/Human. | Detail hydrates prompts; project export extracts heading/text/type. List prompt identity comes from the relational column. |
| Quotes (`CMF-1260`, `CMF-1261`) | Normal strings plus transfer/source-admitted unknown nested values. | List/detail/export consume the value generically; no closed versioned value schema exists. |
| Human envelope/reference (`CMF-1262`, `CMF-1263`) | Answer, comment, created/updated times, ID, answered flag, prompt and `{humanJudgmentId,kind}`. | Human/Both list and detail use answer/comment/dates/prompt; no direct reference-object consumer was found. |

The LLM writer selects the latest active judgment only for the configured
model and four content flags; Human prompt mode and synthetic `summary` mode
use different source tables and prompt identities. The physical PK carries
`review_config_hash` but not those settings separately. JSON equality,
review-config hashing, active-judgment natural identity and transfer
serialization therefore remain distinct unresolved contracts.

### Title Search Fields, Tokenization And Consumers

Dirty projection normalizes titles with JavaScript `NFKD`, removes only the
combining-mark range `U+0300..U+036F`, lowercases, splits on non-ASCII
alphanumerics and deduplicates. Rebuild SQL instead uses DuckDB
`lower(strip_accents(...))` and the same ASCII split expression. Source tests
cover examples but do not prove full-domain equality. `title-token-v1` appears
only in manifest input digest, so table rows cannot independently disclose
their tokenizer version.

The four scope identities (`CMF-1221`-`CMF-1224`) predicate every active
search. `token` and `article_id` (`CMF-1225`-`CMF-1226`) drive prefix existence,
joins and standalone order/cursor. `title_prefix`, `activity_sort_at` and
`search_updated_at` (`CMF-1227`-`CMF-1229`) do not drive current embedded
route/count/bulk membership; the standalone service would return them through
`SELECT *`, but no mounted production caller invokes that service.

Mounted LLM/Human/Both/Unassessed list and count paths require an existence
match for every normalized input token. Posting helpers can apply one prefix,
and bulk workers generate one existence subquery per token. These active
embedded consumers are semantically different from the registered max-50
standalone service, which passes one whole trimmed/lowercase string. Registry
presence and an unused callable service are not product reachability proof.

### Queue Patch, Active Queue, Priority And Prompt-Pair Reconciliation

`mart.review_queue_patch_v4` and its index remain migration/test references.
The generic writer allowlist, startup registry and retention registry omit the
table. Current `projectReviewServingQueuePatches` reads source state, deletes
and inserts the active unassessed queue, writes queue manifest/watermark state
and returns `patchRowCount: 0`. Negative tests prove this checked-in bypass;
they do not authorize deletion or prove deployed absence.

The active queue stores two distinct prompt-pair families:

- LLM `unassessed` uses priority `0` when no judgment exists and `1` when an
  unanswered judgment exists; answered/deleted-or-out-of-scope combinations
  become tombstones and are omitted;
- Human `human-unreviewed` uses priority `0` before any Human update and `1`
  afterward; a nonblank answer or Covidence summary origin removes the row.

Project/review/snapshot/kind fields (`CMF-1240`-`CMF-1242`, `CMF-1244`) scope
all reads. `priority_bucket` and `activity_sort_at` (`CMF-1245`-`CMF-1246`)
order the direct queue contract, Human init, judgment-job article preview and
strict prompt-pair worker. `article_id` (`CMF-1247`) drives route/bulk
existence, distinct-article counts and joins. `prompt_id` (`CMF-1248`) drives
prompt-pair jobs and named summary counts. `queue_identity` (`CMF-1243`) is a
direct-reader tie-break and stored identity, but judgment-job keysets omit it;
`queue_updated_at` (`CMF-1249`) is writer/startup state only.

The Unassessed review route and bulk worker use queue existence by article and
ignore priority/prompt identity. Human init asks the direct queue contract for
one highest row but consumes the article ID. Judgment-job count uses distinct
articles, article preview groups prompt pairs and uses max priority/activity,
and the worker pages as many as 5,000 prompt pairs plus one lookahead with a
strict priority/activity/article/prompt cursor. Summary uses article/prompt/kind
for named counts. Queue rows, article counts, prompt-pair counts and consumed
priority semantics are therefore separate contracts.

### Publication, Recovery, Export, Transfer And Non-Production Closure

- Incremental payload processing writes article payload without acknowledgement
  and then writes judgment detail with the final acknowledgement. Those are
  separate writer transactions. A detail failure can follow a committed
  article-payload mutation; the separate `judgmentInputContent` runner advances
  state without mutating detail.
- Full rebuild handles article payload under `payload` and judgment detail
  under `judgmentInputContent`. Search and queue are separate components.
  Promotion does not make later mutable rows or current-table hydration
  immutable.
- Article-payload strict checksum omits metadata, previews and update time;
  search omits activity/update time; queue omits activity/update time; judgment
  detail omits prompt order, model ID and update time. Cheap counts cover fewer
  values. Successful chunk validation is not full field parity.
- Startup has duplicate checks and separately committed mutation/restore probes
  for the four active tables. Queue patch is omitted. A restored chosen row
  does not prove crash-safe startup or complete repair.
- Source schedules retention checks at 60 seconds and deletes bounded batches
  from one of 11 registered tables while protecting active/LKG/pinned
  snapshots. Mutable cursor state is not a cleaner lease, cycle receipt or
  ordinary-reader lease; queue patch has no registered cleanup.
- Project export reads article payload and judgment detail after durable ID
  selection; transfer serializes source articles/models/judgments/Human state
  and regenerates serving. Neither proves source/target mart equality, frozen
  download hydration, retained-copy integrity or cleanup safety.
- `db:duck:inspect-review-serving-project-state` is package-exposed with the
  primary DB path and creates a read-only snapshot, queries title-search state
  and deletes the snapshot in an acquire/release finalizer. It was not run.
  Invocation success would still not prove crash cleanup, deployed use or
  restore validation. Test seeding, benchmarks, migrations, tests, tasks and
  plans remain non-production references.

Browser and desktop share source route/service code, but no supported physical
browser/desktop capture or approved immutable fixture ran. All deployed row
counts, null/value/domain distributions, JSON sizes, fan-out, tokenizer
cardinality, priority distribution, optimizer plans/use, time, memory, disk,
write cost, cleanup, restore and platform measurements remain explicitly
pending for Phase 4. Missing measurements are unavailable, never zero.

### Posting Membership, Statistics And Consumer Reconciliation

The posting projector emits seven kinds: `importRoute`,
`publicationYear`, `duplicateFlag`, `conflictFlag`,
`llmStatus`, `humanStatus` and `promptAnswer`. It crosses each
eligible article with list-mode membership and serializes
kind/value/list-mode into the stored identity. Prompt-answer values also embed
review/Human mode, prompt ID and answer; that text grammar is not a SQL domain.

Dirty projection computes old/new contributions in memory, reads current
serving totals and writes posting serving plus stats. Full rebuild writes
active serving rows in ranges and refreshes stats later. Neither path writes
the physical patch or persistent contribution table. A valid posting row,
matching identity text, matching stats row and visible snapshot are therefore
four distinct contracts.

Active consumers are narrower than stored production:

| Posting family | Demonstrated current consumer | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `promptAnswer` | LLM/Human/Both list and count predicates plus durable bulk selection | Generated `prompt_filter_N` aliases use project/config/snapshot/list/article/kind/value equality. They do not consume stored posting identity or timestamp. |
| `duplicateFlag` and `conflictFlag` | Generic filtered review reads and bulk selection | Generated `filter_N` aliases intersect membership; strict selection/order remains driven by candidate/job SQL. |
| `importRoute`, `publicationYear`, `llmStatus` and `humanStatus` | Projector/statistics state; no direct current browser/desktop posting consumer proved | Candidate/status fields can provide related filters, but related semantics do not establish these posting rows as consumed. |
| Stats rows | Projector refresh/validation, startup/retention and package duplicate diagnostic | No route/read contract consumes cardinality or selectivity. Stored statistics and optimizer statistics are different contracts. |

`cardinality` counts posting rows by kind/value/list. `selectivity`
divides that count by active `mart.project_scope_article` membership where
curated or route scope is true. That denominator is not a route's later search,
filter intersection or candidate population. A nonnegative cardinality and
computed ratio do not prove semantic selectivity, estimator use or UI need.

### Counts, Facets, Filter Options And UI Boundary

`namedReviewFastCountDefinitions` contains seven count definitions:
`review.list.total`, `review.list.filteredTotal`,
`review.llm.assessedByPrompt`, `review.llm.unassessedByPrompt`,
`review.human.reviewedByPrompt`, `review.both.conflictByPrompt` and
`review.queue.unassessedReady`. It also contains six facet definitions:
`review.filter.duplicateFlag`, `review.filter.importRoute`,
`review.filter.publicationYear`, `review.filter.promptAnswer`,
`review.human.filter.promptAnswer` and
`review.human.filter.summaryAnswer`. Each has an explicit v1 definition
version. Named keys, versions, physical PKs and UI labels remain separate.

`review.list.filteredTotal` is stored unavailable with
`filter:dynamic` for the unsupported derived shape; filtered routes perform
their own count SQL. `review.queue.unassessedReady` is derived from
prompt-pair queue contributions while a UI label may present an article total.
Property names do not reconcile those grains.

The filter-option identity currently fixes empty active filters, sorted filter
and list keys, review versus Human mode, search identity and six summary
definition versions. Source rows cover duplicate/conflict/import/year,
LLM/Human status, prompt answers and Human summary answers. The writer emits
three finite JSON variants, sets `answer_id`, `numeric_min` and
`numeric_max` to null, and computes a distinct-article
`count_value`. The server instead derives options/ranges from payload,
prompt and facet values and does not use the stored count. Both shared
controls consume the response's derived `filters`; raw facets,
filter-option rows, diagnostics and search scope are not demonstrated current
client render inputs. A returned raw field is not a consumed UI contract.

### Contribution, Rebuild-Partial, Reduction And Finalization Boundary

The current contribution service produces in-memory old/new diffs. Direct
summary projection deletes/replaces count and facet serving without the
persistent contribution table. Chunked rebuilds instead write:

- one summary partial per request/chunk/snapshot/serving key; and
- one contribution partial per request/chunk/snapshot/article/component/
  version/contribution key.

Finalization discovers only chunk manifests in `completed` state, derives
an accumulator chunk ID prefixed
`__summary_rebuild_partial_accumulator__:`, and reduces source summary
partials in batches of 256. It deletes each reduced source summary-partial
batch, deduplicates contribution partials across completed chunks, updates
accumulator counts and publishes count/facet rows. The accumulator remains.
Contribution partials are deleted only before rewriting the same chunk; no
terminal completed/failed/abandoned/orphan cleanup path was found. Successful
publication therefore does not prove partial retirement.

Cheap chunk validation counts summary partial rows but omits contribution
partial rows. Strict summary validation checks final count/facet/option
serving, not every chunk-local partial and contribution value. Worker
finalization refreshes posting stats, reduces summaries, refreshes filter
options, refreshes/promotes candidate state and terminalizes the request in
separate steps. If derived-output or promotion fails after every chunk is
complete, the resulting finalization failure is not proven to meet the normal
readmission predicate. Chunk success, derived-output success, promotion,
cleanup and bounded replay remain distinct contracts.

### Publication, Recovery, Export, Transfer, Retention And Reference Closure

- The shared writer accepts active posting/stats/count/facet/options and both
  partial tables. It excludes posting patch and persistent contribution.
  Physical writes, component manifest/acknowledgement and later snapshot
  promotion remain distinct transactions or phases where the caller requests
  no acknowledgement.
- Startup indexed-table repair separately probes posting serving, stats, count,
  facet and option rows by mutating/restoring one timestamp. Patch, persistent
  contribution and partials are absent. A restored selected row and duplicate
  check do not prove crash-safe recovery or complete repair.
- Retention registers the same five active tables and protects active,
  last-known-good and pinned snapshots while rotating bounded deletes. It omits
  patch, persistent contribution, summary partial and contribution partial.
  Mutable cursor/schedule state is not an ordinary-reader lease, cleaner lease,
  durable cycle receipt or terminal partial cleanup.
- Durable bulk/export selection consumes posting membership for
  duplicate/conflict/prompt filters. Download-time export later hydrates
  article/detail/current source state; it does not read counts, facets,
  options or partials. A completed selection does not freeze later hydration.
- Transfer serializes source entities and emits target deltas/dirty tokens; it
  does not serialize these marts. Regeneration is not source/target
  row/index/statistic parity or completion acknowledgement.
- Database backup copies a read-only whole-database snapshot/WAL path. No
  family-specific manifest, concurrent-reader lease, retained-copy lifecycle
  or executable restore validation was run.
- The package-exposed project-state inspector groups duplicate posting-stats
  keys on a read-only snapshot. Static access tests prove the checked-in
  command surface, not authorization, deployment, invocation history,
  remediation or recovery completion.
- Exact non-production references include migrations, schema/projector/
  retention tests, tasks/plans and historical OOM notes. They preserve
  discovery and negative source evidence; they do not provide deletion
  authority, deployed absence or a retention horizon.

Shared browser and desktop code does not prove physical request execution,
query caching, rendered consumers or hash/navigation parity. No supported
browser/desktop controller or approved immutable fixture was used.

### Phase 4 Measurements Explicitly Pending

Every missing runtime observation remains unavailable, never zero. Phase 4
must retain one approved immutable non-live deployed snapshot or fully
specified disposable fixture and collect, at minimum:

- the applied migration ledger through 0114, exact clean/upgraded table and
  index existence, constraints and repair/regeneration outcome;
- per-table rows, per-project/snapshot/list/kind/value fan-out, null/domain/
  range/coherence distributions, posting cardinality/selectivity denominators,
  count/facet/option cardinality, JSON/text bytes and partial/accumulator ages;
- completed/failed/abandoned/orphan partial counts, contribution duplicates,
  retained accumulator rows, terminal cleanup results and reference scans;
- table/index physical bytes, index/write amplification and
  `EXPLAIN`/`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` for every mapped ordered, membership,
  named-count, facet, option, reducer and diagnostic query;
- fixed-profile timing, RSS, DuckDB memory/spill/temp/disk metrics, concurrent
  reader/cleaner behavior, crash/replay/finalization/retention receipts and
  startup mutation restoration;
- supported browser/desktop request/render evidence, frozen export selection
  and download hydration, transfer target readiness/round trip, backup
  integrity and executable restore validation.

Fixture authorization does not approve benchmark-critical configuration.
Project/route membership, seed, scale, model, provider, thinking/options,
prompts, content flags, memory, process topology, clock, versions and complete
collectors must be supplied explicitly before physical execution.

### Recovery, Retention, Export, Transfer And Non-Production Closure

- Comparison generation cleanup deletes older or all rows in all five marts,
  but there is no persisted reader pin or atomic multi-table promotion receipt.
  CSV/conflict exports read serving/current state and do not freeze later
  hydration or prove transfer parity.
- Archived-project cleanup has bounded batches and tombstone progress, but its
  mart registry omits several no-longer-referenced legacy tables and its
  comparison-child temp detach occurs before the restoring transaction.
  Successful catch restoration does not cover process death.
- Transfer session recovery has TTLs, stale-state transitions, artifact cleanup
  and terminal-row pruning; history has no source-observed retention. Those
  controls do not make temp operation/commit tables recoverable or prove
  source-to-target serving equality.
- Startup repair includes fixed mutation probes and a generated full-row probe
  for keyed registry targets. It does not cover every legacy/comparison/temp
  row, and its normal restore/drop path is not a crash-safe receipt.
- Database-wide backup and source-regenerated export/transfer do not establish
  object-family restore validation. Package exposure and maintenance-access
  guards prove checked-in command shape, not authorization, invocation history
  or deployed recovery completion.
- Tests, fixtures, migration SQL and the historical plan remain
  `test`, `historical-migration` or `historical-plan` evidence. Exact source
  absence remains blocked and never becomes deletion authority.

### Declaration And Non-Production Reconciliation

- The US-014 `${databasePath}.tmp` default-spill wording was stale. Current
  `loadEnv` declares sibling `duckdb-temp`; `clearLocalDatabases` additionally
  removes `.tmp` for compatibility. Cleanup recognition is not active-path
  declaration or physical-existence proof.
- Schema v1 remains accepted import shape; schema v2 is the current export
  shape. Neither a supported registry nor fixture archive proves production
  package history, deployed compatibility use or retention.
- Runtime-assets path validation proves relative/root syntax. It does not
  prove a path came from a persisted article/data-source reference, that the
  final filesystem target is not a symlink, or that a concurrent cleaner
  cannot remove it during response streaming.
- Tests and fixtures create temporary database, owner, asset and transfer
  roots. Historical plans, migration text, route inventories and package
  scripts are declaration or non-production evidence, never deployed
  existence, absence, authorization, invocation or deletion authority.
- No cleanup registry covers all files above. Successful-call `finally`,
  transaction catch, expiry cutoff, stale PID, force-delete or manual backup
  invocation must not be reported as a durable cleanup receipt, bounded
  schedule, reader lease, reference scan or validated recovery.

### Measurement Formula Contract

The following formulas are fixed as the required output shape, not reported as
executed SQL. A future approved collector must record the exact query text,
DuckDB version, transaction/snapshot identity and raw result for every value:

| Metric | Required formula/boundary | Current value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table rows | `N(T) = COUNT(*)` at the named post-seed, post-source-write and post-publication checkpoints; filtered active/history counts retain their exact predicate | `unavailable` for every table |
| Row fan-out | `fanout(child,parent) = N(child) / NULLIF(N(parent),0)` plus both numerator and denominator; no ratio is emitted alone | `unavailable` |
| Null ratio | `nullRatio(T,c) = COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c IS NULL) / NULLIF(N(T),0)` for every nullable physical column/material field; empty-table result remains explicitly undefined | `unavailable` |
| Approximate distinct | `approxDistinct(T,c) = approx_count_distinct(c)` with exact non-null row count and DuckDB version; identity/key columns additionally receive exact distinct where bounded | `unavailable` |
| Duplicate values/bytes | `duplicateRows(T,K) = SUM(groupCount - 1)` for groups on the declared key/value/hash; repeated logical bytes require an approved canonical encoding and record top bounded duplicate groups separately | `unavailable`; equality/encoding approval is part of `BLK-0350`/`BLK-0352` |
| Width drivers | Per scalar/JSON/list field record non-null count and logical encoded total, mean, p50, p95, p99 and max bytes; row/family totals remain logical payload, not physical storage | `unavailable` |
| Lifecycle range | Per applicable timestamp/status record `MIN`, `MAX`, null count, age buckets at one frozen clock, and active/archived/resolved/quarantined/delete-pending predicates separately | `unavailable`; clock and predicate authority are `BLK-0351` |
| Orphan evidence | For each declared or intentionally absent relationship, record the exact anti-join numerator, parent denominator and nullable-key treatment; a successful FK declaration is not a deployed orphan count | `unavailable` |
| Rows written | Per stage and statement record inserted, updated, deleted and full-row-rewritten rows separately; `after N(T) - before N(T)` is not accepted as write count | `unavailable` |
| RSS | Record process topology, start/end/peak RSS, growth and sample cadence for source/config writes and required projection/scope publication; temp/spill bytes remain a separate series | `unavailable` |

### Measurement Formula Contract

These formulas define the required future report; they are not executed SQL.
Every value must retain exact query text, DuckDB version, fixture/report and
transaction/snapshot identities, checkpoint, frozen clock and raw result.

| Metric | Required formula/boundary | Current value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table and state counts | `N(T)=COUNT(*)`; every filtered active/pending/deleted/reconciled/quarantined/tombstone count records its exact predicate and denominator | `unavailable` for all 10 tables |
| Null and distinct evidence | For every nullable field, `nullCount(T,c)=COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c IS NULL)` and `nullRatio=nullCount/NULLIF(N(T),0)`; record exact distinct for bounded identities/enums and `approx_count_distinct` plus non-null count/version for open or large values | `unavailable` |
| Repeated values and logical bytes | For declared natural keys, text, list and canonicalized JSON/hash values, record bounded top groups, `duplicateRows=sum(groupCount-1)` and `duplicateLogicalBytes=sum((groupCount-1)*encodedBytes(value))`; equality and encoding remain explicit | `unavailable` |
| Payload widths | Per scalar/list/JSON field record non-null count and canonical logical encoded total, mean, p50, p95, p99 and max; open JSON additionally records root/key/version frequencies without narrowing its contract | `unavailable` |
| Lifecycle ranges | Per applicable timestamp/status record `MIN`, `MAX`, null count and owner-approved age buckets at one frozen clock; creation, update, delete, reconcile, quarantine, lease and tombstone ranges remain separate | `unavailable` |
| Judgment generation | By the seven-dimension judgment natural key, record active/deleted rows, exact `delete_generation` distribution/min/max, generation-zero occupancy after delete, keys with multiple generations and keys with more than one active row. `deleted_at` and generation are not interchangeable. | `unavailable` |
| Sequence versus generation | Delta/outbox `source_high_water_mark`, retry counts and hot-fact upsert/tombstone timestamps are measured as sequences/state, never relabeled judgment generations. Human/review/token/hot tables declare no generation column; current/superseded truth still requires an owner predicate. | Schema distinction recorded; physical distributions `unavailable` |
| Typed extraction savings | For each approved hot key `k`, record raw JSON rows/bytes retained, one hot typed value's bytes, downstream typed copies, consumers/rows avoiding raw extraction and consumers still parsing raw. `parseOpsAvoided(k)=sum(rows for typed consumers)` and `typedLogicalDelta(k)=hot bytes + downstream typed-copy bytes - approved replaced raw-slice-copy bytes`; source raw bytes common to both sides cancel rather than being called saved. | `unavailable`; consumer set, encoding and counterfactual are `BLK-0354`/`BLK-0356` |
| Relationship/orphan evidence | Record exact anti-join numerator, parent denominator and nullable-key treatment for every declared or intentionally absent article/project/prompt/judgment/job/source relationship; a checked-in FK is not a deployed orphan count | `unavailable` |
| Rows written | At every seed, LLM/Human/token, delta append/reconcile/outbox recovery/hot upsert and publication boundary, record inserted, updated, deleted and full-row-rewritten rows separately; `after N(T)-before N(T)` is not a write count | `unavailable` |
| RSS and temporary usage | Record process topology, start/end/peak RSS, growth and sample cadence per stage; temp/spill bytes and directory growth are separate from RSS and persistent bytes | `unavailable` |

fixture/report, transaction/snapshot/file identities, checkpoint, frozen clock
and raw result.

File/container counts remain separate from rows and overlapping path-shape rows are deduplicated by canonical path. | `unavailable` for all 36 table/catalog objects and four file/container rows |

Persisted milliseconds such as oldest-unexported/unacked age remain recorded values, not recomputed timestamps. | `unavailable` |

Open JSON records root/key/version frequencies without narrowing the domain; duplicated relational/payload identity bytes remain explicit. | `unavailable` |

For every persisted lease record active, expired, missing-owner, missing-expiry, owner/token duplicates and heartbeat age at the frozen clock. ### Source Retention Classification

This source classification is not a physical age/row measurement. It keeps a
checked-in policy, a source-proven lifecycle gap and missing deployed
retention evidence separate.

| Classification | Exact checked-in families | What source proves | What remains unavailable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Explicit bounded policy with an active caller | Provider admission leases use a 60-second default TTL and delete expired/released rows; provider telemetry has a three-day cutoff called by the hourly judgment cleanup; local job outbox/queue evidence is pruned in 1,000-row batches after visibility ACK and drained files are checkpointed/deleted | Current source contains predicates and scheduled call composition. | Deployed invocation, lag, backlog, crash receipt, concurrent-reader safety, actual oldest row/file and restore validation. Missing these is missing retention evidence, not proof the policy failed. |
| Bounded visibility or reclaim, not bounded retention | Overlay reads default to five-minute visibility; dirty and bulk work use 15-minute stale reclaim; chunk/provider/file leases use expiry; bulk retries default to three | Rows can become unreadable or reclaimable at a bounded time/state. | A visibility/reclaim threshold does not delete history or prove terminal settlement, row age, pin release or cleanup. |
| Key-replaced/control state without a time horizon | Job health, closeout/backfill, reconciliation/project-import cursors, projector watermarks and retention marks update a key/scope rather than append every observation | Current writers bound repeated updates only for the same identity. | Identity cardinality, retired-key cleanup, duplicates, deployed drift and an age/count horizon remain unavailable; these histories are not called physically unbounded from source alone. |
| Apparently unbounded under checked-in identity growth | Execution snapshots; terminal import markers outside archived-project cleanup; dirty rows and point ACKs; projection/selected/snapshot headers; pins; rebuild requests/chunks; overlays; bulk/search jobs and result state | Exact current searches find no general scheduled delete/retention path for these growing identity families. Selected bases and final serving rows are in the separate 11-table bounded cleanup registry; obsolete non-running chunks can be replaced within one request. | Whether deployed rows exist or accumulate, their counts/ages/bytes and the intended horizon. “Apparently unbounded” is a source-lifecycle classification, never a measured physical conclusion. |
| Source-proven lifecycle gaps | Dirty-ACK compaction, pin release/expiry and overlay reconcile/expire helpers have no non-test caller; search has no executor/terminal cleanup; bulk terminal paths do not settle pins; the 11-table retention registry omits the control/header/job families; all-complete rebuild finalization failure has no automatic readmission path | These missing current-source owners/callers and state-machine edges are evidence-backed lifecycle defects/gaps independent of physical volume. | Deployed impact, occurrence rate, retained history and byte cost still require the approved fixture/runtime collector. |

### Measurement Definitions And Width Boundaries

For a frozen checkpoint and explicit scope `s`, let `N(T,s)` be the exact row
count of physical table `T`; `U(c,s)=SUM(c IS NULL)`; and
`D(c,s)=COUNT(DISTINCT c)`. Any approximate distinct result must also name its
algorithm, error bound and seed and cannot replace `D` where an exact boundary
is required. Ratios use their named table/scope denominator and report empty
denominators explicitly rather than manufacturing zero.

Let `E(type,value)` be the owner-approved canonical scalar/list/JSON encoder
and `b_E(value)` its encoded byte length. For one exact field mapping and
checkpoint, byte-exact duplicate payload is
`Dup_E(c,s)=SUM_v((N(c=v,s)-1)*b_E(v))` for non-null values with frequency
above one. Null encoding, tuple framing, JSON key order and cross-table field
equivalence must be specified before inclusion. Cross-family duplicates are
reported only through an explicit field map; logical duplicates never include
index, WAL, temp or database-container overhead.

For one concrete query `Q`, `Q_pre` is the logical joined/qualified row set
after `FROM/JOIN/WHERE/QUALIFY` and before outer `ORDER BY/LIMIT`; `Q_page` is
the returned page including the documented lookahead row; and `Q_hyd` is every
later payload/detail/current-source hydration row. Record row count plus
`SUM`, p50, p95, p99 and max `b_E(projected row)` separately for `Q_pre`,
`Q_page` and each `Q_hyd` call, then separately record final serialized response
bytes. These are logical widths. Optimizer operator cardinality/bytes, rows
scanned, sort/hash/window state, spill and peak temp are separate profile
outputs and cannot be inferred merely because SQL projects a column before
`LIMIT`.

Rows written are statement/stage counters for inserted, conflict-updated,
matched-updated and deleted rows. `R_full` counts rows emitted through full-row
delete/insert, replace or all-non-key `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` shapes;
column-targeted updates remain separate. Neither counter is a DuckDB physical
block rewrite, WAL-byte or database-growth measure. Process start/end/peak RSS,
sampling cadence and topology remain separate from DuckDB temp/spill bytes and
the two connection-temporary selected-import tables.

### Measurement Definitions And Statement Boundaries

For a frozen checkpoint and explicit scope `s`, let `N(T,s)` be the exact row
count; `U(c,s)=SUM(c IS NULL)`; and `D(c,s)=COUNT(DISTINCT c)`. For a named
grouping tuple `g`, `K(T,g,s)=COUNT(DISTINCT g)` and its fan-out is
`N(T,s)/NULLIF(K(T,g,s),0)`. Every filtered count retains its exact predicate,
denominator and empty-denominator result. Approximation requires a named
algorithm, version, seed and error bound and never silently replaces exact
cardinality.

Let `E(type,value)` be the owner-approved canonical scalar/list/JSON encoder
and `b_E(value)` its encoded byte length. Byte-exact duplicate payload is
`Dup_E(c,s)=SUM_v((N(c=v,s)-1)*b_E(v))` for non-null repeated values. Tuple
framing, null encoding, JSON key order and cross-table equivalence must be
approved before combining fields. Logical and duplicate bytes never include
indexes, WAL, operator/connection/spill temporary state, RSS or database-
container overhead.

For each stage and statement, record `W_insert`, `W_conflict_update`,
`W_matched_update`, `W_delete` and `W_unchanged`. `R_full` counts logical rows
emitted through scoped delete/reinsert, replacement or an upsert that assigns
every non-key column. It is not a DuckDB block/page rewrite. A read-modify-write
sequence records the read statement/result cardinality, dependent transform,
each DML statement, transaction/snapshot boundary, affected rows and failure
point; a source-level statement count or before/after table delta cannot fill
those fields.

Temporary evidence has four independent grains:

- durable partial and accumulator rows remain ordinary `N(T,s)` rows until a
  proven delete;
- connection-temporary rows record declaration, load, scoped clear/replace,
  peak rows/logical bytes, last use, explicit drop and connection teardown;
- optimizer work records operator cardinality/memory/temp/spill from the
  approved profile, never inferred from a CTE declaration; and
- spill-directory evidence records the active configured/effective path,
  pre/stage/peak/post/checkpoint/cleanup file count and allocated/apparent bytes.

For high-fan-out rows, snapshot generation state is joined to the owning
snapshot/component manifest and pins. Active, candidate, LKG, retired, failed,
pinned and orphan counts remain distinct. Rebuild partials additionally retain
request/chunk status and output-base-generation. Comparison temp configuration
uses `(comparison_project_id,generation)` and connection lifetime; selected-
import temps have no generation column. Migration ledger state is completion,
not a serving generation. No identity is relabeled as a generic generation.

### Measurement Definitions, File Identity And Byte Boundaries

For one approved frozen checkpoint `t` and scope `s`, let `N(T,s)` be the
exact table row count, `U(c,s)=SUM(c IS NULL)` and
`D(c,s)=COUNT(DISTINCT c)`. For a declared grain `g`,
`K(T,g,s)=COUNT(DISTINCT g)` and fan-out is
`N(T,s)/NULLIF(K(T,g,s),0)`. Every status/generation/token/age predicate,
denominator and empty result is retained. For a named timestamp `x`,
`Age_t(x)=t-x`; report null/invalid/future counts, min/p50/p95/max and
owner-approved buckets. A table without an applicable timestamp receives a
cited `not-applicable` age subcheck rather than an invented creation time.

Let `E(type,value)` be the owner-approved scalar/list/JSON/file-payload
encoder and `b_E(value)` its encoded length. Logical payload is
`L_E(S)=SUM b_E(value)` over a named field/value set. Repeated logical bytes
are
`Dup_E(c,s)=SUM_v((N(c=v,s)-1)*b_E(v))` for non-null equal values.
Cross-table equivalence requires an approved field map; JSON key order,
framing, null encoding, compression and decoded-versus-raw file payload are
recorded. Logical bytes exclude indexes, WAL, temp/spill, RSS, database
container overhead and filesystem allocation.

For every approved root `r`, `F(r,t)` is the canonical inventory after
lexical validation and final-target resolution. Each entry records root,
relative and canonical path, file type, device/inode, hard-link count,
symlink target, owner/mode, apparent bytes `B_app`, allocated bytes
`B_alloc` and owner-approved time fields. Counts and sums are reported per
family/root/type before any union. Byte-identical regular-file duplication is
grouped by approved cryptographic algorithm/version and
`(content_length,content_hash)`. `Dup_file` counts extra apparent content
copies; canonical `(device,inode)` grouping separately prevents hard links
from being mislabeled as extra physical allocation. A checksum, package
fingerprint or persisted path is not file-existence, reference-equality,
retention or restore evidence.

The byte/resource ledgers never derive one category by subtracting another:

- logical database/file payload and `Dup_E`;
- named-index bytes when attributable, otherwise an approved plan and
  maintenance/rebuild cost;
- active DuckDB `.wal` bytes at exact checkpoint boundaries;
- active DuckDB spill and application temporary paths/bytes;
- active database-container apparent/allocated bytes;
- ordinary backup/snapshot/control/content/import/transfer/generated/client
  file count, apparent/allocated bytes and `Dup_file`; and
- process RSS by named process and sampling interval.

Application direct writes, append, overwrite, temp/rename and streamed
responses are file-publication techniques, not storage-engine WAL. Therefore
the ordinary non-database subset `DBO-0294`-`DBO-0322` has a source-proven
`not-applicable` application-WAL proof check. DuckDB `DBO-0292` remains the
applicable WAL family; OS/filesystem journaling is outside this application
collector unless separately approved. `not-applicable` does not mean zero
bytes, atomic multi-file publication, crash safety or successful cleanup.

Generation and cleanup retain native identities. Comparison active/staged
generation, legacy V3 active generation, dirty/refresh tokens, quarantine
resolution, transfer revision/session/commit/target token, startup-recovery
group, backup/snapshot identity, file checksum/version and client download are
not one generation. Cleanup invocation, durable per-step/cycle receipt,
bounded schedule, concurrent-reader lease, reference scan, post-cleanup
inventory and executable family restore validation are recorded separately.

`Claim: not applicable` below means the checked-in family is not a claimable
queue; it is a source-contract observation, not a `proofCheckState` value.

Update: conflict readback; later migrations can remap a relational model ID without rewriting embedded identity. | Claim: referenced by queue claim, not itself claimed. and async search job each have one table grain and one column-family grain.

approved retirement/replacement owner closes current and deployed references,
inventories and migrates/receipts every row, preserves required recovery or
audit history, removes supporting-index and registry contracts, and proves
API/browser/desktop/export/transfer parity, rollback, retention, same-fixture
benchmark and executable restore. No `move`, `derive` or `archive` row is
introduced by US-075.

or omission:

`recommendationActionability: unresolved` and zero are actionable. The 62

The result-manifest acceptance family deliberately cross-references its single
US-075 ownership assignment. Creating another object or column-family
disposition would claim the same logical JSON and backing fields twice.
Likewise, projection-input watermarks remain the US-075 logical/field
dispositions even though projection manifests consume them. US-076 adds only
the nine object and eight field-family decisions above.

All 17 new rows retain provisional `keep` homes because current source
creates, mutates or consumes them for projection publication, selected-import
resume/rebuild, active/LKG reads, pin protection, rebuild recovery or
reviewer-write visibility. A keep disposition does not certify immutable
identity, publication completeness, recovery, retention, cleanup safety,
physical value or final ownership. No new `move`, `derive`, `archive` or
`delete` recommendation is introduced.

### Publication, Retry, Pin, Active, LKG, Recovery And Cleanup Contracts

`Not directly pinned` or `not an active/LKG object` below is a source-contract
observation, not a `proofCheckState` value. Every family records publication,
retry, pin, active, last-known-good, recovery, retention, orphan, cleanup and
replacement evidence separately.

| Family | Publication and retry | Pin, active and last-known-good | Recovery | Retention, orphan and cleanup | Provisional replacement boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Projection identity | Component writers upsert candidate generation/patch/input/config state under a stable manifest key; dirty/rebuild replay can rewrite it, but the row has no independent retry machine. | Not directly pinned or active/LKG. Snapshot composition copies its state, while later upserts can mutate the source manifest under the same key. | Bootstrap/rebuild and diagnostics can reconstruct or validate source state; startup indexed repair omits this table. | No retirement/delete schedule. Orphans include stale components, config/generation drift and copied snapshot state that no longer equals the manifest. No cleanup receipt or restore result. | `keep` until a versioned immutable component-publication replacement maps all 11 writers/readers, migrates history and proves replay, parity, retention and restore; `EVD-0863`/`EVD-0870`, `BLK-0409`. |
| Selected-import header and base | Header cursor publishes candidate/completed progress while base rows publish deterministic winners. Retry resumes the four-key cursor; rebuild can delete header/base and replay, while dirty/range paths can reuse the selected ID. | Header/base are not independently active/LKG. Serving manifests reference the selected ID; active/LKG/pins indirectly protect matching bases, not a unique immutable header version. | Worker reset/drain and startup probes cover both tables, but probe restoration and existence do not prove crash-safe recovery or header/base atomicity. | Retention can delete unprotected base rows only. Header cleanup, completed-history horizon, FK/reference scan and orphan receipt are absent. | `keep` both tables until an immutable selected-publication contract preserves ordering, header/base completion, reset/retry, all consumers and restore; `EVD-0864`/`EVD-0866`/`EVD-0870`, `BLK-0410`. |
| Serving snapshot and components | Candidate creation/refresh copies component state; promotion revalidates then retires same-config active rows and activates the candidate transactionally. Retry is rebuild/candidate recreation; invalid validation returns without a mandatory failed transition. | Active, LKG pointer and retired fallback are distinct. Pins copy composed identity. No SQL single-active, selected/component FK or copied-identity equality fence exists. | Diagnostics and warnings can observe/admit repair; startup probe mutates/restores candidate/failed rows. Neither is a publication receipt or executable family restore. | Data cleanup protects active/LKG/pinned state, but snapshot manifests/components have no terminal/failed/retired sweep, retirement timestamp/owner, reader lease or orphan scan. | `keep` manifest and logical component state until a versioned immutable publication ledger proves single-active/LKG/pin equality, failed recovery, retention and restore; `EVD-0865`/`EVD-0866`/`EVD-0870`, `BLK-0411`. |
| Snapshot pin | Acquire hashes project/snapshot/composed identity/owner and increments ref count on conflict. No production retry beyond reacquisition. | A live row protects the named snapshot when unreleased, positive-count and unexpired. Bulk job acquisition is separate from job insert; active/LKG remain manifest states, not pin states. | Increment/release/expire helpers exist, but only acquisition has a non-test caller; no startup settlement or owner repair exists. | Pin rows are not deleted. Terminal jobs can retain active pins; orphan owner/snapshot/identity mismatch, expiry settlement, reference scan and cleanup receipt are unresolved. | `keep` until atomic owner admission, release/expiry scheduling, orphan repair, retained-history policy and restore are proven; `EVD-0866`/`EVD-0869`, `BLK-0412`. |
| Rebuild request | Deterministic request admission groups component work and finalization records completion/failure. Conflict re-admission resets execution state; request retry/lease columns are not an operating claimant. | Not directly pinned. Identity can name a candidate snapshot, while active/LKG state changes only during later promotion. | Requestless adoption, diagnostics, startup/post-repair updates and re-admission provide partial recovery. Failed all-complete finalization is marked terminal and is not automatically selected again. | Obsolete non-running chunks can be replaced during explicit request upsert, but terminal requests/history have no bounded sweep, reference scan or cleanup receipt. | `keep` until request/chunk/candidate admission and finalization have one durable retryable phase/receipt or an approved replacement migrates every terminal/recovery state; `EVD-0867`/`EVD-0870`, `BLK-0413`. |
| Rebuild chunk | Planned chunks publish component/range/budget identity. Pending, retryable-failed or expired-running rows can be owner-fenced claimed; heartbeat, retry/backoff, split, validation and completion are persisted. | Optional snapshot/request/parent references do not create a pin. Chunks can write candidate or active-derived outputs, but active/LKG publication is a later step. | Stale lease reclaim, requestless release/adoption, split children, idempotent-output validation and startup/post-repair probes supply partial recovery. Output can exist before completed state. | No FK, abandoned-output compensation, terminal chunk horizon, parent/request/snapshot orphan sweep, cleaner/reader lease or restore receipt exists. | `keep` until output/completion/finalization recovery and every request/parent/snapshot relationship are fenced, retained and restorable; `EVD-0867`/`EVD-0870`, `BLK-0413`. |
| Write overlay | Human submission appends a pending row/detail overlay with source high water and TTL. No retry/consumer schedule is wired beyond conflict upsert. | Not pinned and not active/LKG state; it is a reviewer-write visibility contract scoped by project/article/config/surface. | Callable active-read, reconcile and expire helpers exist, but current non-test closure invokes only append. Startup repair and restore omit overlays. | Expiry filters visibility but does not delete or durably receipt settlement. Pending-expired, reconciled and source/config/article/prompt orphans have no scan or horizon. | `keep` while the writer operates and read-your-write/settlement intent is unresolved; replacement requires consumer parity, watermark receipt, migration/history, cleanup and restore; `EVD-0868`/`EVD-0870`, `BLK-0414`. |
| Bulk result manifest | Existing job/result rows publish initial, progress, PDF and export variants; stale-time claim/retry can replace or merge them without claimant CAS. | Pinned jobs acquire a separate pin before insert; latest jobs resolve active state later. Terminal result does not itself establish active/LKG or pin settlement. | Stale-running reclaim and cursor/result persistence allow partial replay, but side effects and result merges are not owner-fenced. Export later re-resolves/hydrates rows and assets. | `expires_at` is unwritten; no terminal job/result/artifact sweep or pin release exists. Orphans include result without complete side effects, job without pin and result selection diverging from hydration. | Existing `DSP-0102`/`DSP-0128` remain `keep` until a versioned checksummed result, frozen hydration identity, idempotent recovery, pin settlement, retention and restore replacement is proved; `EVD-0869`/`EVD-0870`, `BLK-0415`. |

### US-078 Scope, Prerequisite And State Boundary

US-077 is complete. US-078 continues the normalized Phase 5 disposition
register without reopening the Phase 3 manifests or substituting blocked
Phase 4 measurements. Physical tables, disjoint material column families and
supporting indexes remain separate accounting grains:

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Title-token search | `DBO-0153` | `CMF-1221`-`CMF-1229` (9) | `DBO-0159` | — |
| Async substring control | — | — | `DBO-0139` remains prior owner evidence | Search job `DBO-0131` and `CMF-1027`-`CMF-1047`, `CMF-1082` remain `DSP-0100`/`DSP-0129`. |

| **US-078 new total** | **Three physical tables = three object decisions** | **29 physical fields exactly once** | **Three supporting indexes retained as evidence, not recounted** | **Two prior substring rows revalidated with zero new recommendations.** |

The title-token table and async substring job are different contracts. Active
mounted list/count and bulk paths plus the registered queue/Human-init read use
snapshot-scoped token-prefix membership; the standalone token service has no
checked-in mounted caller.
The separate substring service can insert and observe one pending job, but no
checked-in caller or executor owns results. Likewise, the function named
`projectReviewServingQueuePatches` directly replaces active queue-serving
rows and reports zero physical patch rows; it does not write
`mart.review_queue_patch_v4`.

Current source supports provisional `keep` homes for the title-token and
active unassessed-queue tables. Their retained fields are limited to exact
snapshot/selectivity, eligibility, priority, ordering and keyset contracts.
Repeated title/activity auxiliaries are a provisional `move` to a bounded
one-row-per-snapshot/article validation shape, while per-row search/queue
timestamps are provisional `derive` candidates from immutable component/chunk
publication receipts after startup-probe replacement. The physical queue
patch is a provisional `delete` candidate at table and field grains. The
existing async-substring table/field delete candidates remain unresolved and
are not counted again. No move, derive or delete is actionable.

Every affected DBO and CMF row remains `auditStatus: blocked`. `FAN-0051` and
`FAN-0052` retain `proofCheckState: blocked`; no `PRF-####` row changes. All
new and revalidated `DSP-####` rows retain
`recommendationActionability: unresolved`, and `overallCertification` remains
independently `INCOMPLETE`. The shared proof references are `PRF-0004`,
`PRF-0006`, `PRF-0008` and `PRF-0016`.

No live/current/project DuckDB or SQLite file, configured snapshot/query/
studio, fixture DDL/DML, server, app, browser, desktop shell, worker,
projector, migration, startup repair, export, transfer, cleanup, benchmark or
physical collector ran. Only this audit file and required Ralph tracker
metadata may change.

### Bounded Search, Queue And Alternative Contracts

The budgets below are source-declared admission boundaries, not physical
measurements. A retained field must name its exact selectivity, snapshot,
eligibility, priority, ordering or keyset need. A move or derive must preserve
the immutable publication identity and bounded read grain; a delete candidate
must close deployed state and lifecycle rather than relying on source absence.

| Family and exact fields | Proven current requirement and source budget | Bounded move/derive/delete alternative | Publication, lifecycle and recovery boundary | Browser/desktop consequence and unresolved proof |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Token scope/membership: `project_id`, `search_identity`, `project_scope_identity`, `snapshot_id`, `token`, `article_id` (`CMF-1221`-`CMF-1226`) | All-token `starts_with` intersections constrain mounted list/count and bulk membership plus registered queue/Human-init selection before order/limit. Snapshot/component/scope identity prevents cross-publication joins. Standalone raw search is at most 50 rows/2 MB/5 s ordered by token/article but has no mounted caller. | — | Dirty/full writers replace exact snapshot token rows; optional search publication, active/LKG/pin retention and immutable tokenizer/version equality remain blocked. | Shared search controls submit text, but token rows are not rendered. Web/desktop request/cache/hash parity and deployed selectivity/index plans are unavailable. |
| Search article auxiliaries: `title_prefix`, `activity_sort_at` (`CMF-1227`-`CMF-1228`) | `title_prefix` participates in strict rebuild-chunk checksum; `activity_sort_at` is copied but has no checked-in reader. Neither selects embedded membership/order; generic standalone `SELECT *` is unmounted. | `move` candidate to at most one row per `(project_id,search_identity,project_scope_identity,snapshot_id,article_id)` carrying only an owner-approved normalized-title digest/prefix and activity diagnostic. Validation must range by bounded rebuild chunk and may not rejoin mutable current source. | Publish/validate/retain the auxiliary row with the same immutable search snapshot; backfill/migrate per-token values, preserve rollback, settle old rows/indexes and prove restore before removal. | No current rendered field changes, but standalone/API shape and browser/desktop parity must be explicitly retired or preserved. Physical fan-out/byte savings remain unavailable. |
| Search row time: `search_updated_at` (`CMF-1229`) | Writer timestamp and startup mutation/restore cell only; no membership, order, result or mounted response use. | `derive` candidate from an immutable search component/chunk publication receipt keyed by project/search/scope/snapshot. ## US-079 Provisional Posting, Summary, Filter, Partial And Index Dispositions

### US-079 Scope, Prerequisite And State Boundary

US-078 is complete. US-079 continues the normalized Phase 5 register without
reopening Phase 3 lineage or substituting the blocked US-071 physical
measurements. Physical tables, material column families and named indexes are
three separate accounting grains:

| Family | Table disposition scope | Disjoint material-field scope | Separate associated-index scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Posting patch | `DBO-0162` | `CMF-1264`-`CMF-1274` (11) | `DBO-0171` |
| Posting serving and statistics | `DBO-0163`-`DBO-0164` | `CMF-1275`-`CMF-1294`, `CMF-1379`-`CMF-1380` (22) | `DBO-0172`; the stats lookup dropped by 0114 is historical state, not a current object disposition |
| Persistent contribution | `DBO-0165` | `CMF-1295`-`CMF-1303` (9) | `DBO-0173` |
| Named count and facet serving | `DBO-0166`-`DBO-0167` | `CMF-1304`-`CMF-1329` (26) | `DBO-0174`-`DBO-0175` |
| Filter-option serving | `DBO-0168` | `CMF-1330`-`CMF-1345`, `CMF-1381`-`CMF-1384` (20) | `DBO-0176` |
| Request-scoped partials | `DBO-0169`-`DBO-0170` | `CMF-1346`-`CMF-1378`, `CMF-1385`-`CMF-1386` (35) | `DBO-0177`-`DBO-0178` |
| **US-079 total** | **Nine physical tables = nine table decisions** | **123 CMF rows exactly once = 29 disjoint field decisions** | **Eight current named indexes = eight separate index decisions; one historical dropped index is revalidated but not recounted** |

Current source supports provisional `keep` homes for active posting serving,
posting cardinality state, exact named counts, named facets, prompt filter
options and both rebuild-partial tables. The posting patch and persistent
contribution table have no exact non-migration production owner and are
provisional `delete` candidates at table, field and index grains. Those six
rows represent two physical targets, not six independent tables.

Posting row kinds remain separate logical contracts within the one retained
posting table. `promptAnswer` has mounted foreground and bulk membership use;
`duplicateFlag` and `conflictFlag` have bulk membership use while mounted list
routes use candidate columns instead. `importRoute`, `publicationYear`,
`llmStatus` and `humanStatus` have writers, validation and lifecycle state but
no exact current product posting read, so those row families are provisional
delete candidates without claiming the shared table or fields a second time.
The corresponding stats groups follow the posting-kind decision.

The count table retains six exact named definitions: `review.list.total`,
`review.queue.unassessedReady` and the four prompt-oriented benchmark/internal
definitions. The fixed-unavailable `review.list.filteredTotal` row family is a
provisional delete candidate because mounted dynamic counts bypass it and run
exact direct aggregation. All six named facet families remain provisionally
retained for the two mounted filter routes even though the current controls
ignore raw `facets`. Prompt-answer and Human-summary option groups remain
retained because the server derives the UI `filters` from them; simple/status
option groups are provisional row-family delete candidates because they are
only returned raw. These row-family decisions do not create duplicate table or
CMF disposition rows.

Index decisions are not inferred from `CREATE INDEX` text. `DBO-0174`-
`DBO-0178` receive conditional provisional keeps tied to their exact one-row,
128-row, 512-row or request-reduction access shapes. `DBO-0172` is a
provisional derive/replace candidate because the current sort-before-article
shape serves the unmounted direct ordering contract differently from active
membership probes. `FAN-0064` and `FAN-0072` still record every applied
existence, selected plan, rows scanned/output, residual, timing, maintenance
and cost value as `unavailable`. Therefore no index is measured, certified or
actionable; source predicate alignment is only the reason to preserve the
current five conditional keeps pending measurement.

Every affected DBO and CMF row remains `auditStatus: blocked`.
`FAN-0060`-`FAN-0064` and `FAN-0067`-`FAN-0074` retain
`proofCheckState: blocked`; no `PRF-####` row changes. All 46 new `DSP-####`
rows retain `recommendationActionability: unresolved`, including every
provisional keep, and `overallCertification` remains independently
`INCOMPLETE`. Shared proof references are `PRF-0004`, `PRF-0006`,
`PRF-0008` and `PRF-0016`.

No live/current/project DuckDB or SQLite file, configured snapshot/query/
studio, fixture DDL/DML, server, app, browser, desktop shell, worker,
projector, migration, startup repair, export, transfer, cleanup, benchmark or
physical collector ran. Only this audit file and required Ralph tracker
metadata may change.

### Intermediate Ownership, Lifecycle, Replay And Recovery Contracts

| Physical family | Retained owner and active lifecycle | Cleanup, replay and recovery boundary | Provisional consequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Posting serving/stats | Posting dirty/full projector; request finalizer refreshes stats; chunk checksum and startup probes validate; active/LKG/pins protect snapshot cleanup. | Posting and stats publication are separate; no ordinary-reader lease, applied physical profile or crash-safe startup restore exists. Stats denominator/identity equality and row-kind retirement remain unresolved. | Keep active membership/cardinality state; move/derive repeated order, identity, selectivity and row-time fields only after bounded replacement proof. |
| Count/facet serving | Summary dirty/direct and request-partial reducer; one request-snapshot transaction replaces count/facet outputs; mounted/internal readers and startup/retention consume them. | Chunk completion, reduction, final publication, option refresh, promotion and terminalization are not one transaction. Finalization failure after all chunks complete lacks proven readmission. | Keep exact retained variants; row-family deletes and derived fields remain unresolved. |
| Filter options | Review/Human projector and rebuild finalizer replace identity scopes; mounted filter routes read bounded rows; startup and active/LKG/pin retention apply. | Review/Human refresh can be separate; requested filters/search do not narrow current stored identity; no physical plan or browser/desktop parity exists. | Keep prompt-derived groups; remove raw-only groups/fields only after contract closure. |
| Summary partial/accumulator | Chunk writer owns source rows; completed manifests fence 256-chunk reduction; accumulator is request/project/config/snapshot scoped and publishes count/facet rows. | Reduced source summary rows are deleted, but accumulator rows remain. Failed/abandoned/orphan/terminal cleanup, durable lease, replay cursor, retention schedule and restore validation are absent. | Keep as active intermediate state, with `recommendationActionability: unresolved` and lifecycle blocker. |
| Contribution partial | Chunk writer owns request/chunk/article/component/version/key rows; completed-manifest join deduplicates them into accumulator counts. | Same-chunk rewrite deletes old rows, but no successful-terminal, failed, abandoned or orphan delete exists; cheap validation omits them. | Keep as active intermediate state, with mandatory terminal cleanup/replay/recovery proof. |
| Posting patch/persistent contribution | Migration/index/test maintenance only; current direct-serving/in-memory/partial paths bypass them. | No deployed inventory, producer/consumer history, migration receipt, retention, cleanup, rollback or executable restore. | Delete candidates only; static absence is not actionability. |

### Product, Migration, Recovery, Path And Replacement Planes

| Family | Current product and bounded lookup | Migration, repair and recovery | Path/key, atomicity and browser/desktop | Retention, cleanup and provisional replacement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Active comparison | Config/source tables bind project, route, prompt, source-project and conflict identity; active generation gates list/count/stats; article order, cell hydration and stats have exact keys. Filter-member storage is not a demonstrated reader. | Generation rebuild, promotion, old-generation cleanup and startup mutation probe are separate; no immutable config or reader pin closes them. | No direct file home; comparison CSV/JSON downloads are client-owned. Current copied article payload precedes limit in one wide table. | Keep active keys/marts, delete unread filter-member state, and move copied display/full-text/source payload to bounded generation-scoped post-selection hydration only after parity and rollback proof. |
| Telemetry and local config | Newest 50 LLM and newest 30 GPU rows serve diagnostics; current user settings configure identity, PDF and maintenance memory. | No prune/restore owner for telemetry; settings malformed-input fallback and legacy-key rewrite are not history. | Database rows only; desktop shares the rebased database/settings root through API, not direct file access. | Keep a bounded hot diagnostic/config home; archive older telemetry under an approved redacted versioned policy. Delete five retired tuning columns only after deployed/config parity. |
| Legacy control and marts | Dirty/quarantine/refresh tokens still gate queue/status/ACK/operator paths; ordinal, V3 generation, dictionary and derived legacy marts lack exact current readers. | Operator scripts, archived cleanup and migration history remain; current V4 repair does not consume the old marts. | Database keys are native project/article/prompt/generation/token identities; no file or client contract is inferred. | Keep surviving gates, archive one-way/recoverable audit state, archive potentially divergent answer/detail history, and delete purely derived retired state only after deployed/reference/restore closure. |
| Transfer control and packages | Session/history/fingerprint/token lookups and v1/v2 import/export paths are current and bounded by source contracts. | Startup and 60-second recovery, TTL cleanup, rollback and promotion manifests cover different phases, not one transaction. | DB session state, temp roots, ZIP members, promoted assets, download and target visibility are separate keys/publications. Browser Blob and desktop bridge are not native save proof. | Keep active control/package/session homes; archive approved source packages/history; clean terminal roots only with reader leases and durable receipts. |
| Migration and runtime temporary shapes | Migration shapes are upgrade-local; runtime shapes stage bounded set operations, probes, publication and transfer work. | Nontransactional migration ledger insertion, process crash, connection reuse and current-scope clearing remain gaps. | No durable path is inferred from a TEMP declaration; engine spill and application temp tables are separate. | Keep required operation/migration shapes; move detach/config shapes to crash-safe or bounded-connection homes; require explicit teardown/orphan receipts. |
| Database, content and generated files | Database/WAL/spill, PDFs/import payloads, provider cache, backups, logs, locks, recovery files, transfer assets and downloads each retain their exact producer/consumer. | Checkpoint, backup copy, startup recovery, sidecars and source regeneration are not interchangeable restore contracts. | Web cwd and desktop data-root rebasing, path/reference equality, symlink/final target, direct versus temp/rename publication and client save are separate. | Keep authoritative/active assets, archive approved backups/source payloads/recovery evidence, delete ephemeral snapshots/spools after durable receipts, and never infer file deletion from missing database references. |

### Cross-Reference And Row-Lifecycle Decisions

- `DSP-0001` and `DSP-0024` continue to keep DuckDB full-text scalars,
  references and article payload. `DBO-0304`, `DBO-0305`, `DBO-0313` and
  `DBO-0322` receive the separate physical-file/runtime-route homes below.
- Active telemetry tables remain hot keeps; rows older than an owner-approved
  query/recovery window are a non-counted `archive` row-family candidate.
  No archive can begin without redaction, version, lookup and restore proof.
- Transfer history remains a hot idempotency/audit keep; older completed rows
  are a non-counted archive candidate only after session/package/reference and
  target-visibility closure.
- Migration/runtime TEMP declarations stay shape decisions. Successful drop,
  `finally`, `CREATE OR REPLACE`, current-scope reload and connection teardown
  do not prove crash cleanup, bounded residue or safe replacement.
- `DBO-0294` is the retained cold recovery copy; `DBO-0295` and `DBO-0314`
  are ephemeral delete-after-use homes. Four client download rows remain
  generated browser/OS-owned artifacts with no invented server-retained file.

## US-081 Source And Configuration Proof Requirements

### US-081 Scope, Prerequisite And State Boundary

US-080 is complete. US-081 pairs the exact US-073 source/configuration
dispositions with finite positive and negative proof checks; it does not reopen
their object, column-family or supporting-index accounting. The six family
scopes remain article, import, project/scope, prompt, model/provider and review
configuration. The bridge delete target and six logical derive targets are
also recorded separately because one family-level proof state cannot stand in
for target ownership, cutover or cleanup.

registered route, migration text or planned test is only evidence toward that
predicate. No actual browser/desktop parity, export, transfer, recovery,
migration, retention or physical benchmark work ran, and none is recorded as

projection-input subshape, 145 disjoint material fields or ten supporting
indexes. Judgment execution outboxes, job-local ACKs and cursors, jobs,
leases, bulk/search state and retention marks remain later asynchronous-
control proof scope; the reusable import hot fact remains US-082 scope.

replay, repair, startup, transfer, export, retention, consumer watermark and
cleanup. A source write, `reconciled_at`, local `completed`, ACK row, mutable
cursor or watermark is evidence for its own grain only. None proves every
downstream consumer observed equivalent immutable output, establishes safe
pruning or supplies a recovery receipt.

target row is independently `blocked`. Existing `PRF-0001`-`PRF-0155` retain
their states, so the complete 216-row proof register is eight `satisfied`, 98
`pending`, 110 `blocked` and zero `not-applicable`. No writer/projector,

validation ran, and none is recorded as passed.

Each family has exactly ten independently stateful checks: route, worker,
retry, lease, progress, recovery, export, transfer, pin and cleanup. A route
response, local terminal status, successful claim, heartbeat, cursor, result
JSON, retained pin, expiry field or cleanup invocation proves only its own
grain. None proves end-to-end result visibility, restart convergence,
exactly-once side effects, portable recovery, reader-safe cleanup or later
workload equality.

The 110 family rows are independently 66 `pending` and 44 `blocked`; the one
target row is independently `blocked`. Existing `PRF-0001`-`PRF-0271` retain
their states, so the complete 382-row proof register is eight `satisfied`, 194
`pending`, 180 `blocked` and zero `not-applicable`. No route/browser/desktop,
worker, retry race, lease takeover, progress reconciliation, restart/failure,
export, transfer, pin settlement, cleanup or later workload validation ran,
and none is recorded as passed.

required blocked target contract. The other 52 paired keep rows remain

zero recommendations are actionable. Across all 441 `DSP-####` rows, 423 are
unresolved, 18 are blocked and zero are actionable.

source-proven `not-applicable` row, all prior proof states remain unchanged,
and `overallCertification` remains independently `INCOMPLETE`. No

### Non-Keep Asynchronous-Control Replacement Contract

This target row is separate from the search-job family matrix and does not
authorize implementation. Every named contract and later immutable workload
receipt must pass before actionability can advance.

### Non-Keep Candidate, Display, Selected-Import, And Status Target Contracts

These target rows are separate from family preservation checks and do not
authorize implementation. Every named contract and later immutable workload
receipt must pass before actionability can advance.

For each moved/derived field target (`PRF-0448`-`PRF-0450`), bounded IDs mean
at most 501 route IDs, 101 article-set IDs, one detail ID or 500 export IDs;
the target row's versioned key and carried candidate ordinal govern hydration
and prohibit reordering. `PRF-0449` assigns selected-base writes to the full
and dirty selected projectors; their source/high-water and selected identity
invalidate the bounded derived lookup. Benchmark-critical identity
applicability is also
target-specific: display retirement (`PRF-0451`) must map review-config/model/
provider/thinking/content applicability to display identities or cite and
validate why each dimension cannot apply; selected retirement (`PRF-0452`)
must do the same against selected identity; Human retirement (`PRF-0454`) must
map those dimensions or validate each not-applicable decision. Column absence
is not that validation and never waives invalidation or history mapping.

| rowId | Target / linked dispositions | Bounded IDs, key, hydration and order preservation | Ownership, reads, writes and invalidation | Migration, cutover and rollback | Recovery, retention and cleanup | Later parity validation | proofCheckState / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PRF-0448` | Move 13 candidate display fields to bounded hydration; `DSP-0158` | Select the candidate ordered prefix first. Hydrate only the selected IDs: at most 501 route rows, 101 article-set rows, one detail ID or 500 export IDs. Display base/dirty/rebuild owns target writes; article/import/full-text changes invalidate display/payload identity before activation, with affected-row and ACK receipts. | Backfill every retained active/LKG/pinned snapshot with source/target counts, hashes, null/domain conflicts and ordinal equality; cut over readers then remove candidate copies without dual authority; keep versioned rollback until later validation passes. | Crash between target write, ACK, promotion and cutover must replay idempotently or restore the old copy. Target rows retain active/LKG/pin/export/reader protection; bounded cleanup records scanned/protected/deleted counts, hashes and durable completion before source-column removal. | On one approved immutable release candidate, compare mounted API responses, all list/detail/filter/bulk/export paths, browser normal-history and desktop hash-history requests/caches/navigation/renders, equal-key cursors, concurrent updates, restart/restore and later workloads byte-for-byte or by an approved semantic map. | `blocked`; `EVD-0877`-`EVD-0882`, `EVD-0992`-`EVD-1002`; `BLK-0499`; `OQ-0503` |

## US-087 Payload And Detail Proof Requirements

### US-087 Scope, Prerequisite And State Boundary

US-086 is complete. US-087 pairs the two payload-table and five disjoint
payload-field keep dispositions from US-077 with exact proof for article
payload, judgment payload, detail, prompt, full-text and admin behavior. It
does not reopen or recount two physical tables, 40 material fields or three
supporting indexes. The candidate-to-display move target remains `PRF-0448`;
canonical article/source dispositions remain US-081 scope; local-file
dispositions remain US-080 and object-by-object file/cold-storage proof remains
US-091. Search/queue is US-088 and posting/summary/filter/partial/index proof is
US-089.
