### Proposed Cardinality, Payload, Call And Termination Bounds

These are finite proposed maxima, not measured-safe or owner-approved values.
Later validation may lower them. It may not raise them silently, turn an
over-cap exact result into a partial/zero value, hide adapter retries, or drain
pages recursively inside one API, client or worker invocation.

| Contract | Per article/chunk/call maximum | Request/revision-wide maximum | Exact over-cap behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Project search build `TGT-0039` | 16 KB normalized title, 64 unique tokens and 4 KB encoded token bytes/article; 10,000 source articles, 640,000 token rows and 64 MB encoded rows/chunk | 10,000,000 source articles, 640,000,000 token rows, 64 GB encoded rows and 1,000 chunks/revision | Split the candidate range earlier. One article/title or revision overrun fails the candidate with observed count/range; no token or article is omitted. |
| Global facts/bindings `TGT-0040` | Same title/token caps per immutable fact; 10,000 new facts or 10,000 project bindings and 64 MB/chunk | 10,000,000 new fact versions, 640,000,000 fact-token rows and 10,000,000 project bindings per admitted build | Fact or binding candidate fails. It cannot hash-only reuse unmatched bytes, borrow another project's selected title or fall back to project current source. |
| Project foreground token search `TGT-0039` | Search text 256 UTF-8 bytes; eight unique normalized prefixes, each 64 bytes; 50,001 raw project-token rows/prefix probe, 50,001 distinct anchor articles, 1,000,000 point membership probes, 501 candidate rows and 2 MB | At most three database statements and three physical adapter attempts including revision/admission; five seconds; no automatic continuation | Probe/candidate sentinel, prefix-bound mismatch, unproved plan, timeout or byte/attempt excess returns indexing/async/unavailable before a ready page. A full first page is exact only in registered candidate order. |
| Global foreground token search `TGT-0040` | Same query caps; 100,001 raw global fact-token rows/prefix probe, 50,001 project-binding rows, 50,001 distinct project anchor articles, 1,000,000 point membership probes, 501 candidate rows and 2 MB | At most three database statements and three physical adapter attempts including fact/binding/revision admission; five seconds; no automatic continuation | Broad global prefix, binding/candidate sentinel, fact mismatch, unproved plan, timeout or byte/attempt excess returns async/unavailable. A small project never authorizes scanning an over-cap global posting. |
| Async substring `TGT-0041` | Query 256 UTF-8 bytes; 2,000 candidate titles and 32 MB normalized input/chunk; 2,000 result rows and 4 MB/chunk | 250,000 candidates, 512 MB input, 50,000 result rows/64 MB, 125 chunks, 512 physical attempts and three identical-setting attempts/chunk | Request is not admitted when a sealed candidate/input receipt exceeds a cap. Runtime overrun is terminal failed/unavailable with repairable state; no partial result is exposed as ready. |
| Queue build `TGT-0042`/`TGT-0044` | 512 eligible pairs and 64 KB encoded pair/order data/article; 10,000 source articles, 1,000,000 pair rows, 10,000 article rows and 128 MB/chunk | 10,000,000 articles, 100,000,000 pairs, 10,000,000 article summaries, 16 GB encoded rows and 1,000 chunks/revision | Split earlier by exact article keyset. A single article or revision overrun fails the candidate; pair/article counts remain unavailable rather than truncated. |
| Registered pair page `TGT-0043` | 100 rows plus one sentinel, 2 MB, one statement and five seconds | At most three statements/physical attempts including revision/cursor validation | Return at most 100 with a signed full-tuple cursor. Sentinel is continuation, not dropped work; missing tie-break/revision/order proof is unavailable. |
| Worker pair page `TGT-0043` | 5,000 rows plus one sentinel, 2 MB, one statement and five seconds | One explicit page/call; no read-all recursion | Return at most 5,000 with the full five-value cursor. More rows require the caller to persist and explicitly submit continuation. |
| Article page/preview `TGT-0044` | Mounted page 501 candidate sentinel rows/2 MB; preview 500 rows plus one sentinel/2 MB; exact count one row | Each operation has its own at-most-three-statement binding/read budget | Candidate page preserves candidate order; preview preserves maximum-priority order; count stays separate. No grouped pair scan or count substitution on overrun. |
| Intake receipt `TGT-0045` | Current-compatible maximum 128 fetched pairs plus one lookahead, 2 MB, one explicit window/tick; separate central/local rejection and insertion counts | 10,000,000 fetched pairs, 78,125 page receipts and 1 GB receipt/diagnostic bytes/selection epoch; physical attempts are counted per page and capped at 1,024 per epoch before explicit rollover | Stop the epoch before exceeding a cap and require an owner-approved new epoch/continuation. Never materialize all IDs, recurse until exhaustion, advance past an unreceipted page or coerce rejected rows to inserted progress. |

The search anchor bounds raw posting rows and distinct articles separately.
`LIMIT 50001` is only a sentinel inside a plan whose scanned rows, residuals,
sort and spill have later been proven; it is not itself plan proof. Queue pair,
article and intake caps likewise bound different grains. The design never
infers queue-pair cardinality from an article count or execution progress from
fetched/selected rows.

### Representative Exact SQL

The SQL below is design text only. It was not run or explained. An authorized
implementation must parameterize inputs, use the exact tokenizer/collation and
prefix-successor version, capture the applied plan, and reject any path that
scans, sorts, spills or probes beyond the declared maxima.

For project-specific tokens, one admission statement probes every normalized
prefix under the raw-row sentinel and selects an approved anchor. The result
statement bounds that raw anchor, intersects all remaining prefixes, then joins
the immutable candidate component to restore its registered order. It never
orders by copied search activity.

~~~sql
WITH requested_prefix(prefix_ordinal, prefix_lower, prefix_upper) AS (
  VALUES
    -- at most eight normalized, nonempty prefixes with exact exclusive upper bounds
    (0, $prefix_0_lower, $prefix_0_upper)
),
raw_anchor AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT token.article_id, token.token
  FROM mart.review_project_title_token_v5 AS token
  WHERE token.project_id = $project_id
    AND token.search_revision_id = $search_revision_id
    AND token.token >= $anchor_lower
    AND token.token < $anchor_upper
  ORDER BY token.token, token.article_id
  LIMIT 50001
),
anchor_guard AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS raw_row_count FROM raw_anchor
),
anchor_article AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT DISTINCT article_id FROM raw_anchor LIMIT 50001
),
matched AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT anchor.article_id
  FROM anchor_article AS anchor
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM requested_prefix AS requested
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM mart.review_project_title_token_v5 AS token
      WHERE token.project_id = $project_id
        AND token.search_revision_id = $search_revision_id
        AND token.article_id = anchor.article_id
        AND token.token >= requested.prefix_lower
        AND token.token < requested.prefix_upper
    )
  )
)
SELECT candidate.article_id, candidate.order_value
FROM anchor_guard
INNER JOIN matched ON anchor_guard.raw_row_count <= 50000
INNER JOIN mart.review_candidate_component_v5 AS candidate
  ON candidate.project_id = $project_id
 AND candidate.candidate_revision_id = $candidate_revision_id
 AND candidate.list_mode_key = $list_mode_key
 AND candidate.article_id = matched.article_id
WHERE ($cursor_order_value IS NULL OR
      (candidate.order_value, candidate.article_id) <
      ($cursor_order_value, $cursor_article_id))
ORDER BY candidate.order_value DESC, candidate.article_id DESC
LIMIT 501;
~~~

The reusable alternative bounds global token facts before project
intersection. The binding proves which immutable title fact the project
selected. A broad global prefix is unavailable or asynchronous even when the
project happens to be small; it never triggers an unbounded global scan.

~~~sql
WITH requested_prefix(prefix_ordinal, prefix_lower, prefix_upper) AS (
  VALUES
    -- at most eight normalized, nonempty prefixes with exact exclusive upper bounds
    (0, $prefix_0_lower, $prefix_0_upper)
),
global_raw AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT token.title_fact_id, token.token
  FROM mart.review_global_title_token_v5 AS token
  WHERE token.tokenizer_version = $tokenizer_version
    AND token.token >= $anchor_lower
    AND token.token < $anchor_upper
  ORDER BY token.token, token.title_fact_id
  LIMIT 100001
),
global_guard AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS raw_row_count FROM global_raw
),
project_anchor AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT DISTINCT binding.article_id, binding.title_fact_id
  FROM global_guard
  INNER JOIN global_raw ON global_guard.raw_row_count <= 100000
  INNER JOIN mart.review_project_search_binding_v5 AS binding
    ON binding.project_id = $project_id
   AND binding.search_revision_id = $search_revision_id
   AND binding.title_fact_id = global_raw.title_fact_id
  ORDER BY binding.article_id
  LIMIT 50001
)
SELECT project_anchor.article_id
FROM project_anchor
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM requested_prefix AS requested
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM mart.review_global_title_token_v5 AS token
    WHERE token.tokenizer_version = $tokenizer_version
      AND token.title_fact_id = project_anchor.title_fact_id
      AND token.token >= requested.prefix_lower
      AND token.token < requested.prefix_upper
  )
)
ORDER BY project_anchor.article_id
LIMIT 50001;
~~~

An asynchronous substring chunk scans one immutable candidate keyset and
selected title fact. It writes matching rows directly; it never accumulates a
project-wide ID array. Result order is the frozen requested order, while source
chunk order is an independent strict article keyset.

~~~sql
WITH candidate_chunk AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT candidate.article_id, candidate.order_value, binding.title_fact_id
  FROM mart.review_candidate_component_v5 AS candidate
  INNER JOIN mart.review_project_search_binding_v5 AS binding
    ON binding.project_id = candidate.project_id
   AND binding.search_revision_id = $search_revision_id
   AND binding.article_id = candidate.article_id
  WHERE candidate.project_id = $project_id
    AND candidate.candidate_revision_id = $candidate_revision_id
    AND candidate.article_id > $source_cursor_article_id
  ORDER BY candidate.article_id
  LIMIT 2001
),
bounded_chunk AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT * FROM candidate_chunk LIMIT 2000
)
INSERT INTO mart.review_substring_result_v5 (
  search_result_id, order_value, article_id
)
SELECT $search_result_id, bounded.order_value, bounded.article_id
FROM bounded_chunk AS bounded
INNER JOIN mart.review_title_fact_v5 AS fact
  ON fact.title_fact_id = bounded.title_fact_id
WHERE strpos(fact.normalized_title, $normalized_substring) > 0
ON CONFLICT (search_result_id, order_value, article_id) DO NOTHING;
~~~

`DO NOTHING` is valid only after the immutable request/fact/order identity and
conflict predicate prove the duplicate identical. A differing order or source
fact is a terminal conflict. Chunk checksum, final result checksum, result
visibility, polling termination and cleanup remain separate receipts.

Queue eligibility uses one stable membership key; priority/activity are values
validated in the complete checksum rather than physical identity. The
representative source CTE is bounded by an immutable article chunk and embeds
the approved LLM/Human rules rather than reading current rows later.

~~~sql
INSERT INTO mart.review_queue_item_v5 (
  project_id, queue_revision_id, queue_kind, article_id, prompt_key,
  queue_identity, priority_bucket, activity_sort_at
)
SELECT
  $project_id, $queue_revision_id, source.queue_kind, source.article_id,
  source.prompt_key, source.queue_identity, source.priority_bucket,
  source.activity_sort_at
FROM bounded_exact_queue_source AS source
WHERE source.eligible = TRUE
  AND source.article_id > $chunk_start_article_id
  AND source.article_id <= $chunk_end_article_id
ON CONFLICT (
  project_id, queue_revision_id, queue_kind, article_id, prompt_key,
  queue_identity
) DO UPDATE SET
  priority_bucket = excluded.priority_bucket,
  activity_sort_at = excluded.activity_sort_at;
~~~

Pair pagination binds the full registered tuple. All fields are nonnull and
the cursor is rejected when queue revision, filter or order version changes.

~~~sql
SELECT article_id, prompt_key, queue_identity,
       priority_bucket, activity_sort_at
FROM mart.review_queue_item_v5
WHERE project_id = $project_id
  AND queue_revision_id = $queue_revision_id
  AND queue_kind = $queue_kind
  AND (
    $cursor_is_start
    OR (priority_bucket, activity_sort_at, article_id, prompt_key,
        queue_identity) <
       ($cursor_priority, $cursor_activity, $cursor_article_id,
        $cursor_prompt_key, $cursor_queue_identity)
  )
ORDER BY priority_bucket DESC, activity_sort_at DESC, article_id DESC,
         prompt_key DESC, queue_identity DESC
LIMIT $limit_plus_one;
~~~

Article access is a separately sealed reduction. Mounted pages join its
existence to the candidate component and preserve candidate order; preview
uses only the article summary's named priority order.

~~~sql
INSERT INTO mart.review_queue_article_v5 (
  project_id, queue_revision_id, queue_kind, article_id,
  eligible_pair_count, max_priority_bucket, max_priority_activity_sort_at
)
SELECT project_id, queue_revision_id, queue_kind, article_id,
       COUNT(*) AS eligible_pair_count,
       MAX(priority_bucket) AS max_priority_bucket,
       MAX(activity_sort_at) FILTER (
         WHERE priority_bucket = article_max_priority
       ) AS max_priority_activity_sort_at
FROM bounded_queue_item_with_article_max_priority
GROUP BY project_id, queue_revision_id, queue_kind, article_id;
~~~

No SQL block above authorizes a new table or index. Exact output also requires
the target receipts, byte/call/attempt counters, applied-plan proof and the
target-specific `PRF-####` row below.

### Exact Queue Grains And Semantics

The proposed queue family preserves the currently distinct units instead of
normalizing them into one convenient count or order. The registered pair
contract is the only contract that may call its order serving priority.
Human-first is an intake policy applied after a fetched serving window; SQLite
insertion and claim/execution snapshots remain downstream durability and
execution contracts.

| Operation | Exact eligibility and unit | Exact priority/order | Cursor and continuation | What it cannot prove or replace |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pair eligibility build | One approved LLM `unassessed` or Human `human-unreviewed` article/prompt/identity pair in sealed `TGT-0042`; eligibility includes exact scope, selected state, enabled prompt, mode, model/content, blank/delete/tombstone/summary and Covidence rules | Priority and activity are checksummed values, not membership-key fields | Immutable article build chunks; no read cursor | Does not prove article count, mounted candidate order, local insertion, claim or execution visibility |
| Registered pair page | One queue item from `TGT-0042`, at most 100 plus sentinel | `priority_bucket DESC, activity_sort_at DESC, article_id DESC, prompt_key DESC, queue_identity DESC` | Signed `TGT-0043` cursor carries queue/filter/order versions and all five values; continuation is explicit | Does not prove a distinct-article count or authorize a cursor that omits identity |
| Worker pair page | Same pair eligibility, at most 5,000 plus sentinel | Same full five-value tuple; changing precision or tie-break is a new contract | One page per call; worker durably persists the full continuation before another call | Does not authorize read-all recursion, all-ID materialization or advancing after an unreceipted page |
| Mounted Unassessed list | One `TGT-0024` candidate article whose sealed `TGT-0044` article row exists | Candidate component activity/article order, not queue priority | Existing candidate full-tuple cursor; queue/candidate revisions are both bound | Queue existence does not reorder the mounted page or turn pair count into displayed count |
| Named queue counts | Explicit `eligible_pair_count` and distinct `eligible_article_count` from the same sealed revision | No order | One signed summary result or typed unavailable | Neither count substitutes for the other, preview rows, list envelope count or client-rendered total |
| Queue preview | One `TGT-0044` article summary, at most 500 plus sentinel | `max_priority_bucket DESC, max_priority_activity_sort_at DESC, article_id DESC` | Full three-value preview cursor if continuation is exposed | Grouped maximums cannot recreate individual prompt eligibility or pair execution order |
| Intake selection window | Up to 128 fetched `TGT-0043` pairs plus lookahead under `TGT-0045` | Serving tuple is fetched first; versioned Human-first partition may order only the accepted intake set | Receipt binds cursor in/out and fetched/rejected/inserted counts; next window is explicit | Human-first is not serving priority; fetched, accepted and inserted progress are not equal |
| Local ready insertion | One durable SQLite row accepted under the existing central/local uniqueness and job rules | Durable insertion order is local queue state | Existing local row/key and ACK, cross-referenced by selection receipt | Does not prove the row was claimed, executed, imported or made visible |
| Claim/execution | One accepted claim plus immutable execution snapshot | Claim policy and execution bindings are independently versioned | Existing claim/ACK/retry state; no serving cursor reuse | Does not prove canonical import, visibility ACK, terminal cleanup or serving-priority parity |

An article with 512 eligible prompts can therefore consume 512 pair rows, one
article summary row and one candidate article row. Each number, byte total and
checksum is reported separately. A source cursor that advances over rejected
rows is valid only when `TGT-0045` accounts those rows and preserves the exact
next serving cursor; it is never insertion progress.

### Writes, Ownership, Invalidation And Failure

Let `A` be source articles, `P` admitted unique project-token rows, `F` new
immutable title facts, `G` global fact-token rows, `B` project bindings, `Q`
eligible prompt pairs, `U` eligible queue articles, `C` async substring chunks,
`R` substring results and `W` intake windows. These symbols describe logical
write amplification; physical bytes, compression, index pages, WAL/temp and
write latency remain unavailable until measured.

| Target | Candidate writes and indexes | Exact invalidation boundary | Publication/failure behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TGT-0039` | `A` project article rows, `P` project-token rows, revision/chunk/final receipts and token/article plus article-key indexes; the same selected title can be repeated for every project | Project scope, selected-import/title winner, normalized title bytes, tokenizer/collation/prefix-bound version and any approved diagnostic field | Build immutable revision, validate every chunk and complete checksum, then promote. Any overrun/parity/conflict failure leaves candidate failed and active/LKG unchanged; no current-title join |
| `TGT-0040` | Up to `F` title facts, `G` global tokens, `B` project bindings, two lookup indexes and separate global/project receipts; reuse is a benefit only when measured `F`/`G` is lower than repeated `P` | Fact content/tokenizer changes create a new fact; project scope or selected-title winner changes a project binding revision. Fact retention waits for every project/result/export/reference | Fact publication and project binding publication are separately atomic and validated. Collision, byte mismatch, missing fact or over-broad prefix fails; project-specific target remains an explicit alternative, not silent fallback |
| `TGT-0041` | One request, at most 125 chunk rows, up to 50,000 result rows, result-order index and chunk/final/visibility/cleanup receipts | Query normalization, filter/order/candidate/search/title-fact revision or executor version change creates a new request/result identity | Pending, running, retryable-failed, terminal-failed, ready, expired and cleaned remain distinct. Only complete final receipt plus visibility gate exposes ready; completed-chunk finalization can be readmitted explicitly |
| `TGT-0042` | `Q` immutable pair rows, revision/chunk/final receipts and stable membership plus full-order indexes; priority changes are new revision values, not delete/reinsert key churn | Project scope, selected import, review config, prompts, Human mode, model/content, LLM/Human answer/delete/blank/tombstone/summary/Covidence policy or source revisions | Dirty and full builds must converge on identical complete output. Zero dirty fan-out still records source reconciliation; later membership requires replay. Candidate failure preserves active/LKG and does not ACK/publish partial rows |
| `TGT-0043` | Logical ordered access over `TGT-0042`; physical cost is the full five-value index plus signed cursor bytes | Any priority/activity precision, direction, tie-break, filter or queue revision change invalidates the cursor | Null/missing field, equal-key ambiguity, explicit sort/spill, row/byte/time/attempt cap or cursor mismatch is unavailable, not a weaker order |
| `TGT-0044` | `U` article summary rows, one preview index, reduction chunk/final receipts and exact pair/article count/checksum | Any pair membership, priority or activity change in the source queue revision; candidate-order changes invalidate mounted binding but not the sealed queue article facts | Publish only against the exact pair revision. Missing/conflicting reduction row fails the article component; mounted and preview paths name which revision is unavailable rather than grouping current pairs |
| `TGT-0045` | One selection epoch, `W` bounded page receipts and local ACK references; at the proposed 10-million-pair maximum, no more than 78,125 receipts and never an ID array | Job criteria, queue/candidate/config revision, pair-order/intake-policy version, execution-config identity or starting cursor | Persist page receipt and local ACK before cursor advance. Drift, gap, ACK/checksum/count mismatch or attempt cap stops the epoch; retry is idempotent for the same window and never switches model/content/thinking/provider |

Search and queue invalidation are not interchangeable. A selected-title change
can invalidate `TGT-0039`/`TGT-0040` without changing prompt eligibility. A
Human answer, model/content configuration or queue policy change can invalidate
`TGT-0042` without changing title tokens. Candidate, search, queue, substring
result, intake and execution revisions remain independently named in every
join, cursor and receipt.

### Required Indexes And Applied-Plan Consequences

These indexes are target hypotheses. Checked-in DDL, a successful checksum or
an index name cannot prove that an applied database has the index or that the
optimizer uses a bounded plan.

| Target access | Proposed logical index | Required applied-plan proof and rejection condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Project prefix anchor/membership | `(project_id,search_revision_id,token,article_id)` plus `(project_id,search_revision_id,article_id,token)` | Range seek touches at most 50,001 raw rows; point membership stays under one million probes; no full token/table scan, external sort, spill or post-limit candidate work |
| Global prefix and fact lookup | `(tokenizer_version,token,title_fact_id)` plus fact PK | Global range seek hits the 100,001 sentinel before project join. If a broad prefix cannot be bounded, return async/unavailable rather than rely on a small project filter |
| Project fact binding | `(project_id,search_revision_id,title_fact_id,article_id)` plus binding PK `(project_id,search_revision_id,article_id)` | Prefix-to-project intersection and candidate binding use bounded index lookups; no current-title hydration or cross-project scan |
| Substring scheduler/result | Request `(status,next_attempt_at,search_result_id)`, chunks `(search_result_id,status,chunk_ordinal)` and result `(search_result_id,order_value DESC,article_id DESC)` | Claim one bounded chunk, strict source keyset, idempotent result insert and bounded ordered page; no one-shot project scan, recursive drain or result sort above caps |
| Queue membership/pair order | Membership PK from `TGT-0042` and `(project_id,queue_revision_id,queue_kind,priority_bucket DESC,activity_sort_at DESC,article_id DESC,prompt_key DESC,queue_identity DESC)` | Full-tuple keyset seek returns limit plus sentinel with no sort/spill; equal priority/activity/article/prompt rows advance by queue identity |
| Queue article existence/preview | PK `(project_id,queue_revision_id,queue_kind,article_id)` and preview tuple `(project_id,queue_revision_id,queue_kind,max_priority_bucket DESC,max_priority_activity_sort_at DESC,article_id DESC)` | Mounted existence is a point probe before candidate limit semantics; preview is a bounded keyset seek; neither scans/group-bys pair rows at request time |
| Selection epoch/pages | Scheduler/status index on selection state and unique page/cursor-in identity | One due epoch and one explicit page are claimed; retry finds the identical window receipt. It never reads every page or stores all selected IDs in one row |

Validation must capture normalized and raw `EXPLAIN`/profiler output on the
approved immutable fixture for every minimum, boundary, sentinel, equal-key,
null, broad-prefix and persistent-failure case. It must separately report rows
read, rows emitted, point probes, statements, underlying adapter attempts,
sort/spill/temp/WAL bytes, latency and peak RSS. A `LIMIT` node alone is not a
bounded-plan receipt.

### Snapshot, Availability And Continuation Contracts

| Contract | Immutable identities that must be bound | Ready condition | Stale, unavailable and continuation behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Project token search | Project, search revision, selected-title/import, scope, tokenizer/collation/prefix-bound and candidate/filter/order revisions | Search and candidate receipts are complete and cursor signature matches | Missing/current mismatch is indexing or unavailable. LKG use, if approved, names its old revisions; continuation carries the candidate cursor, never a token row offset |
| Global token search | Global fact/tokenizer revision plus exact project binding/search and candidate revisions | Both global fact and project binding receipts validate, bounded prefix admission passes | Missing fact or binding is unavailable; it cannot join a newer current title or borrow another project. Broad prefix may route only to the explicit async contract |
| Async substring | Query signature, project, candidate/order, search/binding/title-fact, filter and executor versions | All chunks complete, final count/checksum passes and a separate visibility receipt exposes the immutable result | Pending/running/retryable-failed/terminal-failed/expired/cleaned are explicit. Client polls one status result at a time with bounded backoff and stops at a declared terminal state |
| Queue pair/article | Project, queue kind/revision, scope, selected import, config/prompt/mode/model/content and LLM/Human source revisions; article receipt names pair revision | Pair and article components are complete and route binds the intended candidate revision/order | Partial pair/article revisions never mix. Approved LKG is labelled; missing current revision is indexing/unavailable, not an empty queue or current-row regroup |
| Pair/preview cursor | Contract/filter/order version, direction, queue revision and every order value | Exact signature and all values decode and compare under registered types/precision | Any mismatch rejects the cursor. A sentinel yields one explicit next cursor; server/client recursion is forbidden |
| Selection/intake | Selection/job criteria, queue/candidate/config, serving order, intake-policy and execution-config identities | Current page receipt, local insertion ACK and cursor chain reconcile | Drift stops the epoch. Continuation names next page and exact cursor; later claim/execution/import/visibility statuses remain separate |

The selected-import snapshot ID, serving snapshot ID, review-config hash,
project scope identity and source watermarks remain distinct. None may be
compressed into a generic `snapshot_id`. Search/queue component completion and
promotion also remain separate transactions; a failure after all build chunks
complete needs an explicit finalization-repair admission path.

### Retention, Replay, Recovery And Cleanup

| Lifecycle domain | Required target contract |
| --- | --- |
| Retention/reference scan | Protect active, LKG and candidate revisions; every API cursor, substring request/result, selection epoch, local ACK, export/bulk job, pin, repair state and concurrent-reader lease; enumerate global-title fact references separately from project bindings. A timestamp or status is not a lease fence. |
| Replay | Candidate chunks use immutable source ranges and natural identities. Identical retry is idempotent; conflicting duplicate fails. Dirty zero-fan-out source rows retain reconciliation evidence and are replayed if later scope/route membership changes. Completed-chunk finalization and visibility failure have explicit repair queues. |
| Clean-host recovery | Restore canonical sources/config, rebuild title facts/tokens and project bindings/search, rebuild queue pairs then article reductions, re-admit pending substring/selection work under original settings, reconcile local ACK/claim/import/visibility state and validate counts/checksums/routes before promotion. Backup existence or startup probe restoration is insufficient. |
| Bounded cleanup | One scheduled invocation deletes at most 4,096 rows and at most 64 MB across one rotating lifecycle grain, after an immutable reference scan and reader-lease check. Persist cursor, scanned/deleted/retained/error counts and before/after checksum receipt; resume explicitly. Delete final receipts only after every dependent row and artifact is gone. |
| Crash/concurrency | Candidate publication uses application temp/rename or database transaction semantics appropriate to each artifact, not an inferred application WAL. Claim/lease tokens survive process restart; expired work is repaired or failed by policy, never force-deleted while a reader or retry can reference it. |
| Orphans and terminal state | Cover failed/expired substring requests, chunks/results, abandoned search/queue candidates, selection epochs/pages, local ACK references, pins, cursors and global facts with zero references. Terminal job status, cleanup invocation and cleanup completion are three states. |

The current 512-row rotating final-table cleanup is useful source evidence but
does not meet this contract for proposed request/chunk/result/page/receipt rows,
ordinary-reader leases, cross-family references or full-cycle durable receipts.
No byte, duration, deletion-safety or clean-host restore claim is made.

### Migration, Backfill, Cutover And Rollback

1. Owners first freeze exact tokenizer/collation/prefix successor, title
   authority, queue eligibility/priority/activity precision, Human-first
   intake, named counts, cursor and availability semantics. Every unsupported
   or legacy null/open-domain case gets a typed decision.
2. Capture a non-live applied DuckDB/SQLite inventory and immutable workload
   snapshot, including effective migration order, rows/bytes/indexes, null and
   equal-key domains, source revisions, local queue/claim state and existing
   retention/recovery references. Never inspect a live DuckDB directly.
3. Create only approved candidate objects, versioned writers, leases and
   receipts. Backfill immutable article keyset chunks within the proposed caps;
   project-specific and global-token alternatives are measured separately and
   never run as silent fallback for one another.
4. Validate every chunk and final candidate with complete-field checksums,
   tokenizer parity, exact pair/article/count/order/cursor equality, zero
   gap/overlap, applied-plan bounds and structural/data write amplification.
   Preserve source/current tables and active/LKG targets.
5. Run the fixed benchmark plus real browser-path and packaged-desktop
   hash/outer-window/loopback captures at below, boundary, sentinel, over-cap,
   equal-key, null, stale, restart and persistent-failure cases. Missing
   benchmark-critical values remain blockers; no resolver defaults.
6. Cut over one writer first, reconcile current/candidate state, then one reader
   contract at a time. Search, substring, mounted queue, registered pair,
   preview/count, intake and local claim/execution each have independent feature
   gates and rollback to the validated prior active/LKG revision.
7. Observe bounded replay, finalization repair, retention/reference scans,
   clean-host restore and platform parity for an owner-approved window. A local
   success or 2xx status does not waive result visibility or terminal cleanup.
8. Only then archive/delete old project tokens, substring control rows,
   physical queue patch/time columns or old indexes using their existing
   blocked dispositions. Record history mapping, final reference scan, recovery
   copy/manifest, bounded deletion receipts and later validation. Rollback stays
   possible until those proofs pass.

No step above is authorized by this story. In particular, the migration-only
queue patch family cannot be called retired merely because current writes
target the active queue; deployed shape, old tokens/barriers, history,
retention and recovery references must be proven independently.

### Browser And Desktop Consequences

| Flow | Browser requirement | Packaged-desktop requirement | Required evidence before proof |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Token search submit/page/back-forward | Preserve path URL query, TanStack key, exact candidate order/count/select-all filter signature and signed cursor; indexing/unavailable is visible | Preserve `views:` hash route, inner query and outer window state through the loopback bridge; no hook may discard the hash or read only outer `location.search` | Exact request order/count/body, cache key/reuse, history state, cursor/page rendering and response fields in real browser and packaged desktop captures |
| Async substring | Submit one bounded job, show pending/progress/failed/ready/expired, poll with finite backoff/timeout and stop; result page names immutable revision | Same state machine across restart/offline/reconnect and desktop executor availability; no hidden browser-only fallback | Executor registration, job/result visibility, poll count/interval/termination, cancel/retry identity, restart and stale-result captures |
| Mounted Unassessed list | Keep candidate activity order and displayed article total while queue existence filters membership; do not expose pair count as article count | Same route, cache and cursor semantics under hash history and loopback origin | All four list modes where applicable, empty/nonempty/equal-key pages, deduplication, navigation and current-versus-LKG labels |
| Queue preview/count/intake | Name article versus pair totals and preview priority; selection criteria persist exact queue/candidate/config revisions | Desktop job status reports fetched/rejected/inserted/claimed/executed/imported/visible/cleaned separately | Actual API/client field lineage, select-all job criteria, page receipts, status transitions and restart behavior; synthetic adapter/DOM tests are supporting only |

The current client does not render queue priority, prompt/identity or substring
progress. This story does not invent UI exposure. Product owners must approve
whether those fields remain internal, receive a named diagnostic surface or
make async substring unsupported. Source inspection cannot certify browser
request frequency, cache behavior, navigation or desktop parity.

### Rejected Search And Queue Shapes

- Reject foreground project/title scans, `%substring%`, per-candidate current
  JSON/full-text hydration, unbounded global-prefix joins and any `LIMIT` used
  as evidence that the underlying scan/sort/probe is bounded.
- Reject loading every matching article/pair ID into memory, JSON, SQL arrays,
  one manifest or recursive read-all loops. Every page/chunk has row, byte,
  statement, physical-attempt and request/revision caps plus explicit durable
  continuation.
- Reject global tokens keyed only by canonical article ID. Reuse requires an
  immutable normalized-title fact and an exact project-selected-title binding;
  a current-table join would make old search results mutable.
- Reject exposing partial substring chunks as ready, treating a pending/job
  status as result visibility, retrying after settings drift, adopting default
  provider/model/thinking/content, or using missing executor as permission for
  a synchronous scan.
- Reject mutable priority/activity as queue membership identity, nullable or
  omitted final tie-breaks, activity precision changes, strict keyset cursors
  that skip equal keys, and checksum success that omits an order field.
- Reject relabelling Human-first partition, SQLite insertion order or claim
  policy as serving priority. Preserve rejected/fetched/inserted/claimed/
  executed/imported/visible/cleaned states separately.
- Reject pair/article/count/preview/list-total substitution, read-time grouping
  over an unbounded pair set, or using mounted queue existence to change the
  candidate component's order.
- Reject inferring cleanup from `finally`, expiry, status or a scheduled call;
  deletion needs reference/lease scan, bounded receipt, crash replay and restore
  validation. Reject conceptual storage savings without encoded table/index/
  WAL/temp bytes and write/read resource measurements.
- Reject one family `proofCheckState`, checksum, snapshot ID or promotion as
  proof for all seven targets. Each target below has independent owner,
  applied-shape, bound, lifecycle, platform and benchmark obligations.

## US-097 Manifest And Control Target Shapes

US-096 is complete and remains the prerequisite. This story designs bounded
publication and lifecycle alternatives for the identity, selected-import,
serving-snapshot, pin, delta/frontier, dirty-work, watermark, rebuild, overlay,
judgment-job, maintenance, bulk-job and retention families classified in
US-075/US-076 and proved by US-083 through US-085. `TGT-0041` remains the sole
asynchronous-substring target and `TGT-0045` remains the queue-intake receipt;
US-097 cross-references those contracts without claiming a second target.

The designs below are grouped by component owner, publication boundary and
recovery need. They are not schema approval, an applied migration, measured
savings, owner authority or permission to alter routes, writers, projectors,
retention, files or data. Scoped `src`, `scripts` and `package.json` source is
unchanged from the US-083 control baseline `048ec5f5` through HEAD
`cd197355`. Effective checked-in shape was derived from the complete lexical
migration chain, including the final projector-watermark rebuild and index
drop. No live/current DuckDB or SQLite file, configured snapshot, fixture,
server, app, worker, projector, migration, repair, browser or packaged desktop
process was opened or run.

`auditStatus`, `proofCheckState`, `recommendationActionability` and
`overallCertification` remain independent. Every new target proof is
`proofCheckState: blocked`. The 73 linked keep grains remain
`recommendationActionability: unresolved`; the two linked dormant project-
cursor delete grains remain `recommendationActionability: blocked`; no
disposition, existing proof or certification state changes. DBO, CMF, FAN and
the 441-row disposition register are not recounted.

### Current Contract Versus Bounded Alternatives

| Grain | Current checked-in behavior | Exact bounded alternative | Consequence and explicit failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Component identity/input | One semantic manifest ID is updated with generation, patch, scalar/map input and status. Snapshot composition copies the row's current state. | `TGT-0046` writes a content-addressed immutable revision plus closed per-partition input rows and a seal receipt. | Later updates create another revision. Unknown partitions, over-cap inputs, digest/count mismatch or an unsealed revision block composition; no mutable-row reuse. |
| Selected-import publication | Header/cursor/base and projection manifest can be updated/reused under a selected snapshot ID. | `TGT-0047` separates resumable build attempt from immutable sealed header/base revision and exact count/checksum. | Interrupted builds resume by attempt cursor; reset creates a new revision. Missing/extra winners or unsealed base is unavailable, never partially active. |
| Serving active/LKG | Candidate JSON copies are validated, current active rows are retired and the candidate is activated transactionally, without a relational component/FK/single-active fence. | `TGT-0048` stores relational component references and changes one `(active_snapshot_id,lkg_snapshot_id,head_epoch)` row by compare-and-swap. | Readers resolve one head epoch. CAS loss, missing seal/reference, cross-config mismatch or validation failure retains prior active/LKG and records failed candidate. |
| Pin/reader lease | Owner-hashed ref-count rows protect cleanup; bulk acquisition precedes job insertion and ordinary readers do not lease. | `TGT-0049` uses one owner-generation lease per admitted use, atomic job binding/compensation and finite terminal settlement receipts. | Active-lease cap overflow blocks admission rather than evicting references. Stale generation cannot renew/release; cleanup requires zero live leases and a reference scan. |
| Source intake/frontier | Allocation, delta, optional outbox, `reconciled_at`, dirty fan-out and schema-only project cursor are separate and can stop before later membership/publication. | `TGT-0050` stores immutable partition events and separate contiguous allocation, persisted, reconciled, dirty-admitted and visible frontiers with gap receipts. | Zero fan-out remains explicit and can be replayed on membership revision. Gaps, unknown payload/version or over-cap lag quarantine the lane; a mutable cursor cannot authorize prune. |
| Dirty work/ACK | Coalesced rows claim by status/time without owner token; ACK precedes status completion; compaction identity includes threshold. | `TGT-0051` adds owner token/generation/lease, immutable attempt/output receipt and one lane checkpoint whose identity excludes the advancing value. | Only owner-CAS completion can ACK/advance. Stale owner, output mismatch, failed publication or missing visibility leaves work retryable/quarantined and cannot suppress replay. |
| Consumer watermark | Projector row, manifest scalar/map and snapshot copy use different identities; process-local locking guards an unkeyed table. | `TGT-0052` records separate event, dirty, sealed-output and snapshot-visible values per registered consumer lane and signs the monotonic transition chain. | Freshness/pruning uses only an owner-approved visible minimum. Alias drift, duplicate lane, regression or missing receipt blocks advance; values are never merged by `any_value`. |
| Rebuild request/chunk/finalize | Request/chunks have budgets and chunk leases; all-complete derived reduction/promotion is a later sequence with no independent finalization claim. | `TGT-0053` keeps immutable plan, chunk attempt/output, request finalization claim and promotion receipt as separate versioned rows. | Completed chunks remain reusable while finalization retries under its own lease. Attempt/depth/budget exhaustion is terminal/quarantined; active/LKG remains unchanged. |
| Write overlay | Deterministic pending rows expire after five minutes; reads are uncapped and reconcile/expire helpers lack an operating sweep. | `TGT-0054` stores immutable overlay event, bounded article/surface index and exact source-visible receipt; reconciliation and physical cleanup are separate. | More than the approved row/byte cap is unavailable, not truncated. Expiry removes read eligibility only; cleanup waits for visibility/reference/lease proof. |
| Judgment execution job | Central job, per-file scan/queue/claim/snapshot/outboxes/ACKs, import marker, visibility and token closeout use separate current contracts. | `TGT-0055` retains each grain under one immutable job/selection/execution identity and a finite receipt chain; it references `TGT-0045` intake. | Local terminal or owner ACK cannot mark canonical visibility. Config drift, missing receipt or retry exhaustion preserves failure and active evidence; no all-ID job JSON. |
| Maintenance/control runs | Maintenance/provider leases, health, closeout/backfill, delete intent and telemetry have different owners and horizons. | `TGT-0056` uses a versioned work-kind registry, fenced run/step receipts, current-only health projection and separately typed provider/closeout/delete evidence. | No generic status or timestamp implies completion. Unknown work kind, stale owner, incomplete closeout or history-cap overflow blocks the lane; three-day telemetry remains a separate source contract. |
| Bulk job/result | Criteria/job ID is deterministic; stale `updated_at` reclaims running jobs, progress/result is mutable JSON and terminal state does not settle pin/artifact. | `TGT-0057` freezes criteria/selection revision, owner-CAS claims, per-batch side-effect/result receipts, typed final manifest and delivery/pin settlement. | Existing 5,000-ID/1 MB/500-row/three-attempt limits are hard ceilings pending owner validation. A claim loss, checksum/count/artifact mismatch or delivery lease blocks terminal publication. |
| Retention cycle | One mark rotates a table index across 11 data tables, deletes 512 rows and updates `last_cleaned_at`; controls and complete-cycle evidence are omitted. | `TGT-0058` stores versioned policy/registry, owner lease, cycle, per-target eligibility/delete receipt, orphan decision and complete-cycle checksum. | Maximum 512 deletes/step and 16 targets/cycle with explicit continuation. Unknown references, policy drift, lease loss, receipt failure or incomplete restore leaves the cycle failed/resumable, never "clean". |

### US-097 Target Shape Register

Every `v5` object below is proposed only. `MAX_*` denotes a mandatory finite,
versioned owner-approved value; there is no implicit default. If a policy value
is missing or a cap is reached, admission/publication/cleanup returns typed
`unavailable`, `blocked` or `quarantined` state and preserves current active/LKG
or referenced data.

| targetId | Target and linked disposition grains | Exact proposed shape | Owner, source, invalidation and failure | Evidence / proof |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TGT-0046` | Immutable component revision and closed input vector; `DSP-0098`, `DSP-0127`, `DSP-0131`, `DSP-0140` | `app.review_component_revision_v5` PK `component_revision_id=sha256(canonical immutable fields)` stores project/component/projection identity, definition/config/prompt hashes, generation/patch range, source-vector digest, output count/bytes/checksum, `building/sealed/failed`, seal/failure receipt and times. `app.review_component_revision_source_v5` PK `(component_revision_id,source_partition_key)` stores closed registry version and high water; at most 11 components/snapshot and `MAX_SOURCE_PARTITIONS_PER_REVISION`. Sealed rows are append-only. | Each component writer owns its revision; source/config/delta change creates a new ID. Writer retries the same ID idempotently and cannot overwrite a seal. Unknown lane, cap/digest/output mismatch or failure records a failed attempt and blocks snapshot composition. | `EVD-1147`-`EVD-1148`, `EVD-1150`, `EVD-1157`-`EVD-1159`; `PRF-0957` |
| `TGT-0047` | Immutable selected-import build/header/base; `DSP-0132`-`DSP-0133`, `DSP-0141`-`DSP-0142` | `app.review_selected_import_build_v5` PK `build_id` stores immutable scope/source/order policy, owner generation, lease, cursor, attempt/count/byte caps and status. `app.review_selected_import_revision_v5` PK `selected_revision_id` stores sealed build ID, expected/actual winner count, checksum and source vector. Base PK `(selected_revision_id,article_id)` stores winner/rank/display/conflict/tombstone; 512+1 keyset rows/build step, no ID array. | Selected-import projector owns build and seal; source/scope/rank change starts another build. Page retry is idempotent on `(build_id,page_ordinal,cursor_in)`. Missing page, overlap/gap, duplicate winner, checksum/count/cap or lease failure never publishes a partial revision. | `EVD-1147`-`EVD-1148`, `EVD-1155`-`EVD-1159`; `PRF-0958` |
| `TGT-0048` | Relational immutable serving snapshot plus active/LKG head; `DSP-0134`-`DSP-0135`, `DSP-0143` | `app.review_serving_snapshot_v5` PK `(project_id,snapshot_id)` stores config/composed/selected revision, source digest, validation and immutable candidate outcome. Component PK `(project_id,snapshot_id,component,requirement)` references one sealed `TGT-0046` revision, maximum 11. `app.review_serving_snapshot_head_v5` PK `(project_id,review_config_hash_key)` stores exactly `active_snapshot_id`, nullable `lkg_snapshot_id`, `head_epoch`. | Promotion owner validates all references/counts/checksums then CAS-updates one head; failed candidate is append-only. A reader fetches one head epoch and exact snapshot. Missing/unsealed refs, config mismatch or CAS loss retains active/LKG and returns retryable/unavailable without mixed composition. | `EVD-1147`-`EVD-1149`, `EVD-1155`-`EVD-1159`; `PRF-0959` |
| `TGT-0049` | Owner-generation snapshot and reader lease; `DSP-0136`, `DSP-0144` | `app.review_snapshot_lease_v5` PK `lease_id=sha256(project,snapshot,composed,owner_kind,owner_id,owner_generation)` stores heartbeat/expiry/release and bound job/read transaction. Terminal `app.review_snapshot_lease_receipt_v5` records release/expiry/compensation reason and reference scan. `MAX_ACTIVE_LEASES_PER_PROJECT` is enforced before admission. | Bulk/job/export or approved long reader owns acquisition/renew/release. Job plus lease inserts in one transaction, or a compensation receipt reverses acquisition. Only matching generation CAS renews/releases. Overflow, missing owner, expired use or orphan mismatch blocks work; cleanup never evicts a live reference. | `EVD-1149`, `EVD-1154`-`EVD-1159`; `PRF-0960` |
| `TGT-0050` | Immutable source event and typed consumer-frontier intake; `DSP-0090`-`DSP-0093`, `DSP-0096`, `DSP-0120`-`DSP-0122`, `DSP-0125` | `app.review_source_event_v5` PK `(source_partition,event_sequence)` plus unique idempotency key stores typed operation/key/payload version/digest and source time. `app.review_source_frontier_v5` PK `(source_partition,frontier_version)` stores allocated, persisted, reconciled, dirty-admitted and visible-through values separately; event-attempt/quarantine and zero-fan-out/late-membership receipts are append-only and finite. Dormant project-cursor rows map or retire here only after proof. | Source writers own atomic allocation+event; intake owns reconciliation/dirty receipts; publication owns visible frontier. Same source mutation reuses identity. Gap, duplicate conflict, open payload, no approved membership replay, lag/cap or exhausted attempt quarantines without advancing later grains. | `EVD-1147`, `EVD-1150`, `EVD-1155`-`EVD-1159`; `PRF-0961` |

A closed alias registry maps source names; monotonic CAS and unique lane constraints are mandatory. | Publication owner advances only after all referenced receipts exist in one transaction. ### Mandatory Bounds And Continuation

These are design ceilings, not measured-safe or owner-approved values. The
current-aligned numbers below may only become authoritative after the exact
later proof passes. Every `MAX_*` is a finite positive policy value stored with
the revision that used it; null, missing, changed or exceeded values fail
closed. A 512-row page never implies a bounded request unless pages, calls,
encoded bytes, underlying attempts and termination are also capped.

| Target slice | Per operation ceiling | Request, revision or lifecycle ceiling | Continuation and overflow behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TGT-0046` component revision | At most 11 registered component references and `MAX_SOURCE_PARTITIONS_PER_REVISION`; 512 source/control rows and 2 MiB encoded control data/call | `MAX_BUILD_PAGES`, `MAX_COMPONENT_REVISIONS_PER_SCOPE`, three identical-input physical attempts and five seconds/statement | Explicit build cursor or new revision. Unknown/open lane, over-cap vector, byte/call/attempt/time excess or missing seal is unavailable; no partial component copy. |
| `TGT-0047` selected import | 512 winner candidates plus one sentinel/build page; 2 MiB control/receipt bytes | `MAX_SELECTED_ROWS`, `MAX_BUILD_PAGES`, `MAX_BUILD_BYTES`, three attempts/page | Persist page receipt/cursor then continue explicitly. Sentinel proves more work only; cap stops build before seal and retains prior active/LKG. |
| `TGT-0048` snapshot publication | At most 11 component rows and one selected revision; one head CAS/transaction | `MAX_CANDIDATES_PER_SCOPE` and finite failed/retired histories; one active and at most one LKG per project/config head | CAS loser or invalid candidate records failure/retry; it never mutates the active head, auto-promotes a subset or scans historical manifests. |
| `TGT-0049` leases | Point acquire/renew/release; 512 reference rows/page | `MAX_ACTIVE_LEASES_PER_PROJECT`, `MAX_LEASE_RENEWALS`, finite maximum duration and terminal receipt horizon | Admission stops before the cap. Reference scan uses an explicit cursor; no expiry extension without owner generation and no eviction to make room. |
| `TGT-0050` source events | 512 events plus sentinel/partition page; 2 MiB payload+receipt bytes | `MAX_EVENT_LAG`, `MAX_PARTITION_PAGES_PER_RUN`, three attempts/event; finite quarantined/event history | Continue by `(partition,event_sequence)`. Gap/conflict/open payload or lag cap quarantines/stops; no skip to a later high water and no recursive read-all. |
| `TGT-0051` dirty work | At most 64 claims/one lane and 512 rows/wake; 2 MiB output receipts, 120-second proposed lease | Three attempts/work item, five seconds/wake, `MAX_PENDING_WORK_PER_LANE` | Explicit next lane/cursor. Claim/lease/attempt/pending cap or output mismatch fails/quarantines without ACK/checkpoint advance. |
| `TGT-0052` consumer frontier | Point lane read/CAS and at most 512 receipt validations/page | At most the closed source-lane registry per component revision; three CAS attempts | Resume exact receipt page. Missing prior grain, alias/version drift or CAS conflict blocks visibility; no maximum/`any_value` merge across duplicate lanes. |
| `TGT-0053` rebuild | One chunk/batch, 512 control rows/page, default-aligned three attempts/60-second backoff/120-second lease and split depth below 12 | `MAX_CHUNKS_PER_REQUEST`, `MAX_FINALIZATION_ATTEMPTS`, stored input/output/payload/temp/byte budgets | Keyset/split continuation is explicit; finalization remains claimable after all chunks complete. Budget/depth/attempt excess is terminal, never an uncapped split/retry or partial promotion. |
| `TGT-0054` overlay | Maximum 4,096 payload bytes and `MAX_ACTIVE_OVERLAYS_PER_ARTICLE`/`MAX_OVERLAY_BYTES_PER_READ`; 512 cleanup rows | Five-minute current-compatible eligibility only after approval; finite pending/reconciled/expired row caps/horizons | Over-cap read is unavailable, not truncated. Reconciliation uses visibility receipt; expiry changes eligibility and cleanup continues by keyset. |
| `TGT-0055` judgment execution | `TGT-0045` 128-row intake page; typed point/batch receipts and 512 terminal cleanup rows | `MAX_ACTIVE_ROWS_PER_JOB`, `MAX_SELECTION_PAGES`, finite attempts/status horizons and explicit file-byte cap from later file target | Next intake/result/import/visibility page is explicit. Config/receipt/file/cap mismatch stops same settings; no all-ID materialization or recursive queue drain. |
| `TGT-0056` maintenance | At most 64 claimed runs, 512 step rows and 2 MiB diagnostics/receipt bytes | Three attempts/step unless a stricter typed policy applies; `MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS_PER_KIND`, finite terminal/error history; telemetry retains the separate three-day source ceiling | Continue by work-kind/scope/run/step cursor. Unknown kind, open payload, lease loss or cap excess blocks/quarantines; health counters cannot advance cleanup. |
| `TGT-0057` bulk | Existing proposed hard ceilings: 5,000 explicit IDs, 1 MiB criteria, 500 rows/batch plus sentinel, three attempts | `MAX_BATCHES_PER_JOB`, `MAX_RESULT_BYTES`, finite delivery/pin/job/artifact horizon | Persist batch and side-effect receipt before cursor advance. New explicit job/continuation is required at a request cap; no dynamic all-ID result map. |
| `TGT-0058` retention | At most 512 scanned/deleted rows/step and 16 registered targets/cycle | `MAX_STEPS_PER_CYCLE`, three owner-CAS attempts/step, finite cycle/failure/orphan receipt horizon | Persist exact step cursor/receipt; continue with another bounded cycle segment. Policy/reference/lease/restore mismatch stops before unsafe delete and cannot label the cycle complete. |

All target scopes must additionally enforce a request-wide encoded-byte budget,
database-call budget, physical-attempt budget and explicit maximum page/step
count. Reaching a terminal history cap blocks new non-recovery admission until
approved cleanup or cold archival completes; it never causes silent eviction
or indefinite hot growth.

### Representative Target Reads And Writes

The SQL below is illustrative design text. It was not executed and is not
applied-plan proof. Table names, constraints, isolation and caps remain subject
to target-specific validation.

```sql
-- TGT-0046/TGT-0048: compose only sealed immutable revisions, then CAS one head.
BEGIN;
SELECT head_epoch, active_snapshot_id
FROM app.review_serving_snapshot_head_v5
WHERE project_id = ? AND review_config_hash_key = ?;

SELECT component, component_revision_id, output_count, output_checksum
FROM app.review_serving_snapshot_component_v5
JOIN app.review_component_revision_v5 USING (component_revision_id)
WHERE project_id = ? AND snapshot_id = ? AND revision_status = 'sealed'
ORDER BY component
LIMIT 12; -- eleven registered components plus an overflow sentinel

UPDATE app.review_serving_snapshot_head_v5
SET lkg_snapshot_id = active_snapshot_id,
    active_snapshot_id = ?,
    head_epoch = head_epoch + 1
WHERE project_id = ? AND review_config_hash_key = ? AND head_epoch = ?;
-- Require exactly one updated head and insert the publication receipt in this transaction.
COMMIT;
```

```sql
-- TGT-0051/TGT-0052: claim by owner generation; completion binds output and visible frontier.
UPDATE app.review_dirty_work_v5
SET status = 'running', owner_token = ?, owner_generation = ?, lease_expires_at = ?, attempt_no = attempt_no + 1
WHERE work_id IN (
  SELECT work_id
  FROM app.review_dirty_work_v5
  WHERE lane_id = ? AND (status = 'pending' OR lease_expires_at <= ?)
  ORDER BY source_high_water, work_id
  LIMIT 64
)
AND (status = 'pending' OR lease_expires_at <= ?)
RETURNING work_id, source_high_water, attempt_no;

UPDATE app.review_dirty_ack_lane_v5
SET completed_through = ?, output_receipt_id = ?, lane_epoch = lane_epoch + 1
WHERE lane_id = ? AND lane_epoch = ? AND completed_through <= ?;
-- The transaction also verifies the sealed component/output receipt; visibility advances later.
```

```sql
-- TGT-0053: finalization is independently claimable after every chunk is sealed.
UPDATE app.review_rebuild_finalization_v5
SET status = 'running', owner_token = ?, owner_generation = ?, lease_expires_at = ?, attempt_no = attempt_no + 1
WHERE request_id = ?
  AND status IN ('pending', 'retryable_failed')
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM app.review_rebuild_chunk_v5
    WHERE request_id = ? AND status <> 'sealed'
  )
RETURNING request_id, finalization_version, attempt_no;

-- Derived-output receipts and the TGT-0048 promotion receipt are inserted before owner-CAS terminal completion.
```

```sql
-- TGT-0054: bounded overlay lookup; sentinel means unavailable/overflow, never truncation.
SELECT overlay_id, overlay_kind, overlay_value_json, source_event_id, eligible_until
FROM app.review_overlay_event_v5
WHERE project_id = ? AND article_id = ? AND read_surface = ?
  AND reconcile_status = 'pending' AND eligible_until > ?
ORDER BY created_at DESC, overlay_id
LIMIT MAX_ACTIVE_OVERLAYS_PER_ARTICLE + 1;
```

```sql
-- TGT-0057: stale workers cannot update another generation's batch/result state.
UPDATE app.review_bulk_job_claim_v5
SET owner_token = ?, owner_generation = owner_generation + 1, lease_expires_at = ?, status = 'running'
WHERE job_id = ? AND (status = 'pending' OR lease_expires_at <= ?)
RETURNING owner_generation;

INSERT INTO app.review_bulk_batch_receipt_v5 (...)
VALUES (...)
ON CONFLICT(job_id, batch_ordinal, cursor_in) DO NOTHING;

UPDATE app.review_bulk_job_claim_v5
SET cursor_json = ?, processed_count = processed_count + ?, status = ?
WHERE job_id = ? AND owner_token = ? AND owner_generation = ?;
```

```sql
-- TGT-0058: eligibility, bounded delete and receipt commit together.
BEGIN;
SELECT reference_type, reference_id
FROM app.retention_reference_v5
WHERE target_key = ? AND object_id > ?
ORDER BY object_id
LIMIT 513;

DELETE FROM target_table
WHERE rowid IN (
  SELECT rowid FROM target_table candidate
  WHERE candidate.project_id = ? AND candidate.object_id > ?
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM app.retention_reference_v5 ref WHERE ref.object_id = candidate.object_id)
  ORDER BY candidate.object_id
  LIMIT 512
);
INSERT INTO app.retention_step_receipt_v5 (...) VALUES (...);
COMMIT;
```

### Reads, Writes, Leases, Retries And Idempotence

| Target | Representative reads | Representative writes and idempotence | Lease, retry and failure contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TGT-0046` | Point revision; closed source-vector page; snapshot composition by exact revision ID | Insert/build source rows, seal once; content ID makes identical replay a no-op and conflicting bytes a failure | Build owner generation; three same-input attempts; failed/unsealed revisions never compose and terminal attempts have a finite horizon. |
| `TGT-0047` | Build cursor; 512+1 winner page; sealed header/base count/checksum | Idempotent page receipt then base upsert under build ID; one immutable seal | Build lease/owner generation; gap/overlap/count/checksum failure keeps prior selected revision; reset creates a new build. |
| `TGT-0048` | One head, one snapshot and at most 11 component refs | Insert immutable candidate/validation then one head CAS/publication receipt | Promotion has no stale-worker write after CAS loss; failure stays candidate/failed and exact active/LKG remains readable. |
| `TGT-0049` | Point owner lease; bounded active/reference scan | Atomic job+lease insert or compensation; matching owner generation renew/release is idempotent | Finite lease/renewal policy; stale/expired generation is fenced; unresolved orphan blocks cleanup/admission. |
| `TGT-0050` | Partition keyset events and separate frontier values | Atomic sequence allocation/event insert; reconcile/dirty/visible receipts advance only their named values | Typed attempt/quarantine policy; duplicate same digest is no-op, conflicting duplicate/gap is blocked and never skipped. |
| `TGT-0051` | Oldest lane's 64 claims; exact attempt/output/ACK checkpoint | Owner-CAS claim, immutable attempt/output receipt, one advancing lane row | 120-second proposed lease/three attempts; lease loss or output/publication mismatch cannot ACK/complete. |
| `TGT-0052` | Point consumer lane and bounded receipt chain | Monotonic CAS from event -> dirty -> output -> visible; same receipt is no-op | No time-based takeover without owner generation; regression/duplicate/alias drift is quarantined, not merged. |
| `TGT-0053` | Request plan; claimable chunk page; all-chunk terminal check; finalization state | Immutable request/chunk identity, owner-fenced attempts/output, independently claimable finalization/promotion receipt | Three chunk attempts/depth below 12; bounded finalization attempts. Failure preserves sealed chunks and active/LKG. |
| `TGT-0054` | Bounded article/config/surface overlay plus sentinel | Canonical write+event transaction; exact visibility receipt reconciles; expiry and delete are separate | Writer transaction is the ownership fence; overflow/divergence/missing visibility is unavailable, and cleanup retry uses the same row key. |
| `TGT-0055` | Central job; bounded intake/queue/claim/outbox/import/visibility/closeout pages | Each handoff inserts a typed immutable receipt; same receipt key/no changed benchmark settings is idempotent | Owner generations per scheduler/worker/importer; bounded attempts; any missing step preserves retry/quarantine evidence and prevents false completion. |
| `TGT-0056` | Work-kind/scope run and typed step; current health point read; bounded telemetry/history | Run/step receipts are append-only; health is replaceable; provider/closeout/delete receipts retain their natural identities | Per-service owner generation/lease and typed retry policy; unknown kind/open payload/late conflict is quarantined with finite history. |
| `TGT-0057` | Point job; 500+1 selection/batch page; typed result/artifact/delivery manifest | Atomic criteria+pin admission; immutable batch receipt then owner-CAS progress; final manifest sealed once | Owner token/generation replaces `updated_at` ownership; three attempts; failed side effect/artifact/delivery/pin settlement blocks terminal ready. |
| `TGT-0058` | Versioned policy/target, bounded references/orphans and 512+1 eligible rows | Delete and step receipt share a transaction; complete-cycle receipt only after every registered target | Cleaner owner generation/lease; exact step replay is idempotent; policy drift/reference uncertainty/restore failure leaves failed/resumable cycle. |

### Finite Retention, History And Orphan Policy

Every family must store both `MAX_TERMINAL_AGE` and `MAX_TERMINAL_ROWS` (or a
stricter typed equivalent), plus active-work caps, schedule, owner, reference
types and restore requirement. Cleanup applies the earlier safe boundary and
must never treat reaching a cap as deletion authority. Audit-required history
older than the hot bound moves only to an approved versioned cold target under
US-098; without that target, new non-recovery admission blocks before hot
history becomes indefinite.

| State class | Required protection and finite disposition |
| --- | --- |
| Building/pending/running | Protected by live owner generation/lease and request/job/source relation; capped by per-scope active rows and maximum age. Expired owners become repair candidates, not automatic success or deletion. |
| Candidate/unsealed | Retained until sealed, failed or owner-approved abandoned; bounded candidate count/age. Abandonment records reason, input/output digest and reference scan. |
| Active/LKG | Never age-deleted. Protected by the single snapshot head and exact immutable references until a later atomic head change plus reference/restore proof. |
| Pinned/reader-held/export-held | Protected until matching owner generation releases and delivery/read completes. Expiry only permits orphan review; it does not prove safe cleanup. |
| Retryable failed/quarantined | Retain finite attempts, last input/error and repair/operator decision. Retry exhaustion never resets identity or discards benchmark-critical failure. |
| Completed/visible/delivered | Retain until all applicable consumer frontiers, audit/export/transfer references, token/closeout and restore horizons pass; then archive or delete in a receipted 512-row step. |
| Reconciled/expired/released | Logical ineligibility is separate from physical deletion. Reference/orphan scan, reader/cleaner leases and restore validation remain mandatory. |
| Orphan/unknown version | Never delete by age alone. Quarantine under a finite operator queue; resolve to repair, approved archive or receipted delete before the queue cap. |

### Migration, Cutover, Rollback And Cleanup

Each target migrates under its component owner; there is no all-control big-bang
or permanent dual authority.

1. Freeze canonical component/source/work/job/status/owner vocabularies,
   immutable identity fields, benchmark-critical configuration and every
   finite `MAX_*`/horizon. Missing values are blockers, not defaults.
2. Attach an immutable non-live applied DuckDB/SQLite/file inventory with
   effective constraints/indexes, row/status/null/reference/orphan counts,
   JSON/open-domain values and hashes. Never inspect the live DuckDB directly.
3. Create an isolated release-candidate v5 target and migration ledger. Record
   target DDL/hash/version and prove constraints, access plans and backup/restore
   before any production writer changes.
4. Backfill in bounded keyset pages, active and LKG references first, then live
   leases/jobs/work, then finite terminal history. Each page records cursor
   in/out, source/target counts, checksums, bytes, conflicts and attempts.
5. Map legacy mutable identities to immutable revisions/attempts. Preserve
   exact failures, retry counts, source frontiers, selected/snapshot references,
   pins and local-to-central receipts; do not synthesize zero/complete values.
6. Quiesce one component/owner lane at an explicit source high water, drain or
   fence in-flight owners, reconcile source -> dirty -> output -> visible state
   and run shadow reads. Broad dual writers are rejected.
7. Switch that lane's writer to v5, validate repeat idempotence and recovery,
   then build a complete candidate snapshot from sealed v5 revisions. Old
   active/LKG remains authoritative until one `TGT-0048` promotion CAS passes.
8. Switch readers/jobs by versioned contract after exact current/candidate row,
   order, cursor, status/error, export/transfer and browser/desktop comparisons.
   Mixed-version readers fail unavailable; they do not merge old/new rows.
9. Hold a finite rollback horizon. Rollback changes the head/contract fence to
   the last validated old authority, stops v5 writers and preserves v5 failure
   receipts; it never reconstructs old state from a mutable target guess.
10. After all target proofs, zero old writers/readers/leases/references and an
    executable restore pass, archive required history and delete old controls
    in bounded `TGT-0058` steps. Record reclaimed logical/physical bytes
    separately and run later route/worker/export/transfer validation.

### Rejected Control Targets

- Reject a semantic manifest ID whose generation, config, input map, output or
  status can mutate after a snapshot references it.
- Reject open component/watermark JSON as the sole publication relation, or a
  checksum/count that omits fields later used for order, freshness or recovery.
- Reject multiple active rows selected by timestamp, activation without a head
  CAS, and LKG reconstructed from current mutable manifests.
- Reject pin acquisition before job insert without atomicity/compensation,
  ref-count/expiry as cleanup proof, or ordinary long readers without an
  owner-approved lease decision.
- Reject `status` plus `updated_at` as a claim fence, in-process locks as cross-
  process ownership, and progress/terminal writes without owner generation CAS.
- Reject threshold value inside ACK-lane identity, scalar/map maxima as a
  consumer visibility proof, or any watermark that skips a pending/quarantined
  source event or late-membership replay contract.
- Reject chunk completion as request finalization, finalization that cannot be
  claimed after all chunks complete, and retry/split loops without attempt,
  depth, rows, bytes, calls and termination caps.
- Reject expiry/reconcile/release invocation as physical cleanup, mutable
  timestamps as leases, and retention marks that record only a next table index
  or `last_cleaned_at` instead of step and full-cycle receipts.
- Reject one generic job/control table that collapses selection, claim,
  execution snapshot, result, import, visibility, token closeout, artifact
  delivery or cleanup into a single status or open JSON payload.
- Reject all-ID job/result/history arrays, recursive read-all drains, reference-
  blind cleanup, infinite terminal/quarantine history, age-only orphan deletion
  and admission that silently evicts history at a cap.
- Reject a migration that switches readers before complete sealed publication,
  retains permanent dual writers, fabricates missing deployed values, silently
  falls back to old/default benchmark settings or weakens active/LKG recovery.

## Recommendation Proof Gate

Create separate `PRF-####` rows for positive and negative proof. For a move,
derive, archive, or delete recommendation, the minimum domains are:

| Domain | Required proof |
| --- | --- |
| API and UI/runtime | Every mounted and shared browser/desktop behavior is preserved, replaced, or proven unrelated. |
| Writer | Every direct, generated, registry-driven, or script writer and invalidation input is traced. |
| Lifecycle | Create, update, publish, pin, retire, orphan, and cleanup behavior is traced. |
| Recovery | Replay, restart, repair, startup probe, audit-history, and disaster-recovery roles are preserved or proven absent. |
| Export | Project export, PDF/bulk hydration, and other exports are preserved or proven unrelated. |
| Transfer | Transfer-package write/read mappings and compatibility needs are preserved or proven unrelated. |
| Retention | Active, failed, last-known-good, pinned, historical, and terminal retention is explicit. |
| Snapshot consistency | Identity, cursor, ordering, count, freshness, and pin semantics remain exact. |
| Benchmark and parity | Same-fixture semantics and budgets pass without retry, fallback, spill, or settings changes. |
| Migration/backfill | Replacement ownership, bounded cutover/backfill, rollback/recovery, and cleanup are explicit. |
| Bounded reads | No foreground path regresses to a project-scale scan or unbounded hydration. |

Any applicable `pending` proof keeps
`recommendationActionability: unresolved`; any applicable `blocked` proof
sets it to `blocked`. Search absence, a test-only guard, historical migration,
or baseline size alone cannot strengthen a recommendation.

## US-098 Local-File And Cold-Storage Target Shapes

US-097 is complete and remains the prerequisite. US-098 designs concrete,
bounded alternatives for the exact US-091 rooted/file slice: 32 physical
`DBO-0291`-`DBO-0322` objects and 35 `CMF-1948`-`CMF-1982` material domains,
represented by 67 disposition rows. The 55 `keep` rows remain
`recommendationActionability: unresolved`; the 12 `archive`/`delete` rows
remain `recommendationActionability: blocked` through `PRF-0906`-`PRF-0911`.
This story adds target designs and validation requirements only. It does not
recount a file, field, persisted reference, DuckDB scalar, runtime route,
generated response or client-saved copy.

Scoped `src`, `scripts` and `package.json` source is unchanged from the US-091
baseline `ac88a6d7` through HEAD `e073664000f81c72642045509a287530cd61c5a1`.
The current source therefore remains the evidence baseline, not an applied or
deployed file inventory. No live/current DuckDB or SQLite file, configured
snapshot, root inventory, fixture, server, app, browser, packaged desktop,
worker, projector, import, export, transfer, repair, backup, cleanup or restore
process was opened or run.

`auditStatus`, `proofCheckState`, `recommendationActionability` and
`overallCertification` remain independent. Every new target proof is
`proofCheckState: blocked`; no prior proof state, disposition or certification
state advances. Proposed limits are hard design ceilings pending owner and
physical validation. Exceeding one fails, queues a separately admitted bounded
operation, or returns explicit unavailable state; it never truncates, scans a
whole root, falls back to a stable path, weakens configured benchmark settings
or invents a successful cleanup/restore receipt.

### Common Root, Metadata And Lookup Contract

The targets use a closed root registry rather than persisting machine-specific
absolute paths: `data` is the configured DuckDB/platform data root, `runtime`
is the web working root or desktop data root, `os-temp` is an explicitly
registered same-device temporary root, `cold` is an owner-approved recovery/
archive root and `client` denotes bytes handed to the browser/desktop save
boundary. Persisted relative paths use NFC-normalized POSIX separators, at most
2,048 UTF-8 bytes and 255 bytes/segment; absolute, empty, `..`, NUL, raw
backslash, case-fold collision, symlink and root escape fail. Rebase resolves
the registered root then verifies the final target stays below it. A source
path string alone is never file identity or existence proof.

App-managed objects propose a typed logical metadata catalog
`app.local_file_object_v1`, not executed DDL. Its primary key is
`(target_kind,object_key,generation)` and exact fields are `root_id`,
`relative_path`, `byte_length`, `sha256`, `media_type`, `serializer_version`,
`permission_profile`, nullable `encryption_key_id`, `state`, `created_at`,
`published_at`, nullable `invalidated_at`, `retain_until`, `owner_kind`,
`owner_generation` and `manifest_hash`. `relative_path` is unique. A head row
keyed `(target_kind,object_key)` selects one published generation by CAS. A
reference row keyed `(target_kind,object_key,generation,reference_kind,
reference_key)` has a reverse `(reference_kind,reference_key)` index. A cleanup
index is `(target_kind,state,retain_until,object_key,generation)`; a content
lookup index is `(target_kind,sha256,byte_length)`. Engine/bootstrap and cold
targets that must survive an unavailable primary database use the same fields
in a deterministic immutable sidecar plus a bounded atomically replaced head/
catalog file. Client-delivery targets keep the manifest in the response/job
receipt and never pretend the client path is server-managed.

One foreground request may resolve at most 100 exact object keys, 512 metadata/
reference rows, 2 MiB encoded metadata and three physical storage attempts in
five seconds. One cleanup step visits at most 256 catalog rows, deletes at most
64 objects or 4 GiB, and persists a continuation. One cycle runs at most 32
steps/8,192 catalog rows before yielding. A target may impose a smaller cap.
No operation calls `readdir`/recursive walk/glob/newest selection as its normal
lookup or cleanup authority. A one-time migration inventory is separately
capped and resumable below.
