### Atomic Publication, Access, Protection And Distribution

Except for engine-owned WAL and client-only delivery, an object writer creates
`.<object_key>.<generation>.partial` in the final directory with exclusive
create, writes bounded bytes, flushes/syncs the file, computes length/hash and
validates format, renames on the same device, syncs the parent, then commits the
catalog/reference/head CAS and immutable publication receipt. A database row
never points at partial or unvalidated bytes. If the byte rename succeeds and
the reference transaction fails, the immutable unreferenced generation is an
orphan eligible only after catalog reconciliation and grace; it is safer than
publishing a missing reference. Replacing an existing stable pathname,
cross-device rename/copy as an atomic claim, or writing the reference first is
forbidden.

The permission baseline proposed for app-managed roots is owner-only directory
access (`0700`) and file access (`0600`) or the equivalent single-user Windows
ACL. This records the repo's no-auth single-user assumption; it does not add an
auth/session/admin requirement. PDF/import/FHIR/judgment/backup/cold content
requires an owner decision between documented full-volume encryption and
envelope encryption. Envelope keys live outside the artifact/catalog and key
IDs are backed up without key bytes. Logs and portable output require explicit
redaction. Source defaults, OS temp, loopback binding and packaged-desktop
location do not prove any permission or encryption property.

### Retention, Cleanup, Recovery, Portability And Migration

Every cleanup action uses owner generation plus a durable step receipt containing
policy version, target/key range, frozen clock, scanned/protected/deleted/
quarantined counts and bytes, reference/reader/download leases, pre/post hashes,
error, continuation and completion. Expiry removes eligibility only. A complete
cycle receipt is distinct from a successful delete call, and a delete receipt
is distinct from post-cleanup route/worker/export/restore validation. Failed or
interrupted deletion leaves the same continuation retryable; unknown reference,
sole recovery copy, live reader, unvalidated backup or missing key blocks
deletion rather than forcing it.

Portability uses root ID plus relative path, schema/serializer/engine version,
length and hash. Absolute source paths, inode/device IDs and case-sensitive
names are evidence, not portable identity. Relocation validates NFC/case-fold
collisions, target filesystem capabilities, final realpath, permissions,
encryption/key availability and later consumer bytes. Machine-local leases,
caches, scratch and logs rebuild rather than migrate.

### Bounded Migration And Cutover Protocol

Every target follows the same ten receipts, specialized by the last column
above:

1. Freeze target kind, root registry, natural key, generation, serializer/
   engine version, caps, permission/encryption/key policy, owners and supported
   web/desktop/export/transfer behaviors. Unknown values block; no defaults.
2. Obtain an approved immutable non-live root/reference snapshot. Enumerate
   only named roots with a persisted lexical cursor, maximum 256 entries,
   4 GiB and depth 16 per step and 32 steps per cycle. If the platform cannot
   page safely, make an owner-approved immutable file list first; never call an
   unbounded recursive scan.
3. Reconcile every path against database/cursor/session/package/client
   references as referenced, orphan, missing, collision, external/unmanaged or
   blocked. Persist counts/bytes/hash and continuation; unavailable is not zero.
4. Backfill candidate catalog/manifests by exact key. Copy to same-target temp,
   hash/validate/rename and preserve source until target equality passes. Never
   move the only recovery copy or fabricate missing model/content/security data.
5. Run source and target point/bounded-page reads over the immutable inventory;
   compare keys, bytes, hashes, errors, references and order. Browser/desktop or
   operator non-applicability requires owner-signed evidence, not source absence.
6. Quiesce one target writer lane at an owner-generation high water. Broad dual
   writes and reader-first cutover are forbidden.
7. Switch exactly one writer to the target, publish one receipt, shadow-compare
   bounded writes and repair or roll back before accepting another generation.
8. Switch reference/cursor/session/catalog head and then readers/routes/tools in
   a named order. A byte publish and database reference remain separate receipts.
9. Exercise interruption, restart, corruption, permission/key loss, restore,
   export/transfer and supported browser/desktop flows under the same fixed
   fixture. Preserve the first configured failure without retry downgrade.
10. After the finite rollback horizon, zero-reference/lease scan and clean-host
    restore, receipted cleanup removes old generations in bounded steps and
    later validation proves routes/workers/exports still succeed. Only then can
    a linked recommendation be reconsidered; US-098 itself changes none.

### Rejected Local And Cold Targets

| Rejected shape | Reason for rejection |
| --- | --- |
| Directory scan, recursive walk, glob or newest-mtime selection as normal lookup/cleanup | Work is bounded only by deployed residue and can omit case/link/collision/reference state. Exact key/catalog access plus persisted migration/cleanup continuation is mandatory. |
| Stable filename overwrite for PDF, import, settings, cache, manifest, package or recovery output | Readers can observe partial/new bytes under an old identity, retry history is erased and reference equality cannot be proved. Immutable generation plus one head/reference CAS is required. |
| Temp write on another device followed by rename/copy | Cross-device rename is not atomic; copy exposes partial bytes. Temp must share the final directory/device or publication needs an explicit staged-copy protocol and seal. |
| Database/cursor/session reference before byte validation and publication | A committed reference can point to absent/partial/corrupt bytes. Publish immutable bytes first, then reference; orphan bytes are repaired later by exact catalog key. |
| Treating DuckDB WAL, ordinary-file manifest, application temp rename or filesystem journal as one atomicity proof | These are separate proof domains. Engine checkpoint/replay cannot certify application metadata, directory durability, client delivery or cleanup. |
| Cataloging the primary database only inside that database | The catalog is unavailable exactly when bootstrap/restore needs it. Database/WAL/backup/startup targets require an independent bounded manifest/head. |
| Current project-transfer `MAX_*` names as enforced ceilings | The checked-in gate accepts values above several named maxima. US-098 targets must enforce every ceiling and keep inline/background routing separate from admission. |
| TTL, stale status, dead PID, `finally`, terminal job/session or successful `rm` as cleanup proof | Eligibility, ownership, invocation, deletion, reclamation and later validation are separate. Reference/reader/download leases and durable step/cycle receipts are mandatory. |
| OS-temp or desktop location as a permission/encryption guarantee | Actual owner/mode/ACL, link/final path, volume/envelope encryption and key custody must be inventoried and validated per supported platform. |
| Source absence as browser/desktop `not-applicable` | Internal/cold targets still need an owner-approved applicability decision and negative route/platform proof; shared UI code also cannot prove packaged-desktop parity. |
| Package checksum or snapshot key as a freeze of later hydration/assets | Selection, hydration, generated bytes, package assets, delivery and client save are distinct. The sealed output must bind exact source revisions and bytes. |
| Unbounded HTTP stream or client Blob as a complete generated artifact | A partial network response or memory exhaustion has no completed delivery. Bounded bytes must be sealed before handoff or routed to a separately admitted package job. |
| Backup file existence as recoverability | Pairing, versions, encryption keys, open/checkpoint, clean-host restore and later product/export/transfer checks must pass; the sole valid copy is never an ordinary cleanup candidate. |
| Broad hot+cold or old+new dual writes during migration | Two mutable authorities create an unbounded reconciliation tail. Use bounded inventory/backfill, one writer-generation fence, ordered reference/read switch, finite rollback and receipted cleanup. |

## US-099 LLM Row, Order And Cursor Validation

### US-099 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-098 is complete. US-099 is the first target-validation story after the
design phase and is limited to the mounted LLM list row contract. It compares
the checked-in current `review.llm.rows` selection plus bounded LLM judgment
hydration with the layered `TGT-0018`-`TGT-0022`, `TGT-0024`-`TGT-0026`
candidate, display, selected-import, LLM-status, payload and composition
contracts. Counts, facets, options and token/substring search algorithms remain
US-100 scope. The current route's separate count call must be visible in a
future trace, but US-099 cannot certify its value or cost.

Scoped `src`, `scripts` and `package.json` source is unchanged from the US-093
baseline `31b1c024` through HEAD
`4ca6a3de229a949ef2662affd1d83127b708df51`. The v5 component table names and
candidate SQL remain design text only in this audit file; no executable schema,
fixture builder, current-to-candidate adapter or candidate route exists in
checked-in product source.

The story authorizes isolated disposable-fixture mutation only after the
fixture and benchmark-critical values are approved. It does not itself supply
that approval. No immutable fixture/report/root, generator/version/seed,
model, provider, thinking options, ordered prompt set, content flags, frozen
clock, memory limit, runtime profile/role/topology/version, snapshot/component
identities, executable candidate DDL/SQL bundle, semantic oracle or complete
plan/rows/bytes/spill/RSS/latency/attempt collector was supplied or found.
Execution therefore stopped before fixture creation. Repository scale and
workload declarations, resolver defaults, mocked smoke, unit-test rows, an
existing project, a configured snapshot or the live/current DuckDB are not
substitutes.

All physical and semantic comparison results below are `unavailable`, never
zero or passed. `auditStatus`, `proofCheckState`,
`recommendationActionability` and `overallCertification` remain independent.
Eight new validation proofs are `blocked`; no existing target proof,
disposition or recommendation advances.

| Candidate versus hydration | Current SQL joins payload metadata before the limit and later hydrates LLM judgments in at most 100-ID/10,000-row chunks. | `TGT-0024` limits candidates first; `TGT-0020`/`TGT-0021`/`TGT-0022`/`TGT-0025` hydrate only page IDs and `TGT-0026` supplies bounded judgments. | Candidate work, page rows, each hydration call and final response remain separate. The 501st sentinel is never hydrated or returned. |
| Response fields | Current item keys are the exact `ArticleReviewResult` mapping actually emitted by `getResponseRows`; envelope includes page/cursor plus adjacent count fields. | Candidate composer emits the same versioned item/envelope projection or an owner-approved explicit API version; missing required component rows fail. | Deep canonical equality for values, nulls, arrays and order. Count values/cost are captured but remain US-100 proof; their presence cannot certify row parity. |
| Cursor and pagination | Cursor signs contract, normalized filter signature, review config, snapshot, sort tuple and current component generation/watermark/identity state. Page is echoed; forward continuation is cursor-driven. | Cursor signs the exact immutable component revision tuple and reviewed sort values. No offset/current-source fallback is allowed. | Same page IDs and next-page boundary; no duplicate, skip or changed tie direction. Invalid, stale or mismatched cursor rejects before candidate SQL. |
| Snapshot and freshness | Route resolves active else LKG once; `allowStale:true` admits a retired manifest. Candidate, failed and missing manifests reject. | Resolve ready active or explicitly selected LKG plus complete sealed bindings once; acquire target revision leases before reading. | Snapshot/config/component identity, readiness label and failure class are compared separately from returned rows. A different snapshot is not a retry. |
| Resource work | Current route can issue date/config/manifest work, one candidate query, zero-to-five judgment calls and a separate count query; source declarations do not prove applied work. | Binding/lease, one candidate-prefix/page-hydration statement, bounded judgment calls and separate count contract; target build is outside read timing. | Per statement and total rows scanned/returned/written, logical result/response bytes, plans, temp spill, RSS, calls/attempts and latency. Returned page size is not a scan bound. |
| Failure integrity | Reader rejects malformed/mismatched cursor, missing component, non-ready snapshot, SQL-shape or admission failure; no raw OLAP fallback is imported. | Missing revision/row, cap overrun, mixed identity, lease failure or plan/resource violation rejects without current/source fallback. | Preserve the first failure. Any raw/project scan, nonzero foreground spill, hidden retry, alternate snapshot, page shrink, setting change or weaker rerun fails the scenario. |

The fixture must freeze one authoritative corpus and materialize current and
candidate shapes from that same corpus/checkpoint. Setup, candidate build and
cleanup are outside foreground timing but still record their rows written and
bytes. The current and candidate operations run in a randomized, owner-approved
order against immutable copies or reset-to-checksum-equivalent states; no first
run may warm or mutate state for only one side.

### Required LLM Scenario Oracle

| Linked proof | Scenario and frozen cases | Exact semantic oracle | Mandatory rejection checks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PRF-0992` | Ready first/empty/max page: active snapshot, no optional filters, limits 1 and 500, zero-row and 501-sentinel cases. | Exact ordered IDs, `sort_key`/article tie order, at-most-500 returned rows, next-cursor presence, page/limit echo and item/envelope fields. | Sentinel hydration/return, page shrink, missing/extra/duplicate ID, field/null mismatch or unrecorded adjacent count call. |
| `PRF-0993` | Equal-key forward traversal: enough articles sharing each boundary `sort_key` to cross first, middle and last pages; replay every emitted cursor once. | Concatenated pages equal one frozen ordered oracle exactly; cursor predicate is `sort_key < value OR (IS NOT DISTINCT FROM value AND article_id > value)`. | Skip, duplicate, loop, changed tie direction, offset substitution, token reuse under changed filter/config/snapshot/component identity. |
| `PRF-0994` | LLM applicability/status: exact active and wrong model/content identities, enabled/disabled prompts, unanswered/partial/answered rows, current delete generation and tombstones; default/`both`, `partial` and `complete`. | Current and candidate produce identical applicable IDs, `llm_status_key`, judged/enabled counts, non-placeholder judgments, prompt IDs and `isFullyJudged`. | Column absence as applicability proof, stale generation inclusion, placeholder emission, config default, prompt drop or status/detail mismatch. |
| `PRF-0995` | Response and bounded hydration: null/non-null display/selected/source fields, scalar/array answer, explanation/quotes, placeholder input, 100-ID and prompt-count-driven chunk boundaries. | Deep equality of every emitted item key/value/null/array/order and of judgment ordering; hydration covers exactly returned page IDs and complete applicable prompt rows. | Pre-limit target payload work, 501st-row hydration, incomplete article chunk, silent null/default, missing required component, unbounded calls/rows/bytes or response-key drift. |
| `PRF-0996` | Snapshot/revision replay: issue a cursor, publish a distinct active snapshot/revision tuple, then read the original and new identities through their explicitly allowed paths. | Frozen old identity either remains explicitly readable under approved LKG/retention semantics or rejects with the exact typed mismatch; new identity never reinterprets the old token. | Mutable component reuse, mixed current/old revisions, implicit active switch, alternate-snapshot retry or cleanup while a valid lease/reference exists. |
| `PRF-0997` | Stale/LKG: active absent with one retained readable manifest, then active present beside retired; compare explicit stale admission and diagnostics independently. | Exact selected snapshot, stale versus ready state, IDs/order/cursor/fields and no source fallback. | Treating stale as ready, selecting by newest timestamp, mixing active count/hydration with LKG rows, or concealing stale state in a successful row envelope. |
| `PRF-0998` | Indexing/failed/missing/incomplete: candidate, failed with error, missing manifest and ready manifest missing each required LLM component/binding/row. | Exact indexing/unavailable/failure reason, snapshot/error diagnostics and zero candidate-row execution after pre-query rejection; target missing hydrated row is an explicit component-incomplete failure. | Empty-success substitution, raw/source read, default component identity, partial page, retry against LKG/current unless selected before admission, or unavailable-as-zero. |
| `PRF-0999` | Cursor/resource integrity: malformed token plus every contract/filter/config/snapshot/sort/component mismatch; admitted boundary and deliberately over-cap/scan/spill/retry cases. | Exact rejection reason before row SQL for token mismatches; admitted cases stay within approved plan/row/byte/call/RSS/latency budgets with one physical attempt and unchanged settings. | Raw/project-scale scan, nonzero foreground spill, hidden nested retry, result mismatch, OOM, page/config downgrade, collector gap or weaker rerun. |

US-100 owns exact count, filter/facet/option and search-result proof. US-099
nevertheless captures the current list service's adjacent count statement and
its contribution to end-to-end latency/RSS/calls so it cannot disappear from
resource accounting. It does not use count equality to pass any LLM-row proof.

### Measurement Definitions And Recorded Results

For each side and scenario, `rowsScanned` is the sum of actual applied
operator rows scanned for every named statement, with manifest/config/date,
candidate, payload/status, judgment and adjacent count work reported
separately. Returned rows, a `LIMIT`, index declaration or estimated cardinality
cannot substitute. A raw/project-scale scan, an operator over the approved cap
or an unprofiled statement rejects the scenario.

`rowsWritten` separates fixture seed/current materialization, candidate build,
read-window control/lease writes and cleanup. Source read-only intent is not a
physical zero, and target lease insertion/release is not candidate-result
mutation. `logicalOutputBytes` records canonical UTF-8 bytes for each database
result and for the final serialized route response separately; it excludes
index, WAL, temp and database-container bytes.

Temp evidence records engine spill bytes, spill-root growth and residue at
pre/post/cleanup checkpoints. Accepted foreground work requires all three to
be exactly zero. RSS records process topology, sampling cadence, start, peak,
end and peak-minus-start bytes for the complete route envelope. Latency records
wall-clock p50/p95/p99 for the owner-approved warmup/sample count plus every
individual failed sample; failures are not removed. Logical calls, database
statements and underlying physical attempts are distinct. Any retry, nested
adapter attempt above one, benchmark-setting change or weaker rerun rejects
the scenario and preserves the first failure.

The count vector is certified from independent expected membership, not from the
number of current or candidate result rows. Facet raw rows, complete option
domains and UI-derived controls are three comparisons. Product embedded search,
standalone token rows and asynchronous substring state are three contracts.

### Measurement Definitions And Rejection Rules

| Semantic output | Canonical request plus independent expected counts/options/IDs/order/availability/snapshot and serialized response; filters also retain raw facet/option rows and derived controls. | Any mismatch, omitted field/value, unapproved version difference, partial-ready output or unavailable-as-zero fails. |
| Rows scanned | Applied plan/profile operator rows for config/manifest/admission, every foreground query, nested posting/search probe and candidate/result lookup; report per statement and total. | Missing operator coverage, project/raw source scan, unbounded probe or plan drift outside the approved access path fails. |
| Rows written | Fixture/current/candidate materialization writes separately from request-time control/result writes, including substring jobs and receipts; zero requires an actual collector observation. | Undisclosed write, mutable active overwrite, unbounded fan-out or inferred zero fails. |
| Logical output bytes | Canonical encoded query-row bytes and HTTP response bytes; filters split raw rows from consumed controls; search/count retain diagnostics/error payloads. | Missing serializer/version, truncation, over-cap bytes or deriving bytes from row count fails. |
| Temp spill and residue | Per-statement engine spill plus isolated temp-root before/peak/after inventory. | Any foreground spill, residue, unapproved temp root or unavailable value fails. |
| RSS | Isolated process start/peak/end/delta with sampling interval and process tree. | Missing child process, over-budget peak/delta or mixed unrelated process fails. |
| Latency | Raw warm-up and measured samples, side order/cache state, end-to-end and statement timings; p50/p95/p99 computed from retained samples. | Missing sample, over-budget percentile, biased protocol or weaker rerun fails. |
| Calls and attempts | Browser/desktop HTTP requests, service calls, statements and underlying physical adapter attempts separately, plus before/after critical-setting hashes. | More than one physical attempt unless explicitly pre-approved, any hidden retry/fallback/downgrade, request duplication outside the approved UI contract or setting-hash change fails. |

### Measurement Definitions And Rejection Rules

| Metric | Required capture for each scenario and side | Rejection rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Semantic output | Canonical request plus independent expected IDs/order/status/applicability/prompt answers/snapshot/freshness/unavailable state and exact serialized item/envelope. | Any mismatch, omitted key/value/null/row, partial-ready output, unapproved version difference or unavailable-as-empty/zero fails. |
| Rows scanned | Applied plan/profile operator rows for configuration, manifest/admission, candidate/filter probes, payload/status/detail/prompt hydration and adjacent count, per statement and total. | Missing operator coverage, raw/project/source scan, over-cap probe, plan drift or inferring scans from returned rows/limits fails. |
| Rows written | Fixture seed/current materialization, candidate build, read-window lease/control writes and cleanup separately; request result writes require an observed zero. | Undisclosed write, mutable active overwrite, unbounded fan-out or inferred zero fails. |
| Logical output bytes | Canonical encoded database-result bytes per statement and final HTTP response bytes under one serializer/version. | Missing serializer, truncation, row-count-derived bytes, incomplete field projection or over-cap bytes fails. |
| Temp spill and residue | Per-statement engine spill plus isolated temp-root before/peak/after/cleanup inventory. | Any foreground spill, residue, unapproved root or unavailable measurement fails. |
| RSS | Isolated process tree start/peak/end/delta with fixed sampling cadence. | Missing child, mixed unrelated process, unavailable sample or over-budget peak/delta fails. |
| Latency | Retained warm-up and measured samples, randomized side order/cache state, end-to-end and statement times; p50/p95/p99 include failures. | Missing/removed sample, biased protocol, over-budget percentile or weaker rerun fails. |
| Calls, attempts and settings | Logical route/service calls, database statements and underlying physical attempts separately; before/after hashes for every critical value. | Any unapproved retry/duplicate/fallback, attempt above one, alternate snapshot, setting/default/downgrade change or collector gap fails. |

## US-102 Human Count And Filter/Option Validation

### US-102 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-101 is complete. US-102 owns exactly two mounted Human contracts: the
embedded list total returned by `POST /api/articlesreviewshuman`, and the raw
facet, option and derived-control response returned by
`GET /api/articlesreviewshumanfilters`. Human row membership, order, cursor and
hydrated response equality remain the independently blocked US-101 proofs;
US-102 uses their frozen applicability cases only to define the expected count
and filter populations.

Scoped `src`, `scripts` and `package.json` source is unchanged from the US-100
parent `8676cd8949dfcda63e73b1a33306fe018a5dcfc0` through HEAD
`53b8739211f08357a8e50f2a151a49b2bb255030`. The v5 count, facet, option and
filter-result objects remain design text in this audit file. No checked-in
candidate DDL, materializer, reader, route adapter, immutable receipt binder or
cleanup implementation exists.

The story permits isolated disposable-fixture mutation only after an owner
approves the common fixture and every benchmark-critical value. It does not
supply those choices. No immutable fixture/report root, generator/seed, model,
provider, thinking setting, ordered prompts, Human mode, content flags, clock,
DuckDB memory/runtime/platform profile, executable candidate, independent
count/domain oracle, complete physical collector or platform controller was
supplied or found. Same-fixture execution therefore stopped before benchmark
fixture creation. Existing projects, current/live DuckDB, resolver defaults,
source constants and fake rows were not substituted.

Focused current-contract tests ran after that gate. Nine tests created their
own `/tmp/forska-summary-*.duckdb` files with the source-fixed `256MiB` memory
cap; each connection closed and each file was removed in `finally`, and the
post-run residue scan found zero matching paths. Those current-only reducer
fixtures neither execute the candidate nor populate any scenario metric.

Both new proof rows are `blocked`. `auditStatus`, `proofCheckState`,
`recommendationActionability` and `overallCertification` remain independent;
no target proof, disposition or recommendation advances.

### Measurement Definitions And Rejection Rules

| Metric | Required capture for every scenario and side | Rejection rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Semantic and platform output | Canonical fixture/config/request plus independent exact totals, IDs, flags, badges, prompt counts, composition, tones, raw facets/options/counts, derived controls, snapshots, availability/errors and serialized browser/desktop output. | Any mismatch, omitted value/state/field, approximation, cross-grain substitution, unapproved version difference or unavailable-as-zero/empty fails. |
| Rows scanned | Applied operator plans for config/manifest/admission, candidate/status/selected/payload/posting/search/count, named disagreement, facet/option/receipt and platform-triggered statements, per statement and total. | Missing operator coverage, raw/source/project scan, unbounded probe, plan drift or inference from `COUNT`, `LIMIT` or returned rows fails. |
| Rows written | Common fixture seed/current materialization, candidate builds, request/result/lease/receipt and cleanup writes separately; request-time zero requires observation. | Undisclosed write, active overwrite, unbounded fan-out or inferred zero fails. |
| Logical output bytes | Canonical encoded bytes for every database result and HTTP/platform response; split count, selected flag/badge, LLM/Human composition, named disagreement, facet, option and derived-control outputs. | Missing serializer/version, truncation, row-count estimate, omitted ignored field or over-cap bytes fails. |
| Temp spill and residue | Per-statement engine spill plus isolated temp-root before/peak/after/cleanup inventory for both sides and platform processes. | Any foreground spill, residue, unapproved root or unavailable measurement fails. |
| RSS | Isolated process-tree start/peak/end/delta with fixed cadence across the complete server/browser/desktop scenario. | Missing child/concurrent peak, mixed unrelated process, unavailable sample or over-budget peak/delta fails. |
| Latency | Retained warm-up/measured samples with approved side order/cache reset; end-to-end, request and statement timings; p50/p95/p99 retain failed samples. | Missing/removed failure, biased protocol, over-budget percentile or weaker rerun fails. |
| Calls, attempts and settings | Browser/desktop HTTP, service calls, database statements and underlying adapter attempts separately; before/after hashes for fixture, bundles, builds and every critical setting. | Any unapproved duplicate/retry/fallback, attempt above one, alternate snapshot, default/downgrade/setting change or collector gap fails. |

### Measurement Definitions And Rejection Rules

| Metric | Required capture for every scenario and side | Rejection rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Semantic and client output | Canonical fixture/config/request plus independent exact pairs, article IDs/count, order, pages, cursor outcomes, snapshots/freshness/errors, item/envelope keys and serialized browser/desktop output. | Any mismatch, omitted/extra ID or field, pair/article substitution, unavailable-as-zero, unapproved version difference or set-only equality fails. |
| Rows scanned | Applied operator plans for project date, manifest/admission, candidate, selected/display/payload, queue pair/article, posting/search, named/dynamic count and client-triggered statements, per statement and total. | Missing operator coverage, raw/source/project/foreground candidate or queue scan, unbounded probe, plan drift or inference from `EXISTS`, `COUNT` or `LIMIT` fails. |
| Rows written | Common fixture seed/current materialization, candidate pair/article/count builds, request/result/lease/receipt and cleanup writes separately; request-time zero requires observation. | Undisclosed write, active overwrite, unbounded pair fan-out or inferred zero fails. |
| Logical output bytes | Canonical encoded bytes for each database result, pair/article/count receipt, HTTP response and rendered/client-consumed payload. | Missing serializer/version, row-count estimate, omitted null/absent field, truncation or over-cap bytes fails. |
| Temp spill and residue | Per-statement engine spill plus isolated temp-root before/peak/after/cleanup inventory for both sides and client processes. | Any foreground spill, residue, unapproved root or unavailable measurement fails. |
| RSS | Isolated process-tree start/peak/end/delta with fixed cadence across the complete server/browser/desktop scenario. | Missing child/concurrent peak, mixed unrelated process, unavailable sample or over-budget peak/delta fails. |
| Latency | Retained warm-up/measured samples with approved side order/cache reset; end-to-end, request and statement timings; p50/p95/p99 retain failed samples. | Missing/removed failure, biased protocol, over-budget percentile or weaker rerun fails. |
| Calls, attempts and settings | Browser/desktop HTTP, service calls, database statements and underlying adapter attempts separately; before/after hashes for fixture, bundles, builds and every critical setting. | Any unapproved duplicate/retry/fallback, attempt above one, alternate snapshot, default/downgrade/setting change or collector gap fails. |

project review-detail response for one article and the mounted prompt-preview
response for one prompt. Candidate selection, scalar/article payload,
LLM/Human judgment pages, derived placeholders, current judgment history,
Covidence-related records, full text, prompt/project/model configuration,
snapshot identity, client cache and browser/desktop transport remain separate
contracts. A singleton article ID or SQL `LIMIT 1` does not by itself bound
fan-out rows, encoded bytes, calls, recursive termination or later current
joins.

Each validation compares exact fields, IDs, ordering, snapshot identity,
judgment payloads, caps, stale and unavailable behavior, and browser/desktop
contracts. Physical accounting keeps statements, rows scanned, encoded output
bytes, temp spill, RSS, latency and `proofCheckState` separate for current and
candidate.

HEAD `96711e1343f1121c1793bf3e1ffb9bdbbd2cecdd` through current HEAD.

payload, judgment payload, prompt, full-text/blob or page-bounded detail
composer exists in checked-in product source. Current routes are executable,

The story permits isolated disposable-fixture mutation only after one common

## US-108 Full-Text And Keyed-Payload Hydration Validation

### US-108 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-107 is complete. US-108 owns exactly three validation grains: full-text and
ordinary-file hydration for one article; the keyed article payload component;
and keyed LLM/Human judgment payload pages. Candidate selection, article
payload, judgment payload, prompt content, canonical current text/HTML/admin
state, persisted asset reference, physical file, response bytes, client cache
and browser/desktop transport remain separate contracts. A singleton key, a
100-ID `IN` predicate, a 512-row page or one path validation does not by itself
bound fan-out rows, encoded bytes, files, calls, recursive termination or
browser subresource work.

Each validation compares exact bytes or fields, IDs, ordering, per-call and
request-wide caps, snapshot identity, file/reference paths where applicable,
stale/unavailable behavior and browser/desktop contracts. Physical accounting
keeps statements, rows scanned, files read, encoded output bytes, temp spill,
RSS, latency and `proofCheckState` separate for current and candidate.

Scoped `src`, `scripts` and `package.json` source is unchanged from the US-107
HEAD `f265e3c5254bb088a2f9ddf5abb253256f775417` through current HEAD.
`TGT-0025`-`TGT-0030` remain design text in this file; no executable v5 keyed
article/judgment/prompt/full-text/blob component or page-bounded composer
exists in checked-in product source. Current readers and file routes are
executable, but one-sided execution cannot satisfy the required same-fixture
comparison.

The story permits isolated disposable-fixture mutation only after one common
fixture, every benchmark-critical value, both executable sides, independent
byte/field/order/snapshot/path/cap/platform oracles and a complete physical
collector are approved. It supplies none of those inputs. Presence-only
checks found `DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT` plus sixteen named
`FORSKA_REVIEW_AUDIT_*` fixture, report, scale, seed, model, provider,
thinking, prompt, Human-mode, content, clock, runtime, collector, sample,
browser and desktop values unset. Source defaults, fake rows, current project
state and live/current databases are not substitutes. Execution therefore
stopped before common-fixture DDL/DML, EXPLAIN/profile, server/app/browser/
desktop startup, file-corpus creation or candidate execution.

Every same-fixture semantic and physical result below is `unavailable`, never
zero or passed. `auditStatus`, `proofCheckState`,
`recommendationActionability` and `overallCertification` remain independent.
Three new validation proofs are `blocked`; no existing target proof,
disposition or recommendation advances.

### Measurement Definitions And Rejection Rules

| Metric | Required capture for every scenario and side | Rejection rule |
| --- | --- | --- |

## US-109 Warning, Health/Readiness, And Rebuild-Progress Validation

### US-109 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-108 is complete. US-109 owns exactly three validation grains: the mounted
project-warning diagnostic; review health or runtime readiness; and rebuild
progress. The third grain selects rebuild progress rather than bulk-job
progress because later stories own the add/PDF/export operations. Warning
transport, reader admission, manifest freshness, repair mutation, health
reachability, runtime transport, semantic readiness, rebuild request state,
chunk execution, derived-output finalization, promotion visibility and client
polling remain separate contracts.

Each validation compares exact response fields, active/LKG/candidate identity,
stale/indexing/unavailable/failure behavior, declared and observed polling,
browser/desktop predicates and repeated work. Physical accounting keeps SQL
statements, applied rows scanned, encoded output bytes, RSS, latency, calls,
physical attempts and `proofCheckState` separate for current and candidate.

Current HEAD is the US-108 commit
`bffa32816675d65bc8144aa44381177fba0799e1`; scoped `src`, `scripts` and
`package.json` source is unchanged. `TGT-0046`, `TGT-0048`,
`TGT-0050`-`TGT-0053` and `TGT-0056` remain design text in this file. Exact
searches found no checked-in `review_component_revision_v5`,
`review_serving_snapshot_v5`, `review_serving_snapshot_head_v5` or
`maintenance_run_v5` product implementation, and no approved diagnostic route
or client adapter composes those targets. Current warning, health/readiness and
rebuild control paths are executable, but one-sided execution cannot satisfy a
same-fixture comparison.

The story permits isolated disposable-fixture mutation only after one common
fixture, every benchmark-critical value, both executable sides, independent
field/state/failure/polling/platform oracles and a complete physical collector
are approved. Presence-only checks found `DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT` plus sixteen
named `FORSKA_REVIEW_AUDIT_*` fixture, report, scale, seed, model, provider,
thinking, prompt, Human-mode, content, clock, runtime, collector, sample,
browser and desktop values unset. Source defaults, current-only test rows,
current project state and live/current databases are not substitutes.
Execution therefore stopped before common-fixture DDL/DML, EXPLAIN/profile,
server/app/browser/desktop startup, candidate materialization or polling.

Every same-fixture semantic and physical result below is `unavailable`, never
zero or passed. `auditStatus`, `proofCheckState`,
`recommendationActionability` and `overallCertification` remain independent.
Three new validation proofs are `blocked`; no existing target proof,
disposition or recommendation advances.

| Warning server read | Project access -> review-config identity -> diagnostics aggregate -> manifest selection/admission -> scope aggregate -> optional rebuild-request lookup/update/insert. | Rebuild diagnostics/progress | One broad diagnostics statement counts active/candidate/failed/retired snapshots, invalid candidate reasons, dirty work, latest request/chunks, outbox/quarantine/cursor and optional search. Warning folds those values into display counters and timestamps. | Returned counts do not prove immutable receipt linkage, read consistency, physical bounds or final visibility. A progress observation can cause repair work on the same request. |
| Rebuild execution/finalization | Request/chunk repositories select and mutate request priority, claims and status. Worker completion, reductions, option/stat refresh, candidate refresh, promotion and request final status are sequential. Catch-up selects all-completed admitted/running requests; finalization exceptions record failure. | Chunk `completed`, request status, derived output and active visibility are separate. A status transition or catch-up test does not prove crash-safe retry, bounded terminal history, cleanup or restoration. |
| Warning clients | Four review routes each instantiate banner and table observers of `['project-reviews-warnings',projectId]` with five-second interval/stale time and focus refetch disabled. List queries gate on `serving.readable`; filters use different gating. | Two same-key observers do not prove one request. Cache/dedup, offline/reconnect, timer skew, page mount/unmount, mutation count and browser/desktop parity are unobserved. |
| Readiness clients | Root `['backend-availability']` and Settings `['runtime-ready']` each declare 15 seconds under different keys. Settings can start two five-second diagnostics queries. Desktop startup recursively polls every 250 ms until any 2xx or 30 seconds. | Distinct keys permit repeated calls and a downstream waterfall. Browser semantic failure and desktop transport success can disagree during the same startup; no actual transition capture exists. |

### Measurement Definitions And Rejection Rules

| Metric | Required capture for every scenario and side | Rejection rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Semantic output and state | Canonical fixture/config plus independent exact fields, nullability, status/reason vocabularies, counts/timestamps, head/snapshot/component/request/finalization/promotion identities and browser/desktop states. | Any field mismatch, omitted/extra key, silent null/default, stale-as-ready, mixed identity, merged lifecycle grain or unapproved semantic difference fails. |
| Statements, requests and attempts | Retained SQL text/hash and service/database/HTTP/bridge order for access, config, diagnostics, manifest, scope, health, owner probe, rebuild repair/progress and every client poll; physical attempts separately. | Missing statement/request, hidden retry/repair/fallback, attempt above cap, alternate route/origin or inference from source intervals/query keys fails. |
| Rows scanned | Applied operator plans per statement and total, separating rows visited, qualified and returned across source scope and every control table. | Missing operator coverage, unbounded project/control/history scan, broad sort/JSON expansion, plan drift or inference from `LIMIT`/returned rows fails. |
| Encoded output bytes | Canonical encoded database values, JSON response bytes and aggregate browser/desktop bridge bytes by serializer/version for every success and failure state. | Character count, row estimate, omitted diagnostics, silent truncation, unbounded payload or unavailable measurement fails. |
| Temp spill and residue | Per-statement engine spill plus isolated database/WAL/temp/report before/peak/after/cleanup inventory. | Foreground spill, unapproved path, residue, missing phase or unavailable measurement fails. |
| RSS | Isolated backend/owner/client/desktop process-tree start/peak/end/delta at fixed cadence across reads, polls, repair, transition and cleanup. | Missing child/client peak, mixed unrelated process, unavailable sample or over-budget peak/delta fails. |
| Latency | Approved warm-up/measured samples with randomized side/cache order; per statement/request/poll and end-to-end p50/p95/p99 retain failures and unavailable states. | Removed failure, biased cache/side order, over-budget percentile or weaker rerun fails. |
| Polling and repeated work | Actual observer mounts, query-cache state, timer/focus/offline/reconnect/manual/startup triggers, HTTP calls, owner probes, diagnostics statements and repair mutations per interval and transition. | Source interval, shared key or test fake substituted for runtime count; duplicate/unbounded call, mutation-on-read not approved, or dedup assumption fails. |
| Settings and cleanup | Before/after hashes for fixture, both bundles, model/provider/thinking/prompts/content/runtime/platform/collector; fixture/build/report/cleanup writes and all process exits separately. | Default, downgrade, changed predicate/timeout/page, undisclosed write, incomplete cleanup/process stop or missing hash fails. |

## US-110 Token-Prefix And Substring-Search Validation

### US-110 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-109 is complete. US-110 owns exactly two validation grains: token-prefix
search and exact asynchronous substring search. Product embedded multi-token
prefix membership, the standalone one-prefix token-row service, substring job
control, result visibility, progress and browser/packaged-desktop reachability
remain separate contracts inside those two grains. A registered search mode or
pending job row is not result or caller proof.

Each validation compares exact IDs and order, project/config/search/scope/title/
candidate/snapshot identities, canonical signatures, cursor or continuation,
ready/stale/LKG/indexing/async/unavailable/failed/expired states, progress and
actual platform callers. Physical accounting keeps applied rows scanned,
fixture/build/control/result/cleanup rows written, canonical output bytes, temp
spill/residue, process-tree RSS, p50/p95/p99 latency, calls, physical attempts
and `proofCheckState` separate for current and candidate.

Current HEAD is the US-109 commit
`012aaf1b17de3ff882b6b5e77449756505e96831`. Scoped `src`, `scripts` and
`package.json` source is unchanged from the US-096 search design commit
`cd197355` through HEAD. Exact product-source searches found zero
implementations for `review_project_title_token_v5`,
`review_project_search_article_v5`, `review_project_search_revision_v5`,
`review_title_fact_v5`, `review_global_title_token_v5`,
`review_project_search_binding_v5`, `review_substring_request_v5` and
`review_substring_result_v5`. `TGT-0039` and `TGT-0040` remain mutually
exclusive design alternatives; `TGT-0041` remains design-only. No approved
candidate DDL, writer, bounded reader, substring executor/result API, progress
adapter or client exists.

The story permits isolated disposable-fixture DDL/DML only after owners approve
one immutable common fixture/report root, every benchmark-critical setting, one
prefix target architecture, the executable current and candidate bundles,
independent semantic/state/platform oracles and a complete physical collector.
Presence-only checks found `DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT` plus sixteen explicit
`FORSKA_REVIEW_AUDIT_*` fixture, report, scale, seed, model, provider,
thinking, prompt, Human-mode, content, clock, runtime, collector, sample,
browser and desktop values unset. Source constants, fake-adapter rows, current
project data and live/current databases are not substitutes. Execution stopped
before common-fixture DDL/DML, EXPLAIN/profile, candidate materialization,
server/app/browser/desktop startup, worker execution or polling.

Every same-fixture semantic and physical value below is `unavailable`, never
zero or passed. `auditStatus`, `proofCheckState`,
`recommendationActionability` and `overallCertification` remain independent.
Two new proofs are `blocked`; no target proof, disposition or recommendation
advances.

### Measurement Definitions And Rejection Rules

| Measurement or contract | Required retained evidence for each side | Reject when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IDs, order, scope and signature | Independent expected product ID vectors, standalone token rows, substring result vectors, full tie order, normalized query/filter signature and every project/config/search/scope/title/candidate/snapshot identity. | Set-only equality, omitted/duplicate/reordered ID, signature/scope drift, standalone substitution, mixed revision or unapproved versioned difference. |
| Rows scanned | Applied operator plan plus visited/qualified/returned rows for manifest, token anchor/intersection, candidates/counts/filters, job control, title chunks, result/progress and cleanup, per statement and request total. | Missing operator, raw project/global title/token scan, unbounded residual/probe/sort, inference from returned rows/`LIMIT` or unavailable value. |
| Rows written | Fixture seed; current token build; candidate token/fact/binding build; job/request/chunk/attempt/result/final/visibility/progress rows; retries/conflicts; cleanup, each by table and phase. | All-ID JSON/array/materialization, omitted control/cleanup write, mutable receipt overwrite, unexplained amplification or unavailable value. |
| Canonical output bytes | Database result, persisted token/control/result/receipt and serialized HTTP/client/desktop-bridge bytes under named encoders, separately from database/index/temp files. | Character count/estimate substitution, truncation, omitted state/progress/error, unbounded payload or unavailable value. |
| Temp spill and residue | Per-statement spill plus isolated database/WAL/temp/report pre/peak/post/cleanup inventory with active DuckDB temp root recorded. | Foreground spill, unapproved path, residue, missing checkpoint or unavailable value. |
| RSS | Isolated database/backend/worker/browser/desktop process-tree start/peak/end/delta at fixed cadence for build, foreground prefix, substring execution/poll and cleanup. | Missing child/platform peak, mixed unrelated process, over-budget or unavailable sample. |
| Latency | Approved warm-up/measured sample count and randomized side/cache order; build and foreground/end-to-end p50/p95/p99 plus each failure and async time-to-ready. | Failure removed, warm-side bias, over-budget percentile, endless polling, timeout hidden by retry or weaker rerun. |
| Calls, attempts, states and progress | Logical API/client/poll calls, SQL statements and physical adapter attempts separately; exact async state/count/cursor transitions and terminal visibility. | Source interval/`jobState`/query key substituted for observation, duplicate/unbounded polling, status-only completion, hidden retry/fallback or partial-ready. |
| Settings, cleanup and process stop | Before/after hashes for fixture, both bundles, model/provider/thinking/prompts/content/runtime/platform/collector; artifact inventory, cleanup/restore receipts and every process exit. | Default/downgrade, page/cap/executor change, undisclosed write, incomplete cleanup/restore/process stop or missing hash. |

## US-111 Select-All And Add-To-Project Validation

### US-111 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-110 is complete. US-111 owns exactly three validation grains: client
select-all, add-by-filter and add-by-ID. A displayed total, client selection
flag, normalized filter signature, persisted criteria, worker-selected rows,
project membership writes and visible progress are separate contracts inside
those grains. A successful job admission or selected-row counter is not an
inserted-membership receipt.

Each validation compares exact IDs and order, count unit, normalized signature,
criteria and job identity, strict keyset pages, cardinality/request-byte/call
caps, duplicate behavior, snapshot or current-hydration identity, selected and
written progress, failure/retry/restart/cleanup and actual browser/packaged-
desktop callers. Physical accounting keeps applied rows scanned, job/control/
selection/project/prompt/delta/receipt rows written, canonical output bytes,
temp spill/residue, process-tree RSS, p50/p95/p99 latency, logical calls,
physical attempts and `proofCheckState` separate for current and candidate.

Current HEAD is the US-110 commit
`8019ae80a532545cf5a2f443b99840cb95f59170`. Scoped `src`, `scripts` and
`package.json` source is unchanged from the US-097 target-design commit
`cd197355` through HEAD. Exact product-source searches found zero files for the
`TGT-0049`/`TGT-0057` owner-generation lease, bulk claim, batch receipt, final
manifest and delivery-receipt markers. The targets remain design-only; no
approved candidate DDL, admission adapter, frozen-selection reader, owner-CAS
worker, side-effect receipt, client adapter or cleanup bundle exists.

The story permits isolated disposable-fixture DDL/DML only after owners approve
one immutable common fixture/report root, every benchmark-critical setting,
the executable current and candidate bundles, independent count/selection/
signature/order/duplicate/write/state/platform oracles and a complete physical
collector. Presence-only checks found `DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT` plus sixteen
explicit `FORSKA_REVIEW_AUDIT_*` fixture, report, scale, seed, model, provider,
thinking, prompt, Human-mode, content, clock, runtime, collector, sample,
browser and desktop values unset. Source constants, fake-adapter rows, current
project data and live/current databases are not substitutes. Execution stopped
before common-fixture DDL/DML, EXPLAIN/profile, current or candidate job
materialization, server/app/browser/desktop startup, worker execution, project
writes or polling.

Every same-fixture semantic and physical value below is `unavailable`, never
zero or passed. `auditStatus`, `proofCheckState`,
`recommendationActionability` and `overallCertification` remain independent.
Three new proofs are `blocked`; no target proof, disposition or recommendation
advances.

| Select-all | Four table containers accumulate loaded pages and pass that cumulative ordered ID vector as `currentPageRowIds`. Add later chooses filter mode from the boolean and rebuilds the current filter body. It stores bounded explicit IDs only for add-by-ID; select-all retains criteria/revision plus explicit continuation and never materializes all matching IDs in the foreground. | Exact loaded IDs/order, checkbox/indeterminate/count state, reset behavior, top/bottom controls, filter body/signature and approved selection count equal the independent oracle on both platforms. A mutable post-selection filter/count, cross-snapshot total, all-matching ID array, duplicate/lost loaded ID, implicit order, stale cache, hidden request or setting change fails. |
| Add-by-filter | Route normalizes filters/search, adds a random request ID and admits latest/no-pin `review.bulk.selection`. Each worker page re-resolves active snapshot/search identity, selects distinct `article_id ASC` with strict keyset and limit at most 500, invokes current project/prompt/delta writes, then increments selected progress. Total estimate is null and no request-wide batch/result/byte/call cap exists. | `TGT-0057` freezes criteria and one selection revision under an atomic `TGT-0049` lease. Owner-CAS claims persist a max-500-plus-sentinel batch receipt before cursor advance, including ordered IDs, input/output cursor, side-effect/result counts and checksum. Explicit request-wide pages/rows/bytes/calls/attempts terminate or return continuation; final visibility and cleanup settle separately. | Every mode/filter/search/count case yields the exact ordered oracle once; signature, selection revision, cursors, selected/existing/invalid/inserted/prompt/delta counts and status remain coherent through replay/restart. Cross-batch active-snapshot drift, below-cursor loss, raw/project scan, all-ID materialization, unbounded fan-out, selected-versus-written substitution, stale claimant write, hidden retry/fallback or weaker setting fails. |
| Add-by-ID | Route accepts one string or an array, preserves raw order/duplicates in criteria, reports raw length and enforces at most 5,000 IDs and 1,000,000 stable-JSON bytes. No snapshot or source-project membership is required. Worker sorts non-distinct IDs ascending, applies strict `>` keyset and max 500; writer deduplicates each batch, validates current articles, ignores existing target rows and returns counts the worker discards. | `TGT-0057` keeps the capped caller-supplied ID criteria and an owner-approved normalization/duplicate/order version. ### Measurement Definitions And Rejection Rules

| Measurement or contract | Required retained evidence for each side | Reject when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IDs, order, count and signature | Independent expected loaded/selected/batch/inserted ID vectors; full tie and duplicate-position order; count unit/value; normalized filter/search signature; criteria/job/selection identity and every project/config/component/snapshot revision. | Set-only equality, omitted/duplicate/reordered ID, selected/inserted substitution, raw-count ambiguity, signature drift, mixed revision or unapproved versioned difference. |
| Rows scanned | Applied operator plan plus visited/qualified/returned rows for config/manifest/job, candidate/search/queue/postings, explicit criteria, current article/membership/judgment/prompt reads, status and cleanup, per statement and request total. | Missing operator, raw project/current scan, unbounded prompt/target scan, residual/sort, inference from returned rows/`LIMIT` or unavailable value. |
| Rows written | Fixture seed; current/candidate criteria/claim/batch/final/visibility/cleanup controls; project article, prompt, scope/config delta and receipt rows, each by table and phase with conflict outcomes. | All-matching ID JSON/array, omitted side effect/cleanup write, mutable receipt overwrite, unexplained amplification, selected-count substitution or unavailable value. |
| Canonical output bytes | Persisted criteria/cursor/result/error/receipt, database results, SQL parameters, HTTP/status/client/desktop-bridge bytes under named encoders, separately from database/index/temp files. | Character/estimate substitution, omitted duplicate/state/error/result, unbounded payload, all-ID result map or unavailable value. |
| Temp spill and residue | Per-statement spill plus isolated database/WAL/temp/report pre/peak/post/cleanup inventory with active DuckDB temp root recorded. | Foreground spill, unapproved path, residue, missing checkpoint or unavailable value. |
| RSS | Isolated database/backend/worker/browser/desktop process-tree start/peak/end/delta at fixed cadence for admission, each selection/write batch, polling, restart and cleanup. | Missing child/platform peak, mixed unrelated process, over-budget or unavailable sample. |
| Latency | Approved warm-up/measured sample count and randomized side/cache order; select state/admission/batch/write/end-to-visible p50/p95/p99 plus each failure/restart and time-to-terminal. | Failure removed, warm-side bias, over-budget percentile, endless poll, timeout hidden by retry or weaker rerun. |
| Calls and physical attempts | Logical UI/API/poll/worker/writer calls, SQL statements and underlying adapter attempts separately, including exact page/heartbeat/retry/restart counts. | Query key/source interval substituted for observation, recursive unbounded drain, current initial-plus-three attempts treated as target three attempts, duplicate polling, hidden retry/fallback or unavailable value. |
| Progress, recovery and callers | Selected/valid/existing/invalid/inserted/linked/delta/visible counts; claim owner/generation, cursor in/out, retry, cancel, terminal, cleanup and actual web/desktop request/render/relaunch transitions. | Status-only completion, unfenced stale-owner write, missing batch receipt, partial side-effect replay, selected progress presented as insertion truth, suppressed executor ignored or source-only platform proof. |
| Settings, cleanup and process stop | Before/after hashes for fixture, current/candidate bundles, model/provider/thinking/prompts/content/runtime/platform/collector; artifact/reference inventory, cleanup/restore receipts and every process exit. | Default/downgrade, cap/batch/attempt/worker change, undisclosed write, incomplete cleanup/restore/process stop or missing hash. |

## US-112 PDF Filter, Project And ID Validation

### US-112 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-111 is complete. US-112 owns exactly three validation grains: PDF-by-filter,
PDF-by-project and PDF-by-ID. Persisted selection IDs/order, filter signature,
snapshot pin, remote source attempts, generated file generation/reference,
article and delta publication, aggregate job counters, later runtime-asset
visibility and client behavior are separate contracts inside those grains. A
`succeeded` counter, stable path or HTTP 202 does not prove exact file bytes,
pin protection, cleanup or browser/desktop visibility.

Each validation compares selected, attempted, skipped, missing, failed,
succeeded and file-visible IDs in their exact approved order; normalized
signature and criteria; snapshot and artifact pins; page, request, call,
concurrency, response-byte and file-count caps; generated path/key, length,
checksum and reference; progress, failure/retry/restart, cleanup/restore and
actual browser/packaged-desktop paths. Physical accounting keeps applied rows
scanned, job/article/delta/object/reference/receipt rows written, HTTP and file
output bytes, database/spill/staging/residue bytes, file counts, process-tree
RSS, p50/p95/p99 latency, logical calls, physical attempts and
`proofCheckState` separate for current and candidate.

Current HEAD is the US-111 commit
`df70023d0a783574cc4bd5286e78320252916e63`. Scoped `src`, `scripts` and
`package.json` source is unchanged from the US-098 target-design commit
`4ca6a3de` through HEAD. Exact product-source searches found zero files for ten
`TGT-0049`/`TGT-0057`/`TGT-0070` lease, owner-generation, batch, delivery,
request-cap and content-addressed PDF markers. The targets remain design-only;
no approved candidate DDL, frozen-selection adapter, owner-CAS worker,
bounded source collector, immutable object/reference writer, final/delivery
receipt, runtime gateway adapter or cleanup bundle exists.

The story permits isolated disposable-fixture DDL/DML and generated outputs
only after owners approve one immutable common fixture/report root,
deterministic PDF corpus/source adapter, every benchmark-critical setting,
executable current and candidate bundles, independent selection/file/state/
platform oracles and a complete physical collector. Presence-only checks found
`DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT`, sixteen common `FORSKA_REVIEW_AUDIT_*` fixture,
configuration, collector and platform values, plus explicit PDF corpus, source
profile and asset-root values all unset: 20 values total. Source constants,
fake response bodies, current project data, public network responses and live/
current databases are not substitutes. Execution stopped before common-fixture
DDL/DML, EXPLAIN/profile, current or candidate jobs, remote requests, PDF file
generation, server/app/in-app-browser/desktop startup, worker execution,
polling, cleanup or restore.

Every same-fixture semantic and physical value below is `unavailable`, never
zero or passed. `auditStatus`, `proofCheckState`,
`recommendationActionability` and `overallCertification` remain independent.
Three new proofs are `blocked`; no target proof, disposition or recommendation
advances.

## US-113 Project Export And Transfer Validation

### US-113 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-112 is complete at HEAD
`3f2d1c2bb5dedb8424e0cc9030a98f2dbdd8e1c3`. US-113 owns exactly two
validation grains: project review CSV export and project-transfer package
export/read/clean-target round trip. Prompt-only CSV export remains a separate
route and is not silently counted as either grain. Durable selected IDs,
download-time hydration, streamed or packaged bytes, client save, target
identity mapping and restored visibility remain separate contracts.

The project CSV comparison freezes request fields, source projects, list/filter
criteria, explicit IDs, prompt and metadata columns, selected ID order,
snapshot semantics and pin, result batches, download-time article/prompt/
judgment hydration, exact UTF-8 CSV bytes, checksum, filename, delivery and
actual browser/packaged-desktop behavior. The transfer comparison freezes
project scope, every serialized field and warning, approved redaction/
omission decisions, row/member order, package and asset hashes, inline versus
background routing, session/artifact state, download, import analysis/commit,
source-to-target ID maps, restored visibility, concurrent readers, restart,
cleanup and recovery.

Scoped `src`, `scripts` and `package.json` source is unchanged from the
US-098 target-design commit `4ca6a3de` through HEAD. Exact product-source
searches found zero files for twelve owner-generation, immutable selection,
lease, result-byte, delivery and generated-output candidate markers. The
proposed `TGT-0025`-`TGT-0027`, `TGT-0049`, `TGT-0057`,
`TGT-0071`, `TGT-0074`-`TGT-0076` and `TGT-0079` bundle remains
design-only; no approved candidate DDL, materializer, reader, serializer,
artifact publisher, download lease, import adapter, recovery or cleanup
implementation exists.

The story permits isolated disposable-fixture DDL/DML and generated outputs
only after owners approve one immutable common fixture and report root, every
benchmark-critical value, executable current and candidate bundles,
field-complete export/round-trip/platform oracles and a complete physical
collector. Presence-only checks found `DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT` and nineteen
named `FORSKA_REVIEW_AUDIT_*` fixture, report, scale, seed, model, provider,
thinking, prompt, Human, content, clock, runtime, browser, desktop, collector,
sample, export-oracle, transfer-oracle and artifact-root values all unset: 20
values total. No value was printed, defaulted or weakened.

Execution therefore stopped before common-fixture DDL/DML, EXPLAIN/profile,
current or candidate export jobs, generated CSV/ZIP/assets, server/app/browser/
desktop startup, download, import/commit, restart, cleanup or restore. No live,
current or project DuckDB was inspected. Every same-fixture semantic and
physical value below is `unavailable`, never zero or passed. Two new proof
rows are `blocked`; no target proof, disposition, actionability or
certification state advances.

| CSV hydration | Download-time latest/pinned scopes; first-batch prompt details; per-batch article and judgment queries | Header plus article-ID ascending rows | Current author/raw-source joins can drift from snapshot pieces; prompt metadata absent from the first batch falls back even if present later |
| CSV publication/client | Streaming encoder after header; two hydration reads per 500-ID batch plus first prompt read | HTTP CSV only; filename includes download date; browser target-blank save | No aggregate row/column/cell/byte/call rejection, checksum, retained file, reader/delivery lease, save receipt or client lifecycle |
| Transfer source selection | Current project, date-bounded route/direct scope and current app families | Transactionally staged JSON/NDJSON payload rows | Query-specific deterministic orders exist; DB transaction does not include later asset bytes. Default raw provenance omit and other warning-backed omissions require explicit owner classification |
| Transfer assets/package | Current referenced runtime assets after DB commit; sorted paths; stat before/after and streaming hash | Staged asset files, payload files and directly written final ZIP; manifest fingerprint and archive checksum | Default copy concurrency four. Named resource maxima are not enforced; direct final write has no temp/rename/fsync crash publication receipt |
| Transfer admission/session | Preflight estimates and 64 MiB asset/128 MiB package thresholds | Inline bytes, or queued/assembling/packaging/ready session plus package/manifest/completion/progress files | Thresholds route instead of reject. Files and ready state publish sequentially; session owner token is not an export generation or reader lease |
| Transfer download/client | Ready/unexpired session and current package path | `Bun.file` response headers; Blob/object URL click and immediate revoke | Server has no download lease; client checks content type but not length/hash/fingerprint/save completion. Desktop fully buffers and base64-expands the body |
| Transfer import/recovery | Package guards, manifest/payload/member checks, analysis/plan/dependency reads and target commit | Target rows, promoted assets, history/completion and cleanup state | Clean-target mapping and final product visibility are separate. Stale export work fails and cleans rather than resumes; ready expiry can race a download |

## US-114 Initial Build And Shared-Import Workload Validation

### US-114 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-113 is complete at HEAD
`63f8c3da7326321f176fe45f80247853e11184aa`. US-114 owns exactly two
validation grains: a fresh initial review-serving projection build for one
project and a rank/filter-field update to one existing source record on one
import route shared by a fixed set of projects. The shared-update fixture must
keep canonical article values, source-record key and route membership fixed so
source persistence, project fan-out and projection work can be counted without
silently including the membership-change workload owned by US-115. A zero-
membership then later-membership case remains a required recovery edge, not a
third benchmark grain.

Initial request admission, mutable request/chunk/control state, component
execution, derived-output finalization, candidate promotion, list/count/filter/
queue reads and retention/recovery remain separate contracts. Shared import
source/current-link/hot-field writes, high-water allocation, immutable delta,
reconciliation, project/component dirty fan-out, downstream projection,
snapshot visibility and later reads also remain separate contracts. List row
equality does not substitute for count/facet/option/queue equality, and a
terminal request or reconciled delta does not substitute for bounded recovery
or visible result equality.

Scoped `src`, `scripts` and `package.json` source is unchanged from the US-098
target-design commit `4ca6a3de` through HEAD. Exact product-source searches
found zero files for seventeen candidate revision, owner-generation, frontier,
finalization, output-receipt, head-CAS, lease and retention implementation
markers. The proposed `TGT-0016`, `TGT-0018`-`TGT-0027`,
`TGT-0031`-`TGT-0038`, `TGT-0042`-`TGT-0044` and
`TGT-0046`-`TGT-0053`/`TGT-0058` contracts remain design-only; owners have
not supplied one coherent executable candidate DDL, writer, reader,
finalization, recovery and cleanup bundle.

The story permits isolated disposable-fixture DDL/DML and generated reports
only after owners approve one immutable common fixture, every benchmark-
critical setting, both executable sides, an independent semantic oracle and a
complete physical collector. Presence-only checks found `DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT`
and 25 named `FORSKA_REVIEW_AUDIT_*` fixture/report/temp/project/import-route/
source/scale/seed/model/provider/thinking/prompt/Human/content/clock/runtime/
sample/current-bundle/candidate-bundle/oracle/collector/recovery/retention/cap
values all unset: 26 values total. No value was printed, defaulted or weakened.

Execution therefore stopped before common-fixture DDL/DML, migration,
EXPLAIN/profile, current or candidate build/update, projector/finalizer,
restart, interruption, cleanup or restore. No live, current or project DuckDB
was opened. Every same-fixture semantic and physical value below is
`unavailable`, never zero or passed. Two proof rows are `blocked`; no target,
disposition, actionability or certification state advances.

### Measurement Definitions And Rejection Rules

| Measurement or contract | Required retained evidence for each side and scenario | Reject when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rows written and rewrites | Per statement/table/phase inserted, updated, deleted and conflict-no-op rows; before/after key digests; a rewrite is a write to a pre-existing logical key, and multiple writes to one row are counted separately | Selected/result/counter estimate substitutes for storage mutations; insert/update/delete or repeat writes collapse; unexplained fan-out or any value unavailable |
| Wall time and percentiles | Monotonic admission, each component, finalization, promotion, read, update/intake/publication/recovery/cleanup wall time; approved warm-up/sample count and randomized side/cache order; p50/p95/p99 include failures | Only aggregate job duration, removed failure, warm-side bias, timeout hidden by retry, missing phase/sample or unavailable percentile |
| Logical payload | Canonically encoded input, SQL parameter, stored scalar/JSON, component row, delta/receipt and list/count/filter/queue response bytes, with serializer/version and row counts | Character count, declared estimate, decoded object count or physical file delta substitutes for encoded logical bytes |
| Index/WAL/physical/temp bytes | Database, every index and sidecar, storage-engine WAL, ordinary output/report and active spill/temp roots measured pre/peak/post/cleanup; file identities and hashes retained | Application temp/rename, DuckDB WAL, filesystem journal and ordinary bytes are conflated; missing sidecar/root, foreground spill, residue or unavailable value |
| RSS | Isolated database/backend/worker/finalizer process-tree baseline/peak/end/delta at fixed cadence, including child processes and failure/restart | Process-local only, unrelated processes mixed, OOM, missing peak/sample or unavailable value |
| Retained generations | Counts and byte totals for request/attempt/chunk/component/candidate/active/LKG/failed/pinned/partial/contribution/dirty/ACK/frontier generations before, peak, terminal and post-cleanup | Mutable current row presented as attempt history; failed/partial generations erased; references/leases omitted; unbounded or unavailable value |
| Semantic parity | Independent exact list IDs/order/fields, named counts, facets/options, queue pair/article IDs/order, component/snapshot identity and error/availability envelopes at each checkpoint | Set/count-only equality, ignored HTTP-success error, cross-snapshot values, queue change in rank-only case, source behavior used as oracle or unavailable result |
| Attempts, recovery and cleanup | Logical calls and underlying attempts separately; owner/generation/lease, interruption receipt, finite retry/terminal history, active/LKG outcome, reference scan, bounded cleanup, residue and clean-host restore | Retry/fallback/default, fatal restart, partial promotion, reconciled-but-invisible result, cleanup race, missing restore or unavailable value |
| Settings | Before/after hashes of fixture, source/config/model/provider/thinking/prompt/Human/content, current/candidate bundles, memory/runtime/temp caps, collector, sample/cache/side/retry order | Any default, downgrade, cap/retry change, hidden spill/workaround, unrelated rewrite, incomplete process exit or missing hash |

## US-115 Membership And Project-Article Workload Validation

### US-115 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-114 is complete at HEAD
`ea0af8a8d5b892308a70e3bd8a2fae809092fd4c`. US-115 owns exactly two
validation grains: an accepted pre-judgment-job import-route membership
add/remove through the project edit route, and a direct project-article
add/remove through the project article routes. Each grain includes a newly
effective membership case and an overlap case where effective article
membership remains true while `in_curated_scope` or `in_route_scope`
provenance changes. Idempotent replay, invalid input, protected post-job edit,
boundary cardinality, interruption and cleanup are finite cases inside those
two grains, not additional benchmark scenarios.

Source membership rows, review-change deltas, mutable dirty work, physical
`mart.project_scope_article` flags, selected-import rows, list/count/queue
publication, project-membership reads, durable export selection,
download-time hydration, transfer serialization and recovery/retention are
separate contracts. A successful source transaction, reconciled delta,
projector counter, manifest update, queue ACK or completed export job does not
prove any later state. Exact article IDs, provenance flags, order, fields,
snapshot/component identities and serialized bytes must therefore be checked
independently at every checkpoint.

Scoped `src`, `scripts` and `package.json` source is unchanged from the US-098
target-design commit `4ca6a3de` through HEAD. Exact product-source searches
found zero files for seventeen candidate revision, owner-generation,
frontier, finalization, output-receipt, head-CAS, lease and retention
implementation markers. `TGT-0006`, `TGT-0010`, `TGT-0018`-`TGT-0027`,
`TGT-0031`-`TGT-0038`, `TGT-0042`, `TGT-0044`,
`TGT-0046`-`TGT-0053` and `TGT-0058` remain design-only. No owner supplied one
coherent executable candidate DDL, writer, reader, publication, export,
recovery and cleanup bundle.

The story permits isolated disposable-fixture DDL/DML and generated reports
only after owners approve one immutable fixture, every benchmark-critical
setting, both executable sides, an independent semantic oracle and a complete
physical collector. Presence-only checks found `DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT` and 27
named `FORSKA_REVIEW_AUDIT_*` fixture/report/temp/project/import-route/direct-
article/scale/seed/model/provider/thinking/prompt/Human/content/clock/runtime/
sample/current-bundle/candidate-bundle/oracle/collector/recovery/retention/cap/
export-profile values all unset: 28 values total. No value was printed,
defaulted, inferred from a unit fixture or weakened.

Execution therefore stopped before common-fixture DDL/DML, migration,
EXPLAIN/profile, current or candidate membership mutation, projector,
publication, export, restart, interruption, cleanup or restore. No live,
current or project DuckDB was opened. Every same-fixture semantic and physical
value below is `unavailable`, never zero or passed. Two proof rows are
`blocked`; no target, disposition, actionability or certification state
advances.

| Physical scope | Authoritative route/direct union plus project dates and article rows | Incremental manifest/ACK/watermark only; range rebuild delete/insert physical flags | Effective membership and both provenance flags; incremental acknowledgement versus mandatory rebuild admission/write/validation/promotion |
| Selected/component publication | Physical scope, selected routes/hot facts, active/candidate templates and component state | Mutable selected-import and serving component rows, partial/derived outputs and snapshot state | Scope identity, selected-import snapshot, review config, component revisions and active/LKG/pin histories independently |
| Reads and exports | Project GET, list/count/filter/queue contracts, durable export criteria/result IDs, transfer current-source union | Response rows/envelopes, CSV stream and transfer package/source rows | Exact ID/order/field/zero/error/snapshot equality; durable selection versus later hydration versus current-source transfer serialization |
| Recovery/retention | Source delta, dirty/ACK, request/chunk/component/snapshot/job/pin/reference histories | Retry/readmission, promotion/LKG, cleanup/retention and restore receipts | Logical call versus underlying attempts; immutable owner generation; finite terminal history; reader-safe cleanup and clean-host restoration |

For `PRF-1049`, a one-route change from `N` old routes to `M` new routes
currently executes an all-`N` delete and all-`M` insert; the collector must
measure every physical mutation and count unchanged logical memberships as
rewrites without inferring counts from `N` or `M`. For `PRF-1050`, the route-
overlap removal must prove `in_curated_scope` changes to false while
`in_route_scope` remains true even though current source emits no removal
delta. Neither source observation is assigned a zero physical value.
