### Measurement Definitions And Rejection Rules

| Measurement or contract | Required retained evidence for each side and scenario | Reject when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rows written and rewrites | Per statement/table/phase inserted, updated, deleted and conflict-no-op rows; before/after key digests; unchanged route links deleted/reinserted and repeated writes to one logical key counted separately | Counter/array length/declared fan-out substitutes for mutations; delete/insert collapses to net count; broad selected-route rewrite, unexplained fan-out or unavailable value |
| Wall time and percentiles | Monotonic source, intake, each component, finalization, promotion, project/list/count/queue read, export selection/hydration/transfer, recovery/cleanup time; approved warm-up/sample count and randomized side/cache order; p50/p95/p99 include failures | Aggregate job duration only, hidden wait/retry, warm-side bias, missing phase/sample or unavailable percentile |
| Logical payload | Canonically encoded request JSON, SQL parameters/statements, stored scalar/JSON, delta/dirty/component rows and every response/CSV/transfer manifest/package byte, with serializer/version and row count | Character/object count, estimate or physical file delta substitutes for encoded logical bytes; open JSON, repeated SQL or output omitted |
| Index/WAL/physical/temp bytes | Database, every index/sidecar, storage-engine WAL, output/report/package and active spill/temp roots pre/peak/post/cleanup; exact paths, identities and hashes | DuckDB WAL, application temp/rename, ordinary files and filesystem journal are conflated; missing root/sidecar, any spill, residue or unavailable value |
| RSS | Isolated database/backend/worker/export process-tree baseline/peak/end/delta at fixed cadence, including children and failure/restart | Process-local only, unrelated process mixed, missing peak/sample, OOM, fatal restart or unavailable value |
| Retained generations | Source delta, dirty/ACK, request/attempt/chunk, scope/selected/component, candidate/active/LKG/failed/pinned, export result and cleanup generation counts/bytes before, peak, terminal and post-cleanup | Mutable current row presented as history; membership generation reused; failed/partial/output/pin state erased; unbounded or unavailable value |
| Semantic parity | Independent exact source rows, physical flags, selected winner, list IDs/order/fields, named counts, queue pair/article IDs/order, snapshot/component tuple, project GET, CSV and transfer bytes at every checkpoint | Effective set hides provenance mismatch; set/count-only equality; ignored error; mixed snapshot; current source used as oracle; any mismatch or unavailable result |
| Attempts, recovery and cleanup | Logical calls and underlying attempts separately; owner/generation/lease, interruption receipt, finite retry/terminal history, active/LKG result, reference scan, bounded cleanup, residue and clean-host restore | Retry/fallback/default, reconciled-but-unpublished scope, stale-owner write, fatal restart, partial promotion/export, cleanup race, missing restore or unavailable value |
| Settings and bounds | Before/after hashes of fixture, route/direct identities, config/model/provider/thinking/prompt/Human/content, bundles, collector, runtime/memory/temp caps, samples/cache/side/retry/export order; explicit per-call and request-wide row/byte/call ceilings | Default, downgrade, cap/retry change, hidden workaround, unbounded request/fan-out/recovery, broad rewrite, unrelated mutation, incomplete process exit or missing hash |

Any OOM, foreground or background spill, fatal restart, retry, fallback,
broad selected-route rewrite, request-wide unbounded work, physical/semantic
mismatch, partial visibility, stale provenance, unbounded recovery, residue or
weaker benchmark-critical setting rejects the applicable side. A rejected
current run is retained as failure evidence and is never rerun under different
settings. Candidate agreement with a current defect is not parity.

## US-116 Article Metadata And Payload-Update Workload Validation

### US-116 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-115 is complete at HEAD
`524d48d0c81abdbc1cef5b95adecdd863834084e`. US-116 owns exactly two
validation grains: a same-route, same-source-record-key reimport that changes
routine article metadata while retaining the canonical article identity, and
a user PDF replacement followed by full-text conversion for the same article.
No-op replay, field-at-a-time and combined changes, reference/no-reference,
membership/no-membership, boundary cardinality, invalid input, interruption,
restart and cleanup are finite cases within those grains, not extra benchmark
scenarios.

Route acceptance, canonical article mutation, identifier state, selected
source/current-link and hot-fact mutation, review-change deltas, dirty work,
component-local writes, derived-output finalization, snapshot promotion, list
display, filters, detail hydration, CSV selection/hydration, transfer
serialization, generated files, client visibility and recovery are separate
contracts. A response count, source hash change, completed component, active
snapshot, ready file or successful download cannot substitute for another
state.

US-098 target-design commit `4ca6a3de` through HEAD. Exact product-source

### US-116 Measurement And Rejection Rules

| --- | --- | --- |
| Row mutations | Per statement/table inserted, updated, deleted, conflict/no-op and rewritten row identities; old/new canonical/source/component values | Accepted/succeeded count, planned batch size, delta count or projector counter |
| File mutations | Per rooted path created, opened, overwritten, renamed, deleted and retained; before/after bytes, cryptographic digest, inode/reference and generation | A stored path, successful `writeFile`, package checksum or absence after cleanup |
| Logical payload | Canonical UTF-8/JSON/PDF input, normalized metadata, converter input/output, response/CSV/transfer/package bytes by serializer | Character count, SQL `LENGTH`, preview size or file-system allocation |
| Engine and filesystem bytes | Every named index, storage-engine WAL, database, DuckDB temp, application temp, report, source file, generated file and client output before/peak/after/cleanup | Application file write as engine WAL; source absence as zero bytes; database delta as index bytes |
| Memory and time | Process-tree RSS baseline/peak/end/delta; monotonic phase wall time and p50/p95/p99 for approved samples/order | Heap-only sample, one aggregate duration, timeout constant or successful response time |
| Generations and attempts | Canonical/source/file/payload/component/snapshot/head/pin/export/retention generations; logical call and every underlying attempt with owner/lease | Mutable current status, retry wrapper count, latest active ID or retained row count alone |
| Semantic parity | Field/order/identity/availability/error equality at canonical, source, list, filter, detail, export, transfer, asset and recovery checkpoints | HTTP 2xx, nonempty row, checksum of omitted fields, active status or candidate agreement with a current defect |
| Settings and bounds | Before/after hashes of fixture/corpus/config/model/provider/thinking/prompts/content/bundles/converter/collector/runtime caps/order/retry/recovery/retention/platform profiles | Resolver default, changed cap/retry, fallback, inferred fixture value or hidden workaround |

Any OOM, foreground or background spill, fatal restart, retry, fallback,
broad rewrite, unbounded request/recursive work, physical or semantic mismatch,
partial file/row visibility, stale snapshot, missing asset, unbounded recovery,
residue or weaker benchmark-critical setting rejects the applicable side. A
rejected current run must be retained as failure evidence and cannot be rerun
under different settings. Candidate agreement with a current defect is not
parity.

## US-117 LLM Judgment Create, Update And Delete Workload Validation

### US-117 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-116 is complete at HEAD
`b1d0c52e88e5e816d34db21d8b07ff45436d17ff`. US-117 owns exactly three
validation grains: one LLM judgment create, one LLM judgment update and one
LLM judgment delete. Fresh, duplicate, conflicting, inactive-generation,
shared-project, boundary-cardinality, interruption, restart and cleanup cases
are finite cases inside those grains, not additional scenarios.

The active seven-dimension model/content identity, physical
`delete_generation`, canonical judgment ID, job-local outbox identity, import
marker, source delta, project fan-out, write overlay, dirty work, component
output, derived finalization, serving snapshot, list/count/filter/detail/queue
read, export/transfer result and recovery receipt are separate contracts. A
canonical row, accepted outbox entry, delta count, component counter, active
snapshot, export status or checksum cannot certify another grain. Persisted
job status, source-change kind, dirty claim state, projector progress and
visible result state remain distinct.

Scoped `src`, `scripts` and `package.json` product source is unchanged from the
US-098 target-design commit `4ca6a3de` through HEAD. Exact product-source
searches found zero files for seventeen candidate markers:
`review_component_revision_v5`, `review_serving_snapshot_v5`,
`review_serving_snapshot_head_v5`, `review_snapshot_lease_v5`,
`review_source_event_v5`, `review_source_frontier_v5`,
`review_dirty_work_v5`, `review_dirty_output_receipt_v5`,
`review_dirty_ack_lane_v5`, `review_consumer_frontier_v5`,
`review_overlay_event_v5`, `review_llm_status_component_v5`,
`review_judgment_payload_component_v5`, `review_queue_item_v5`,
`review_named_count_component_v5`, `review_filter_posting_component_v5` and
`retention_policy_v5`. Linked `TGT-0011`, `TGT-0018`, `TGT-0022`,
`TGT-0024`-`TGT-0027`, `TGT-0031`-`TGT-0038`, `TGT-0042`-`TGT-0044` and
`TGT-0046`-`TGT-0058` remain design-only. No owner supplied one coherent
executable canonical/component/event/overlay/job/head/lease/retention
candidate or applied path.

The story permits isolated disposable-fixture DDL/DML and generated output
only after owners approve one immutable fixture, every benchmark-critical
identity and setting, both executable sides, an independent oracle and a

restart, retry, fallback, broad invalidation/rewrite, unbounded input/read-all or
recovery, physical or semantic mismatch, inactive-row reuse, partial
publication, stale snapshot, residue or weaker benchmark-critical setting

evidence and cannot be rerun under changed settings. Candidate agreement with
a current defect is not parity.

## US-118 Human Judgment Submit, Move And Delete Workload Validation

### US-118 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-117 is complete at HEAD
`d86b30007e5ca1a444b074c4d84cc55f24534bab`. US-118 owns exactly three
validation grains: one prompt-mode Human judgment submit, one prompt-merge
Human judgment move and one Covidence-reimport Human judgment delete. Required,
optional-blank, prompt-drift, collision, prompt/summary, reseed, boundary,
interruption, restart and cleanup cases are finite cases inside those grains,
not additional scenarios. Project-prompt cleanup, pending-row cleanup and merge
collision deletion are writer variants inside the delete proof; they do not
create extra proof rows.

The pending-row identity, answered state, answer/comment payload, old and new
prompt identities, physically deleted row, source-operation tombstone, reviewer
overlay, comparison invalidation, dirty work, component output, derived
finalization, serving snapshot, Human/Both/Unassessed membership, exact count,
conflict, queue, detail, CSV/transfer result and recovery receipt are separate
contracts. A returned `updated` or `deletedHumanPromptAnswers` count, source
delta, overlay row, stale comparison generation, component counter, active
snapshot, export status or package checksum cannot certify another grain.
`auditStatus`, `proofCheckState`, `recommendationActionability` and
`overallCertification` remain independent.

Scoped `src`, `scripts` and `package.json` product source is unchanged from the
US-098 target-design commit `4ca6a3de` through HEAD. Exact product-source
searches found zero files for seventeen candidate markers:

| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity and row mutations | Per statement/table inserted, updated, deleted, conflict/no-op and rewritten row identities with before/after values; pending/Human/project-prompt/comparison/delta/overlay/dirty/component/snapshot rows | Requested/submitted/imported/succeeded/deleted count, planned batch, source delta count or projector counter |
| Logical payload | Canonical UTF-8/JSON bytes for submit answers/comments, keep/merge/delete/reseed criteria, delta/overlay/dirty/result and CSV/transfer serializers | Character count, SQL `LENGTH`, row count, preview bytes or checksum omitting fields |
| Engine and filesystem bytes | Every named index, storage-engine WAL, database, DuckDB temp, application temp, report, export/package and client output before/peak/after/cleanup | Source absence as zero; ordinary file as engine WAL; database growth as index bytes |
| Memory and time | Process-tree RSS baseline/peak/end/delta; monotonic phase wall time and p50/p95/p99 for approved samples/order | Heap-only sample, timeout constant, one aggregate duration or HTTP success time |
| Invalidation and generations | Exact source HWM, project/comparison fan-out, overlay identity/status, component-local rows/bytes/checksums, finalization, immutable attempts, snapshot/head/lease/export/retention generations | Registry component list, dirty ACK, stale generation, active snapshot ID or retained row count alone |
| Calls, attempts and recovery | Every logical call and transitive physical attempt, claim/owner/lease, failure/restart/cleanup/restore receipt | Wrapper retry constant, mutable status, terminal counter or in-process `finally` |
| Semantic parity | Identity/field/order/count/availability/error equality at overlay, Human, Both, Unassessed, count, conflict, queue, detail, snapshot, CSV, transfer and recovery checkpoints | HTTP 2xx, property presence, nonempty result, final reseed, stale snapshot or candidate agreement with a current defect |
| Settings and bounds | Before/after hashes of fixture/config/model/provider/thinking/prompts/content/payloads/bundles/collector/runtime/order/retry/recovery/retention/platform profiles | Resolver default, fallback, changed cap/retry, inferred fixture value or hidden workaround |

Any missing identity dimension, OOM, foreground or background spill, fatal
restart, retry, fallback, broad invalidation/rewrite, unbounded input/read-all or
recovery, physical or semantic mismatch, partial publication, stale snapshot,
residue or weaker benchmark-critical setting rejects the applicable side. A
rejected run must be retained as failure evidence and cannot be rerun under
changed settings. Candidate agreement with a current defect is not parity.

## US-119 Prompt, Model And Content-Setting Workload Validation

### US-119 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-118 is complete at HEAD
`33bb843fc9aba1e3c4114d9287168ffde2f5c103`. US-119 owns exactly three
validation grains: one semantic replacement of one active project prompt, one
ordinary selected-model change and one valid four-flag content-setting vector
change. No-op, invalid, existing-job, shared-judgment, provider/model
execution-identity, boundary, interruption, restart and cleanup cases are
finite cases inside those grains, not additional scenarios.

Current project settings, immutable prompt/link identity, model/provider
execution identity, active judgment natural identity, execution snapshot,
review-config hash, selected-import identity, dirty scope, component output,
derived finalization, serving snapshot, comparison staleness, transfer dirty
tokens, list/count/filter/queue result and recovery receipt are separate
contracts. A source-row update, changed-field set, accepted delta, dirty ACK,
component count, active snapshot, current-hash lookup, export result or transfer
package cannot certify another grain. `auditStatus`, `proofCheckState`,
`recommendationActionability` and `overallCertification` remain independent.

Scoped `src`, `scripts` and `package.json` product source is unchanged from the
US-098 target-design commit
`4ca6a3de229a949ef2662affd1d83127b708df51` through HEAD. Exact
product-source searches found zero files for eighteen candidate markers:
`review_config_receipt_v1`, `review_component_revision_v5`,
`review_serving_snapshot_v5`, `review_serving_snapshot_head_v5`,
`review_snapshot_lease_v5`, `review_source_event_v5`,
`review_source_frontier_v5`, `review_dirty_work_v5`,
`review_dirty_output_receipt_v5`, `review_dirty_ack_lane_v5`,
`review_consumer_frontier_v5`, `review_overlay_event_v5`,
`review_human_status_component_v5`, `review_judgment_payload_component_v5`,
`review_queue_item_v5`, `review_named_count_component_v5`,
`review_filter_posting_component_v5` and `retention_policy_v5`. Linked
`TGT-0005`, `TGT-0008`-`TGT-0011`, `TGT-0018`-`TGT-0038`,
`TGT-0042`-`TGT-0044` and `TGT-0046`-`TGT-0058` remain design-only. No

The story permits isolated disposable-fixture DDL/DML and generated output only
after owners approve one immutable fixture, every benchmark-critical identity
and setting, both executable sides, an independent oracle and a complete

### US-119 Measurement And Rejection Rules

- Every side records fixture, source commit, bundle/schema/serializer/oracle/
  collector hashes, project/article/prompt/model/provider/execution/content/
  review/selected-import/component/snapshot identities, frozen clock, memory/
  runtime/platform/retry/request/recovery/retention settings and raw-report
  checksum. Missing or changed dimensions reject the side.
- Rows are distinct per table and operation: selected, inserted, updated,
  deleted, conflict, duplicate/no-op, invalidated, dirty, acknowledged,
  rewritten, finalized, promoted, retained and cleaned. A changed-field list,
  accepted delta or aggregate counter is never substituted for physical rows.
- Record total and phase wall time plus p50/p95/p99; canonical encoded logical
  payload; each declared index delta; storage-engine WAL, database, sibling
  DuckDB temp, report and output bytes separately; process-tree baseline/peak/
  delta RSS; retained config, judgment, component and snapshot generations;
  logical calls and transitive physical attempts.
- The applicable proof rejects a silent default, fallback, retry, downgrade,
  changed unrelated setting, unbounded request/read/write/replay, OOM, fatal
  restart, any spill, broad unrelated invalidation/rewrite, missing old/new
  identity, incomplete component/finalization/promotion, list/count/filter/
  queue/snapshot/comparison/transfer mismatch, orphan/residue, failed restore
  or unavailable required measurement.
- `proofCheckState` is evaluated only after both sides and the independent
  oracle complete. HTTP success, source-only findings, unit-test success or
  current-versus-candidate agreement cannot change it.

## US-120 Date-Range, Project-Scope And Selected-Route Workload Validation

### US-120 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-119 is complete at HEAD
`6ea41e5ebb395fff801a0d61c83c872fad1472f0`. US-120 owns exactly three
validation grains: one pre-job project date-range change, one direct
project-scope membership/provenance change and one pre-job selected
import-route-set change. Null, equal, inclusive-boundary, inverted, no-op,
invalid route, direct/route overlap, one/many, interruption, restart and
cleanup cases are finite cases inside those grains, not additional scenarios.

Typed project dates, direct project-article membership, selected project-route
membership, current article-route links, effective logical scope, physical
scope rows, selected-import winner/base, review-config hash, source
watermarks, component state, serving snapshot, durable export selection,
download-time hydration and transfer-time current-source scope are separate
contracts. A successful edit, source link, accepted delta, dirty ACK,
component status, snapshot, count, export job or transfer package cannot
certify another grain. `auditStatus`, `proofCheckState`,
`recommendationActionability` and `overallCertification` remain independent.

US-098 target-design commit

Each scenario still requires exact candidate membership, filters, counts,
queues, snapshots, export and recovery parity before its proof can advance.

### US-120 Current Write, Identity And Read Inventory

| Contract | Current source-observed behavior | Proof boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Date admission | Date-only input becomes UTC midnight; same-bound replay is a no-op; any judgment job rejects changed dates; only two simultaneously supplied bounds are ordered together. | Acceptance cannot prove the stored old/new pair is valid against an omitted bound, or that every consumer uses the same inclusive upper-bound semantics. |
| Direct scope source | Direct add is conflict-safe and emits one delta per returned link. Remove emits no delta when a selected route still covers the article. | Effective membership can remain true while curated provenance changes; absent delta is not a no-write or published-provenance receipt. |
| Selected route source | Set equality ignores order, blanks and duplicates. A changed set deletes all existing links, resolves submitted routes, then inserts every selected route with fresh UUIDs. | One logical add/remove can rewrite unrelated unchanged links; a config delta or route count cannot reveal deletes, inserts or preserved identity. |
| Invalidation and dirty work | Date/route config deltas request ten project-scoped components; direct source deltas request nine article-scoped components. Dirty work is mutable per component/scope and ACK is separate. | Registry vectors are not physical rows; zero overlap delta, duplicate dirty upsert and later full rebuild must be measured independently. |
| Physical project scope | Incremental runner publishes control only. Range rebuild deletes/inserts direct-plus-route membership with archive and date predicates and validates count/checksum. | ACK and component status do not prove mandatory physical mutation, provenance flags, full old-range tombstones or atomic request-wide publication. |
| Selected import | Winner projection reads physical scope and current route/hot facts. Its ID omits date/route/direct/review-change dimensions and base state can be reset/reused. | Deterministic current winner and completed header do not freeze membership across snapshots or protect old pinned exports. |
| Lists, filters and counts | Mounted modes resolve serving manifests/components separately; separate count calls, filter facets/options and client requests can bind different observations. | ID/set/count equality alone cannot prove order, cursors, fields, legitimate zero, errors, selected values or browser/desktop visibility. |
| Queues | Serving count/preview combine snapshot rows with current date/route/direct predicates; refill and judgment reuse consult current source scope and local queue state. | Queue article count, prompt-pair rows, durable ready rows and claim-time execution snapshots are different grains and can straddle a scope edit. |
| Snapshots and recovery | Review hash omits dates/routes; source watermarks can create another snapshot ID while scope/selected identities are reused. Chunk, finalization, promotion, active/LKG/pin and retention states fail independently. | Same current hash, completed chunks or active snapshot cannot prove new membership, immutable generations, bounded retry or cleanup. |
| Export and transfer | Export freezes a durable selected ID result but later resolves/hydrates serving data. Transfer independently recomputes current source scope and serializes current settings/routes/links. | Selection, hydration, generated bytes, transfer rows, pins, concurrent readers, cleanup and clean-host restore require separate exact receipts. |

| `PRF-1062` | Null-to-start/end/both; clear one/both; equal instant; inclusive start/end article; just outside each bound; date-only and timed upper bound; partial edit against stored opposite bound; inverted pair; identical replay; zero/one/many/approved maximum scoped articles; interruption after source update/delta/reconcile/scope/each component/finalization/promotion/export/cleanup; restart and restore | Old/new typed values and source version; accepted/rejected/no-op write set; physical IDs and curated/route flags; selected winners; exact requested/physical component rows; list IDs/order/fields; filters/options; exact counts; queue article/pairs/order; snapshot/component tuple; CSV and transfer bytes; restored equality |
| `PRF-1063` | Add/remove/replay one direct link; new-effective article; route-overlap and multiple-route overlap; missing link; in/out date boundary; zero/one/many/approved maximum fan-out; interruption after link/delta/reconcile/scope/each component/finalization/promotion/export/cleanup; restart and restore | Exact direct link/provenance and emitted-or-absent event; physical curated/route flags; selected winner/tombstone; nine requested versus physical component rows; candidate/filter/count/queue/snapshot/export/transfer values; bounded calls/work and restoration |
| `PRF-1064` | Empty/one/many/approved maximum old/new sets; add/remove/replace/identical replay; invalid/blank/duplicate routes; unchanged-link preservation; route-only and direct-overlap articles; equal selected ranks; before-job admission and after-job rejection; interruption after project update/all-link delete/insert/delta/reconcile/scope/each component/finalization/promotion/export/cleanup; restart and restore | Exact old/new project-route IDs/values and rewrite evidence; route-set/config receipt; ten requested versus physical component rows; physical flags and selected winner; list/filter/count/queue/snapshot/CSV/transfer values; protected/no-op zero-write proof and restoration |

- Every side records fixture/source commit, bundle/schema/serializer/oracle/
  collector hashes, old/new source/config/scope/route/selected/component/
  snapshot identities, frozen clock, memory/runtime/platform/retry/request/
  recovery/retention/export settings and raw-report checksum. Missing or
  changed dimensions reject the side.
- Rows are distinct per table and operation: selected, inserted, updated,
  deleted, conflict, duplicate/no-op, invalidated, dirty, acknowledged,
  rewritten, finalized, promoted, retained and cleaned. Source-observed
  `10/9/10` component vectors are declarations, never physical counts.
- Record total and phase wall time plus p50/p95/p99; canonical encoded logical
  payload; each declared index delta; storage-engine WAL, database, sibling
  DuckDB temp, report and output bytes separately; process-tree baseline/peak/
  end/delta RSS; retained source, scope, selected, component, snapshot and
  export generations; logical calls and transitive physical attempts.
- The applicable proof rejects a silent default, fallback, retry, downgrade,
  changed unrelated setting, unbounded request/read/write or unbounded replay,
  OOM, fatal restart, any spill, broad unrelated invalidation/rewrite, missing
  old/new
  identity, date-boundary disagreement, stale provenance, incomplete
  finalization/promotion, candidate/filter/count/queue/snapshot/export/
  transfer mismatch, orphan/residue, failed restore or unavailable required
  measurement.
- `proofCheckState` is evaluated only after both sides and the independent
  oracle complete. HTTP success, source-only findings, unit-test success,
  source-declared component count or current-versus-candidate agreement cannot
  change it.

## US-121 Article Deletion, Project Deletion And Archive Workload Validation

### US-121 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-120 is complete at HEAD
`6a635ef7786cf493c128e2be3448b23c2c0a43d7`. US-121 owns exactly three
product lifecycle grains:

1. mounted canonical article deletion through `DELETE /api/articles/:id`;
2. mounted project soft archive through `DELETE /api/projects/:id`, deletion
   admission through `POST /api/projects/delete-archived`, and operator-driven
   permanent cleanup through
   `db:duck:run-archived-project-bounded-cleanup`; and
3. mounted data-source archive through `DELETE /api/datasources/:id`.

Project archive is an admission checkpoint inside permanent project deletion,
not the third archive grain. Data-source archive is independently observable
through active/archived/detail/import-route/import-handler state. Article
identity, article references, source/current links, project membership,
serving snapshots, active/last-known-good/pinned generations, export
selection, later hydration, transfer serialization, generated files,
authoritative state, audit/replay evidence and recovery receipts remain
separate contracts. A route success, changed flag, tombstone, deleted-row
counter, job status, checksum or file existence cannot certify another
contract.

Scoped `src`, `scripts` and `package.json` product source is unchanged from the
US-098 target-design commit
`4ca6a3de229a949ef2662affd1d83127b708df51` through HEAD. Exact
product-source searches found zero files for 20 candidate markers:
`review_config_receipt_v1`, `review_component_revision_v5`,
`review_serving_snapshot_v5`, `review_serving_snapshot_head_v5`,
`review_snapshot_lease_v5`, `review_source_event_v5`,

| Project archive | Mounted delete flips the archive flag, emits a config delta and drains jobs. | Soft archive does not prove permanent deletion admission, snapshot/file preservation or bounded cleanup. |
| Project deletion admission | Tombstone request requires an archived project and drains jobs, but leaves `delete_pending_at` null. | Tombstone and column are separate route gates; ordinary routes and transfer can disagree during cleanup. |
| Project cleanup | One mutation/table/batch is bounded, but total invocation ends at 100 batches. Lists focus on legacy/runtime/source rows and omit current V4/snapshot/pin/export/transfer/file closure. | Local row/batch caps do not prove complete bounded cleanup, preservation or no orphaned families. Requiring more work remains nonterminal. |
| Project terminal state | Final transaction deletes tombstone and project; service retains no completed tombstone/attempt/output receipt. Zero-row tombstone cleanup may be reported complete. | Missing control state cannot prove deletion, retained audit, restore, cleanup schedule or terminal no-residue state. |
| Data-source archive | One transaction changes the source archive flag. Active/archived lists diverge, detail remains readable, routes remain independently active and direct handlers can reuse the archived source. | Accepted archive cannot prove import rejection, current-link/membership invalidation, snapshot/export parity or file/reference lifecycle. |

## US-122 Snapshot Retirement, Pin Protection And Last-Known-Good Retention Validation

### US-122 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-121 is complete at HEAD
`f2105e683d86c9792a06af9168ec421a1935ac83`. US-122 owns exactly three
snapshot-lifecycle grains:

1. promotion-driven retirement of the current active snapshot and later
   retirement/cleanup eligibility of older generations;
2. protection of one explicitly pinned active snapshot across promotion,
   bulk/export work, terminal job state, expiry and cleanup; and
3. retention and exact fallback behavior of the last-known-good snapshot
   across failed candidates, later promotions, missing active state, restart
   and cleanup.

Candidate snapshot status, the candidate implementation side, active status,
the persisted LKG pointer, route fallback selection, explicit pin rows,
retired manifest rows, serving data, selected-import header/base rows, bulk
job state, export selection, download hydration, cleanup eligibility and
recovery remain separate contracts. A promotion transaction, active-pin
predicate, stale read, completed job, cleanup invocation or retained manifest
cannot certify another contract.

Scoped `src`, `scripts` and `package.json` product source is unchanged from the
US-098 target-design commit
`4ca6a3de229a949ef2662affd1d83127b708df51` through HEAD. Exact
product-source searches found zero files for 12 candidate markers:
`review_component_revision_v5`, `review_selected_import_revision_v5`,
`review_serving_snapshot_v5`, `review_serving_snapshot_component_v5`,
`review_serving_snapshot_head_v5`, `review_snapshot_lease_v5`,
`review_snapshot_lease_receipt_v5`, `review_bulk_job_claim_v5`,
`review_bulk_batch_receipt_v5`, `retention_policy_v5`,
`retention_step_receipt_v5` and `retention_reference_v5`. The linked
`TGT-0048`, `TGT-0049`, `TGT-0057` and `TGT-0058` designs remain unimplemented
and unapplied.

The story permits disposable-fixture DDL and DML only after owners approve one
immutable fixture, all critical identities/settings, both executable sides,
an independent lifecycle oracle, a complete physical collector, budgets and
cleanup authority. A presence-only check printed no values and found `set=0`,
`unset=62`, `total=62` for:

## US-123 Delta, Dirty-Work And Rebuild-Partial Cleanup Validation

### US-123 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-122 is complete at HEAD
`d4bff7d300bb2bc7c92825c39428503ef7b8b91f`. US-123 owns exactly three
intermediate-state cleanup grains:

1. cleanup of reconciled current review/import delta rows only below an
   explicit minimum watermark for every later consumer;
2. cleanup or compaction of completed dirty-work and acknowledgement state
   only after output and snapshot visibility are proved; and
3. cleanup of contribution, source-summary, accumulator and other rebuild
   partials only after owner-fenced finalization, exact publication and
   retained repair/replay needs are settled.

Source high-water allocation, delta persistence, `reconciled_at`, dirty
admission, dirty claim/completion, point ACK, compacted-through ACK,
projector watermark, projection-input watermark, component output,
request/chunk terminal state, derived-output finalization, snapshot
visibility, active/LKG retention, exact reads, replay, repair, physical
deletion and terminal cleanup receipt remain separate contracts. A reconciled
delta, completed dirty row, compacted ACK, completed chunk, published count,
request status, active snapshot or successful cleanup invocation cannot
certify another contract.

Scoped `src`, `scripts` and `package.json` product source is unchanged from the
US-098 target-design commit
`4ca6a3de229a949ef2662affd1d83127b708df51` through HEAD. Exact
product-source searches found zero files for 14 candidate markers:
`review_source_event_v5`, `review_source_frontier_v5`,
`review_dirty_work_v5`, `review_dirty_output_receipt_v5`,
`review_dirty_ack_lane_v5`, `review_consumer_frontier_v5`,

`review_serving_snapshot_head_v5`, `review_rebuild_plan_v5`,
`review_rebuild_chunk_attempt_v5`, `review_rebuild_finalization_v5`,
`retention_policy_v5` and `retention_step_receipt_v5`. The linked
`TGT-0046`, `TGT-0048`, `TGT-0050`-`TGT-0053` and `TGT-0058` designs remain
unimplemented and unapplied.

The story permits disposable-fixture DDL and DML only after owners approve one

## US-124 Orphan, Generated-File And Retention-Boundary Cleanup Validation

### US-124 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-123 is complete at HEAD
`e19450b474f4929d5586f9b8c5aaaa89ea850092`. US-124 owns exactly three
lifecycle cleanup grains:

1. current and candidate orphan-generation cleanup, including active, LKG,
   pinned, candidate, failed, retired and unreferenced generations;
2. current and candidate generated or partial-file cleanup, including upload,
   build, package, manifest, completion, progress, promoted, recovery, backup
   and client-delivery boundaries; and
3. exact retention-boundary cleanup at one tick before, exactly at and one tick
   after every applicable pin, export, transfer, terminal-history, generated-
   file and recovery cutoff.

Manifest status, active-head selection, persisted LKG, comparison active
generation, candidate attempt, pin/ref count/expiry, job/export/transfer
ownership, ordinary reader/download lease, artifact publication, file
existence/checksum, recovery/backup reference, terminal history, cleanup
eligibility, physical deletion and durable cleanup receipt remain separate
contracts. A successful promotion, ready package, terminal session, expired
timestamp, removed root or returned row count cannot certify any other
contract.

Scoped `src`, `scripts`, `package.json` and `bun.lock` product source is
unchanged from the US-098 target-design commit
`4ca6a3de229a949ef2662affd1d83127b708df51` through HEAD. The engine-owned
`tasks/prd.json` modification pre-existed and remains untouched. Exact
product-source searches found zero files for 18 candidate markers:
`review_component_revision_v5`, `review_serving_snapshot_v5`,
`review_serving_snapshot_head_v5`, `review_snapshot_lease_v5`,
`retention_policy_v5`, `retention_step_receipt_v5`,

Measurements remain separate:

- Row evidence records each table, natural identity, owner generation, status,
  cutoff, before/after count, removed identities and retained identities.
- File evidence records each rooted relative path, object/reference/manifest
  identity, owner, generation, checksum, encoded bytes and removed/retained
  decision. Root deletion count is not a file count.
- Time records total and named phases plus retained raw per-case samples;
  percentiles require an owner-approved sample count and are never inferred
  from unit-test duration.
- Storage-engine WAL, ordinary-file publication/rename, filesystem behavior,
  sibling DuckDB temp baseline/peak/end/delta/events, process-tree RSS
  baseline/peak/end, calls/attempts and cleanup cursors remain independent.
- Generations record comparison active/staged/failed/removed, review
  candidate/active/LKG/pinned/retired/failed, transfer owner/revision/package/
  download, backup/recovery and cleanup policy/cycle/step identities.

Reject a side immediately for a missing or changed critical setting, missing
owner, missing measurement, inferred/default cutoff, unknown reference,
unbounded directory or history scan, unreceipted recursive delete, current-
only substitution, retry/fallback/downgrade, mixed generation, partial
publication, deleted active/LKG/pinned/export/transfer/reader/recovery file,
checksum drift, indefinite history, spill, OOM, fatal restart, residue or
failed restore. Preserve the failure; never weaken settings or relabel an
unavailable value zero or passed.

## US-125 Interrupted Rebuild And Incremental Projection Validation

### US-125 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-124 is complete at HEAD
`b17a78e1f130cc4812e222c8d7800c163f351ca4`. US-125 owns exactly two
interruption grains:

1. current and candidate interrupted full rebuild, from admission through
   chunks, output, derived finalization, promotion, restart and cleanup; and
2. current and candidate interrupted incremental projection, from dirty
   intake/claim through per-component and per-snapshot writes, ACK, watermarks,
   restart and cleanup.

output, chunk completion, derived finalization, promotion, active head,

separate contracts. A completed chunk, ACK, advanced watermark, successful
promotion, active read, LKG read or cleanup invocation cannot certify another
grain.

Measurements remain separate:

- Row evidence records table, natural identity, snapshot/component generation,
  statement kind, inserted/updated/deleted/conflict/no-op result, before/after
  value and duplicate-effect classification.
- Rebuild state records plan/request, chunk/range/split, claim
  owner/generation/lease, input/output digest, attempt, validation,
  finalization, promotion, active/LKG and cleanup receipt identities.
- Incremental state records dirty range/work/owner, ACK, component manifest,
  snapshot-state copy and source/input/projector/consumer-visible watermark
  values before interruption, after restart and after convergence.
- Time records monotonic total and named phases with retained raw samples.
  Unit-test duration is not workload wall time.
- Storage-engine WAL, ordinary output files, sibling DuckDB temp
  baseline/peak/end/delta/events, process-tree RSS baseline/peak/end/delta,
  calls/attempts, pins, retained generations and cleanup cursors remain
  independent.
- Route parity records exact active and LKG IDs plus list/count/filter/detail
  status/order/count/error/payload hashes for server, browser and desktop at
  every checkpoint.

Reject a side immediately for a missing or changed critical setting,
unavailable measurement, inferred/default identity, retry, silent fallback or downgrade,
partial active or candidate publication exposure, mixed component/snapshot
generation, lost work, ACK/watermark without required output, duplicate effect,
unbounded replay or cleanup, watermark regression, active/LKG/pin loss, route
hash mismatch, spill, OOM, fatal restart, residue or failed restore. Preserve
the failure; never weaken settings, silently retry, or relabel unavailable as
zero, passed or not-applicable.

## US-126 Expired Lease, Failed Publication And Application Restart Validation

### US-126 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-125 is complete at HEAD
`40952d32e3927640aaa14abce4abe2ab9233fafd`. US-126 owns exactly three
control-failure grains:

1. current and candidate expired lease, from lease deadline through heartbeat,
   stale-owner completion, takeover, retry, job/pin state and cleanup;
2. current and candidate failed publication, from output/validation through
   finalization, head change, active/LKG reads, job visibility and recovery;
   and
3. current and candidate application restart, from persisted in-flight state
   through startup role/owner/pause admission, claims, retries, jobs, cleanup,
   operator state, route parity and convergence.

Lease deadline, lease owner string, owner token/generation, heartbeat,
expiration, takeover, claim, attempt number, retry/backoff, output receipt,
completion, finalization, publication receipt, active head, persisted LKG
pointer, latest-retired fallback, route result, side-effect idempotence, job
criteria/claim/progress/result, pin/delivery settlement, cleanup eligibility,
step/cycle receipt, operator role/pause/log/diagnostic state and recovered
state remain separate contracts. Expiration, a successful claim, terminal job
status, active read, LKG read, warning response, worker restart or cleanup
invocation cannot certify another grain.

unchanged from the US-098 target-design commit

Measurements and state fields remain separate:

- Claim evidence records lease/work/job identity, owner string/token/generation,
  deadline, heartbeat, expiration, takeover CAS and accepted/rejected result.
- Retry evidence records immutable attempt number, error class, backoff,
  terminal state and request-wide total; a wake-local retry is not a durable
  attempt bound.
- Publication evidence records component output, validation, derived
  finalization, head epoch/CAS, active and persisted-LKG IDs and receipt.
- Read evidence records active, direct LKG and latest-retired fallback
  separately, plus exact list/count/filter/detail status/order/count/error/
  payload hashes for server, browser and desktop.
- Idempotence evidence records input identity, output/side-effect receipt,
  inserted/updated/deleted/conflict/no-op rows and duplicate classification.
- Job evidence records admission, criteria, claim, cursor/batch, result,
  artifact/delivery, pin/lease and terminal settlement separately.
- Cleanup evidence records eligibility/reference scan, bounded step cursor,
  retained/removed generations and complete-cycle receipt; operator evidence
  records role/owner, mutation mode, pause marker, log/diagnostic state and
  restart generation independently.
- Time records monotonic total and named phases with retained raw samples.
  Storage-engine WAL, sibling DuckDB temp baseline/peak/end/delta/events,
  process-tree RSS baseline/peak/end/delta and retained generations remain
  independent. Unit-test duration is not workload wall time.

Reject a side immediately for a missing or changed critical setting,
measurement or identity; inferred/default owner, clock, retry or runtime
profile; silent fallback/downgrade; stale-owner completion; competing accepted
claims; partial/mixed publication; active/LKG/pin loss; route mismatch; lost
work; duplicate side effect; unbounded retry/restart/cleanup; unsettled job,
delivery or operator state; spill; OOM; fatal restart; residue or failed
restore. Preserve the failure; never weaken settings, silently retry or relabel
unavailable as zero, passed or not-applicable.

## US-127 Desktop Restart And Resume Validation

### US-127 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-126 is complete at HEAD
`d9d6b7421cca9481c7b5e840e9ba43946a58d94f`. US-127 owns exactly two
desktop lifecycle grains:

1. desktop restart: stop or lose the packaged desktop/backend process at each
   finite current/candidate control, request, publication, job and pin
   checkpoint, then relaunch the complete approved desktop topology; and
2. desktop resume: retain the same desktop process across each approved
   suspend/wake, background/foreground and connectivity interruption, then
   prove request, cache, navigation, job, snapshot, pin and UI convergence.

Desktop process state, backend child state, single-instance lease, runtime
paths, database generation, storage-engine WAL, application log generation,
outer window URL/hash, client cache, route requests, semantic readiness,
active snapshot, persisted LKG pointer, latest-retired fallback, snapshot pins,
queued-job criteria/status, executor progress, detail hydration, warning/
unavailable state, recovered state and terminal cleanup remain separate
contracts. A relaunched window, HTTP 2xx, active snapshot, succeeded job
counter, retained pin, matching list count or visible review tab cannot certify
another grain.

Scoped `src`, `scripts`, `package.json` and `bun.lock` product source remains
unchanged from the US-098 target-design commit
`4ca6a3de229a949ef2662affd1d83127b708df51` through HEAD. The pre-existing
engine-owned `tasks/prd.json` modification remains untouched. Exact
product-source searches found zero files for 23 candidate/runtime markers:

### US-127 Frozen Two-Scenario Contract

| Proof ID | Finite scenario | Required checkpoints and exact pass boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PRF-1082` | Desktop restart | On the same immutable fixture, execute current then candidate in fixed order. Capture a clean whole-desktop quit/relaunch, forced whole-desktop loss and backend-child loss before readiness, after transport 2xx but before semantic readiness, during every four-tab/filter/count/detail/progress request, during queued-job admission/claim/progress/result, before/after pin acquisition, during component/derived/head publication and during cleanup; repeat to the approved cap. At every checkpoint record process tree, single-instance lease, data/log/database/temp/runtime paths, request vector, UI/hash/cache state, active/LKG/latest-retired identity, pins, jobs and unavailable/recovered state. Pass requires exactly one available desktop and bounded convergence to the signed expected state with no fatal restart, lost state, stale silent fallback, partial publication, duplicate effect, OOM, spill, unbounded recovery or residue. |
| `PRF-1083` | Desktop resume | On the same fixture and executable sides, keep the desktop process alive across each approved suspend/wake, background/foreground and offline/online interruption before, during and after every four-tab/filter/count/detail/progress request and queued-job/publication/pin phase. Capture outer/hash URL, router state, query cache age/data/error/fetch status, request cancellation/replay/deduplication/order, backend child, semantic readiness, active/LKG/fallback, jobs, pins, unavailable UI and convergence. Pass requires the exact signed request and rendered-state vector, bounded resume/recovery, no lost or duplicated work and no fatal restart, stale silent fallback, partial publication exposure, OOM, spill or residue. |

The exact route vector for both scenarios is:

| Consumer | Exact request or route | Required comparison |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop readiness | `GET /api/runtime/ready` | Transport status and semantic `data.ready` independently, including timeout and backend-child state |
| Progress/admission | `POST /api/projectsreviewswarnings` | Status/body hash, readable/indexing/unavailable state, poll order/count and mutation side effects |
| LLM tab | `GET /api/articlesreviewsfilters`; `POST /api/articlesreviews`; `POST /api/articlesreviewscount` | Snapshot/status/order/item/count/filter/error hashes and rendered rows/count |
| Human tab | `GET /api/articlesreviewshumanfilters`; `POST /api/articlesreviewshuman` | Snapshot/status/order/item/filter/error hashes and rendered rows |
| Both tab | `GET /api/articlesreviewsfilters`; `POST /api/articlesreviewsboth` | Snapshot/status/order/item/filter/error hashes and rendered rows |
| Unassessed tab | `POST /api/articlesreviewsunassessed`; current filter control disabled | Snapshot/status/order/item/error hashes and rendered rows without an invented filter request |
| Detail | `POST /api/projectsreview`; every tab title currently navigates through `/projects/$id/reviews-llm/$articleId` | Request count/body/status/payload/error/unavailable hash, cache reuse and exact URL/hash |
| Add-job progress | `GET /api/projects/add_articles_jobs?jobId&sourceProjectId` | Durable criteria/status versus local tracking handle, executor progress/result and rendered status |
| Pins and publication | Internal pin, manifest, active/LKG/fallback, job and cleanup state | Exact identities, reference counts, component/frontier state, retained generations and terminal settlement |

At each checkpoint, retain request method/path/body hash, response
status/body hash, start/end/order/retry/cancel classification and owning
snapshot identity separately. Retain process ID/generation, child exit,
single-instance lease, file paths, outer URL/hash, query-cache state,
readiness, job state/progress, active head, persisted LKG, latest-retired
fallback, pin reference/expiry and rendered unavailable/recovered state as
independent values. An HTTP-success error payload, legitimate empty result,
cached prior response, stale fallback or local terminal signal must not be
accepted as another state.

Reject a side immediately for a missing or changed critical setting,
measurement, path or identity; an inferred/default runtime; transport-ready
but semantic-unready admission; fatal restart; missing or extra child;
single-instance conflict; lost or duplicated request/work/job; stale silent
fallback; cross-snapshot route/UI mismatch; partial publication; lost/expired
pin; unbounded request, retry, restart, resume or cleanup; OOM; spill; residue
or failed restore. Preserve the failure and never weaken settings, silently
retry or relabel unavailable as zero, passed or not-applicable.

| Runtime paths and startup mutation | Desktop fixes the macOS data root under Application Support, creates data/log roots, rewrites `DUCKDB_PATH`, truncates the backend log and starts owner-mode server initialization; normal startup runs migrations and recovery mutations. | No physical desktop may run against an inferred/current root. Backend exit is only guarded before readiness; after readiness there is no child restart supervision. | A window launch or startup success cannot prove semantic availability, fatal-restart rejection or bounded backend recovery. |
| Resume, hash navigation and cache | No explicit desktop suspend/wake/resume/connectivity lifecycle exists. Desktop uses hash history, while the shared filter hook reads outer search and rewrites pathname/search without retaining hash. Lists disable focus refetch; detail caches for five minutes. | Same-process resume can expose stale cached state or lose hash navigation without a request. Exact outer/hash URL, cache state, request vector and render are required. |

Warning polling gates list readability and structured unavailable detail must not render as data. | Shared components and passing fake/test-DOM checks establish applicability only, not exact four-tab/detail/progress request or UI parity. |
| Queued jobs and progress | Add/PDF tracking handles are local signals. Pin and job creation are separate; deterministic job upsert mutates current state; worker progress is not owner-generation fenced. The desktop default memory profile omits the bulk worker. | A durable job row, local ID or succeeded counter cannot prove executor registration, resumed progress, pin settlement or later client visibility. |
| Active/LKG, pins and publication | Ordinary reads use active else latest retired; explicit LKG uses its pointer/fallback. Pins are mutable reference counts. Component/derived/head publication spans transactions. | Every route must bind one signed identity; active, persisted LKG, fallback, pin protection and absence of partial publication require separate capture. |

## US-128 Replay, Repair And Operator Recovery Validation

### US-128 Scope, Prerequisite And Execution Gate

US-127 is complete at HEAD
`2df465e44bbcc9f5ddbca1f9e33eda4bde25a099`. US-128 owns exactly three
recovery grains:

1. replay: owner-completion and judgment-SQLite-outbox work is interrupted at
   each approved handoff, then the same immutable receipt is replayed;
2. targeted repair: exactly one named judgment job is preflighted, repaired
   and observed through terminal cleanup without admitting unrelated jobs; and
3. documented operator recovery: the stopped-stack system-`sqlite3` recovery
   procedure exports one named job, applies its generated update, reconciles
   central/local state and retains or cleans its evidence under an approved
   runbook.

Completion-journal ACK, accepted-claim deletion, SQLite outbox claim,
central import marker, canonical judgment, review delta, dirty-work intake,
source/consumer/projector/visible watermarks, active snapshot, persisted LKG,
latest-retired fallback, job status, storage state, route response, recovery
sidecars, WAL checkpoint, file cleanup and retained generations remain
separate contracts. One owner ACK, duplicate counter, canonical row, empty
queue, active storage state, successful route status, advanced legacy token or
`fullyRecovered: true` cannot certify another grain.

Scoped `src`, `scripts`, `package.json` and `bun.lock` product source remains
unchanged from the US-098 target-design commit
`4ca6a3de229a949ef2662affd1d83127b708df51` through HEAD and the worktree.
The pre-existing engine-owned `tasks/prd.json` modification remains untouched.
Exact product-source searches found zero files for 17 candidate/runtime
markers: `app.review_component_revision_v5`,
`app.review_serving_snapshot_v5`, `app.review_serving_snapshot_head_v5`,
`app.review_source_event_v5`, `app.review_source_frontier_v5`,

### US-128 Frozen Three-Scenario Contract

| Proof ID | Finite scenario | Required checkpoints and exact pass boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PRF-1084` | Replay | On the same immutable fixture, execute current then candidate in fixed order. Interrupt completion and outbox handoffs before local journal/outbox insert, after local commit, before/after owner ACK, before central transaction, after central commit but before local ACK, after local ACK but before maintenance completion and before/after visibility publication. Replay exactly to the approved attempt/call/time cap. Capture accepted claim, completion, queue/outbox claim, import marker, canonical judgment, delta, dirty/output/ACK/consumer frontiers, job, active/LKG/fallback snapshot, exact route, WAL/files and cleanup. Pass requires the signed final state, one effect per immutable receipt, bounded duplicate suppression and no lost data, duplicate conflict/effect, changed setting, silent fallback, unbounded replay, OOM, spill, fatal restart or residue. |
| `PRF-1085` | Targeted repair | Name one job and execute preflight plus the approved route/CLI repair under stopped/live semantics fixed by the oracle. Interrupt before/after lease recovery, outbox flush, sent/orphan repair, claim reap, prune, drain finalization, WAL checkpoint, job-state update, visibility publication and cleanup; repeat to the cap and prove all non-target jobs/files unchanged. Pass requires exact local/central rows, files, watermarks, snapshot/head, job/storage/route state and cleanup with bounded work and no lost data, unrelated effect, duplicate effect, lease bypass, fallback, OOM, spill, fatal restart or residue. |
| `PRF-1086` | Documented operator recovery | With the approved stack stopped, invoke the signed canonical system-`sqlite3` runbook for one quarantined job and immutable source SQLite identity/revision. Interrupt generation and application before/after export, central import, update/reconcile member publication, SQLite update, WAL checkpoint, job state, visibility ACK and cleanup; perform same-revision repeat, differing-revision rejection and clean restore. Pass requires immutable checksummed/signature-validated files, exact row/file effects, canonical visibility and token closeout, bounded retained generations, idempotent repeat, mismatch rejection, rollback and zero unapproved residue with no lost data, duplicate effect, unbounded read/application, missing operator step, fallback, OOM, spill or fatal restart. |

At every checkpoint, retain the following values separately:

| Grain | Required current and candidate values |
| --- | --- |
| Admission/control | fixture/schema/data/tool/config hashes, scenario/failure-point/attempt, owner/generation/lease, unchanged-settings hash and exact command |
| Local execution | journal/job SQLite identity and hash; queue, accepted claim, execution snapshot, result/completion/outbox/import-claim rows and their statuses |
| Central effects | import marker, canonical judgment, review delta, dirty work, output/ACK receipt, maintenance run and duplicate-conflict classification |
| Watermarks/publication | allocated/persisted/reconciled/dirty-admitted/output-sealed/consumer-visible values, component revision, candidate, active, LKG, latest-retired and head epoch |
| Job and routes | admission-only status, executor progress/result, storage/quarantine state and exact health/detail/list route status/body/error/snapshot hashes |
| Files/lifecycle | every file read/written/deleted, encoded bytes/checksum, DuckDB/SQLite WAL, temp/spill, retained generations, reader lease, cleanup receipt, residue and restore outcome |

Reject a side immediately for a missing or changed setting, identity,
measurement, command, receipt or oracle; lost data; duplicate effect or
conflicting duplicate; unrelated-job mutation; advanced watermark without its
prior receipt; cross-snapshot or exact-route mismatch; mutable/unsigned
operator evidence; missing operator step; unbounded row/byte/file/call/attempt/
time/cleanup work; implicit retry; stale/silent fallback; OOM; spill; fatal
restart; residue or failed restore. Preserve the failure and never weaken a
critical setting or relabel unavailable as zero, passed or not-applicable.

### US-128 Current Source Findings

| Contract | Current checked-in behavior | Audit consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Completion replay | Journal rows use durable SQLite WAL/FULL; replay orders unacked rows, applies a failure backoff, discards explicit stale conflicts, records failures and deletes accepted claims only after ACK. Startup limit is one and normal background limit is 64/five seconds. | These are per-invocation controls. No persisted request-wide replay cursor, total cap, consumer-visible receipt or cleanup history proves bounded complete replay. |
| Outbox import and duplicate suppression | A 100-row/4 MiB claim feeds one central transaction. Natural-identity insert and `(job_id,outbox_seq)` marker suppress reapplication; crash-after-commit test retains one canonical row, one marker and five dirty rows. | Current idempotence is supported at this interruption point, but `importedCount` is importable rather than inserted count and recursive flush is unbounded request-wide. |
| Watermark and snapshot settlement | Import appends review delta and dirty work; visibility ACK is deliberately deferred to a worker. Active/LKG/head and route state are not part of the import result. | Canonical import or empty local outbox cannot certify consumer visibility, active publication, exact fallback or route parity. |
| Targeted repair | Route and CLI identify one job. Full repair can initialize SQLite, preflight/fallback, flush, requeue, reap, repair up to 1,000 orphan rows, prune until stable, finalize, checkpoint and update storage state. Automatic orphan repair has 100-batch/30-second bounds. | One-job scope is source-supported, but full flush/prune recursion, total rows/bytes/files/RSS/time, retained history and later visibility remain unbounded or unmeasured. |
| Repair route state | Structured repair/action tests pass for missing storage, orphan requeue, multiple batches, stopped-stack guidance and drain isolation. | The exact healthy-job health-route test fails twice with a non-JSON response, so an exact recovered route vector cannot be certified from the current suite. |
| Operator command surface | The runtime message documents stopped-stack `bun scripts/runJudgmentJobRepair.ts --action=repair --jobId=<job>`. Package exposes `db:judgment-job:repair`. Direct system recovery is a separate non-package script and wrapper. | There is no single approved runbook selecting the repair CLI versus direct recovery or fixing shutdown, tool identity, sidecar security, rollback, repeat and cleanup rules. |
| Direct system recovery | System `sqlite3` reads all pending/outlier rows, writes mutable JSON/SQL sidecars, imports centrally, updates the legacy ACK token, deletes local rows, checkpoints and sets current job state. Pair lookups alone are chunked by 500. | Read-all/materialization, mutable filenames, missing revision/manifest/signature/encryption/application/visibility/cleanup receipts and absent retention prevent bounded exact operator certification. |
| Candidate | `TGT-0055` keeps typed bounded job handoffs; `TGT-0056` keeps maintenance attempts; `TGT-0048`/`TGT-0050`-`TGT-0052` bind immutable publication/frontiers; `TGT-0078` defines a finite signed/encrypted recovery bundle. | The design supplies the comparison predicate but cannot be executed. Implementing it here would violate the audit-only boundary. |

## US-129 Mounted API And Read-Contract Terminal Reconciliation

### US-129 Scope, Prerequisites And Source Freeze

US-099, US-113 and US-128 are complete. US-129 started from HEAD
`f0712251537d690014b390239d3f17721e2f4492`; the only pre-existing worktree
change was the engine-owned `tasks/prd.json`, which remains untouched. The
audit-only mutation boundary remains in force: no schema, product source,
route, projector, retention, runtime behavior or data is changed; no live,
current or project DuckDB is opened; no product process or physical benchmark
is started; and no recommendation is finalized.

The authoritative API discovery union is frozen from these checked-in sources:

1. actual `ProjectsRoutes`, `ArticlesRoutes`, `ArticleAdminRoutes`,
   `HumanAssessmentRoutes`, `ProjectArticlesRoutes`, export/transfer,
   runtime-readiness and runtime-asset composition;
2. all 36 entries in `reviewServingReadContractList` and all 17 entries in
   `reviewServingReadContractRouteInventory` (16 marked mounted and one marked
   internal/unmounted);
3. all 11 `reviewServingRouteParityCoverage` rows and seven
   `reviewServingJobParityCoverage` rows;
4. all 12 `reviewServingAdjacentRouteClassifications`, the complete
   `routeSurfaceRoutes` inventory, route services and exact route tests; and
5. all 55 normalized `UIR-####` callers/query keys, including explicit
   outside-inventory references, plus the 33 prior `MAP-####` rows.

Registry labels, actual composition, a mounted HTTP route, an explicit
read-contract key, an internal reader, a UI query key and a canonical
background writer remain separate accounting grains. A route already owned by
`BGO-####` is cross-referenced rather than duplicated unless the current UI
manifest also needs a distinct HTTP input/response contract. This preserves
one API row per HTTP/read-contract grain while retaining writer/lifecycle
ownership in the background manifest.

### US-134 Scope, Prerequisite And Evidence Boundary

US-133 is complete at story-start HEAD
`d49250113d0de3ac3bd835e8f37ec60756993c85`; the only pre-existing worktree
change was the engine-owned `tasks/prd.json`, which remains untouched. Product
source is unchanged by this documentation-only story. No configured product
database, live DuckDB, browser, desktop application, migration command,
maintenance command, benchmark or physical collector ran. Focused tests used
only mocks, test-owned temporary files/databases and disposable child-process
attempts; their failures are retained as blockers rather than repaired or
reinterpreted.

The US-134 discovery union is frozen from:

1. the 66 canonical non-route lifecycle/operator rows left by US-133:
   `BGO-0006`-`BGO-0017`, `BGO-0022`-`BGO-0039`,
   `BGO-0067`-`BGO-0071`, `BGO-0073`, `BGO-0075`-`BGO-0077`,
   `BGO-0079`-`BGO-0080` and `BGO-0088`-`BGO-0112`;

   `startBackgroundWork`, ownerless-backend validation, runtime-role leasing
   and worker-registry heartbeat code;

   process locks, readiness probes, child monitoring, restart, takeover and
   shutdown behavior;

   caller/registration/retention/cleanup searches.

The union resolves six previously unallocated startup/supervision contracts as

`BGO-0067`: selecting a backend, owning a lease, publishing a worker
heartbeat, reacting to parent loss, supervising children and watching source
changes have different identities, writes, failure modes and cleanup
contracts.

`electrobun.config.ts` is unchanged from the US-054 source/configuration census
commit `c1c2b406218d15ebabe9cee7ede91722c28d4fe3` through story-start HEAD.

The US-135 discovery union is therefore frozen from:

1. all 127 DuckDB migration SQL files in the lexical filename order implemented
   by `migrateDuckdb.ts#getDuckdbMigrationFiles`, including every rebuild,
   add-column, constraint, index creation and index drop affecting this family;
2. canonical source/configuration rows `DBO-0001`-`DBO-0031`,
   `DBO-0179`-`DBO-0181`, `DBO-0211` and `DBO-0220`-`DBO-0223`, restricted
   to the 39-row allocation below;

   `DSP-0029`, family proofs `PRF-0017`-`PRF-0076` and target proofs
   `PRF-0077`-`PRF-0083`; and

   US-067, US-073 and US-081 reconciliations.

This closes exactly 39 rows: 17 physical tables, six logical objects and 16
named indexes. Primary keys, foreign keys, unique constraints and checks are
attributes of their owning table rows, not additional index dispositions.
Logical objects cross-reference backing fields without claiming a second
physical disposition. Named indexes are supporting accounting grains linked
to the owning table disposition; they are not independent keep/delete
recommendations.

No configured product database, live/current/project DuckDB, product server,
worker, projector, migration command, benchmark or physical collector ran.
The focused migration and service tests use test-owned disposable databases,
mocks and temporary data only. Missing deployed shape, plan, selectivity,
row/byte/write/rebuild, retention and restore observations remain unavailable,
never zero.

### US-137 Duplicate And Contradiction Resolutions

| Grain | Apparent duplicate or contradiction | Terminal resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Object versus logical-field count | US-069 assigned 74 non-overlapping identity/snapshot column rows while the five current tables declare 76 columns. | The two projection-input backing columns are already assigned to logical `DBO-0112`. Record 448 actual declarations across 26 tables, retain the prior disjoint CMF allocation, and do not claim extra logical columns. |
| Selected-import table name | `FAN-0036` named nonexistent `app.review_selected_import_snapshot_v4`. | Correct the measured object to current `app.review_selected_import_snapshot`; no DBO row is added or removed. |
| Execution named indexes versus constraints | `DBO-0047` exactly repeats the unique claim tuple; `DBO-0048` begins with PK `id`. | Keep constraint backing as a table attribute and each named index as one supporting row. Physical use/redundancy/cost remains blocked. |
| Imported-marker index versus readers | The index name and prior description implied status/time import, cleanup and diagnostics use. | Current reads use compound PK identity, job prefix/sequence maximum or project/job cleanup. Record no current literal status/time reader without inferring deletion. |
| Historical job-control indexes | Bootstrap migrations declare health-freshness and provider-expiry indexes. | 0056/0057 drop health freshness; 0070 drops provider expiry with the table rebuild. Do not count either among the 29 current named indexes. |
| Maintenance/provider branch indexes | Project/article/provider prefixes overlap selected branches while recovery/closeout queries also have global or alternate-scope branches. | Map each compatible branch only; do not claim the named index serves the combined/global path without a physical plan. |
| Dirty-work lookup versus global claim | `DBO-0113` shares project/high-water vocabulary with dirty processing. | Current global claim is status/projection/partition/update/high-water/ID-led; diagnostics use only project before grouping. Remove the claim-use implication. |
| Selected-header/base indexes versus publication | `DBO-0123` was described as active-header adjacency and `DBO-0124` as selected ordering. | Header status reads use PK snapshot ID; base article reads use the PK, and no current literal selected-rank-key order exists. Preserve both named indexes as blocked supporting rows. |
| Rebuild and bulk status indexes versus claims | Project-leading `DBO-0135` and `DBO-0138` resemble their respective worker status predicates. | Both operating claims can be global and use additional admission/retry/lease/stale/order fields. Project-prefix compatibility does not certify global claim use. |
| Mutable state versus audit state | Rows persist statuses such as ready, active, completed, failed, released or expired. | Product state never changes `auditStatus`, `proofCheckState`, disposition actionability or certification. All 58 story rows remain audit-blocked. |
| Late-object search | Complete migrations and current/dynamic source could expose an unassigned manifest/control/job DuckDB object. | No late table, logical subshape or current named index exists. Any future late row lacking lifecycle, measurement and validation must enter as `blocked`. |

blocked`. Both subtotals have zero nonterminal rows. Global accounting remains
`322 = 0 classified + 0 out-of-scope + 322 blocked`; its named-index subset
remains `127 = 0 classified + 0 out-of-scope + 127 blocked`.

question. Physical values remain unavailable. Existing keep/delete-candidate

Exact physical patch literals are migration/test-only in current source; this proves a checked-in bypass, not deployed absence or deletion safety. |
| Clean declarations versus forward adds | 0097 already declares later candidate/display/payload/selected fields; 0098, 0104, 0105 and 0108 repeat additions or backfill legacy state. | Count each clean-forward column once. Retain upgraded-shape/backfill completion and possible historical extra-column state as blockers rather than inventing duplicate current columns. |
| Current versus historical rebuild shape | 0099 rebuilds detail, 0103 destructively rebuilds active queue, and 0109 rebuilds/copies detail and recreates its index. | Use final 0103 queue key/index and final 0109 detail key/index. Earlier declarations are lifecycle evidence, not additional current objects. |
| Named index versus PK backing | Title-token, queue-patch and final active-queue named indexes repeat their PK expression; other named indexes overlap PK prefixes. | Keep PK/unique backing as table attributes and all 12 explicit named indexes as separate DBO rows. Redundancy/use requires deployed physical measurement. |
| Candidate projection versus selection | Generic SQL projects all 44 candidate columns and joins metadata before its outer limit. | Only scope/filter/search/queue/cursor/order fields establish candidate membership. Projection position, later hydration and physical optimizer materialization remain separate. |
| Registered versus invoked title search | Route inventory and read-contract metadata map token-prefix search to more consumers than exact current callers demonstrate. | Preserve actual mounted list/count and bulk embedded predicates, the callable unmounted standalone service, and generic posting/queue construction as separate evidence grains. |
| Queue order versus article existence | One index contains priority, activity, article, prompt and identity while route, Human-init and job readers use different subsets. | Record registered priority order, prompt-pair job order, article-existence, distinct-article count and grouped preview separately; one compatible branch does not certify every consumer. |
| Product state versus audit state | Candidate/patch rows carry generations, watermarks, tombstones, statuses, counts and timestamps. | Product state never advances `auditStatus`, `proofCheckState`, disposition actionability or certification. All 22 story rows remain audit-blocked. |
| Late-object search | Complete migrations and current source could expose an unassigned durable family table/index. | No late durable table or current named index exists. Any future late row without route/runtime, lifecycle, measurement and validation evidence must enter as `blocked`. |

US-140 is complete at story-start HEAD

source under `src`, `scripts`, `package.json`, `bun.lock` and
`electrobun.config.ts` is unchanged from the object-census baseline
`c1c2b406218d15ebabe9cee7ede91722c28d4fe3` through story-start HEAD.

The discovery union starts with all 36 inherited payload/file DBO rows:
`DBO-0060`, `DBO-0061`, `DBO-0092`, `DBO-0093` and `DBO-0291`-
`DBO-0322`. It then replays all non-test production file reads, writes,
copies, moves, removals, directory walks, path resolvers, response/download
builders, package members, lock/lease/log writers, repair/operator scripts and
browser/desktop runtime-asset consumers. Every inherited row retains one
canonical object assignment and its existing material, measurement,
disposition and proof cross-references.

That union exposes four in-scope shapes omitted by the 36-row census:

   `app.article.full_text_assets` or local HTML `src`/`href` values;

material rows `CMF-1986`-`CMF-1989`. The story therefore closes 40 DBO rows.
The four late paths are not aliases of the generic assets gateway, FHIR spool,
promoted transfer assets, recovery-script sidecars, DuckDB owner lease or
browser/client downloads because their producers, contents, consumers and
lifecycle contracts differ.

No configured product database, live/current/project DuckDB, server, worker,
projector, migration, import, export, transfer, repair, cleanup, browser,
desktop app, benchmark, filesystem collector or physical fixture ran. Focused
tests used source assertions, mocks and test-owned disposable databases/files.
No application file inventory, byte size, checksum, duplicate/reference scan,
age, permission, active-reader lease, crash residue, deployed runtime access,
retention receipt or restore result was observed; every such value remains
unavailable rather than zero.
